items.title: PARAM-ADMISSIBLE: is the chart-index binder hdeg satisfiable, and at which n?
items.summary:
*** MEASURED AND LANDED 2026-07-30 (run 0088 r6, ajcr-p2). THE BINDER IS EXACTLY AN ARITHMETIC FACT, AND THE THETA-EXPONENT IS IDLE. Read this before pricing any chart-parameter question. ***

THE MEASUREMENT. 23 chart files bind hdeg (deg_k Z = m*d1 - n) and ZERO produced one; the two theorems that conclude an exists over (m, Z) take the same constraint as a hypothesis and say so. Picard/Pic0ChartIndexAdmissible.lean now proves, both directions:

  chartIndex_iff_isDegree :  (exists m Z, deg_k Z = m*d1 - c)  <->  IsDivisorDegree C c

i.e. the binder carries EXACTLY 'c is in the image of deg_k' and nothing else -- no chart, no certificate, no representation. Two consequences, both correcting live pricings:
 * THE THETA-EXPONENT m IS IDLE. The producer direction takes m = 0, Z = -W. So hdeg imposes NO coupling of m to n; any such coupling comes from the chart PARAMETER (ledger_forces_b_eq_n), not from this hypothesis.
 * ADMISSIBILITY IS SHIFT-INVARIANT AND SUBGROUP-CLOSED (isDegree_add_mul_iff, isDegree_sub, isDegree_zero, isDegree_mul_thetaDeg). So admissibility at n and at n + a*d1 are the SAME statement -- the parameter-matching consequence (I-1345). Multiples of d1 are admissible unconditionally.

IT REACHES THE CONSUMER. Picard/Pic0ChartIndexLedgerFeed.lean: mem_chartLocus_of_ledgerIndex_of_isDegree replaces exists_chartIndex_mem_chartLocus_of_ledgerIndex's unexhibited (m, Z) with IsDivisorDegree C (M*delta + g) -- discharging the clause that theorem's own docstring calls 'a divisor-side existence statement this file does not prove and does not claim'.

WHAT IS NOT DONE, and it is the whole remaining price. IsDivisorDegree C (M*delta + g) IS NOT KNOWN TO HOLD, and I do not claim it. Over an arbitrary base field deg_k is residue-degree weighted, so its image is a proper subgroup index*Z in general; PROBED that the tree cannot prove deg_k surjective (exact? fails on IsDivisorDegree C c for a variable c) and that the tree's only residue-degree-one point needs [IsSepClosed k] (Over.dense_baseChange_rationalPoints, Curve/SepPointsDense.lean:278), which the arbitrary-field statement forbids. NO ANTECEDENT OF pic0RepresentableByOfCharts MOVES: IsChartUniv, the pointwise-to-neighbourhood spreading-out, and rep at every parameter are untouched.

TWO PROBES I RAN AND THE ANSWERS, so nobody repeats them:
 * is windowdelta pi = classDeg k (thetaCechClass C)? NOT PROVABLE BY exact? -- different carriers (C.left over k vs the base-changed product curve). If it WERE, M*delta would be a multiple of d1 and shift-invariance would reduce the ledger target to g alone. That transport is the cheapest known route to inhabiting the residue and NOBODY HAS BUILT IT.
 * read against I-1389: the (m, Z) this route produces is UNIFORM in the point (hadm does not mention t), but this is NOT one-chart coverage -- L, M0, hM0 stay per-point. The non-uniformity is in the SPLITTING DATA, not the chart parameter.

NEXT, in cost order: (1) the windowdelta-vs-d1 transport above; (2) state 'the image of deg_k is index*Z' as a theorem -- three files assert it in prose (JacobianDataAbelDegreeWindow.lean:23, :200, JacobianDataAbelEffective.lean:128) and none states it, and isDegree_sub is the subgroup half already.

VERIFICATION: both modules rooted in AlgebraicJacobian.lean and built IN GRAPH, lake build EXIT=0 (8900 jobs); all 10 declarations axiom-clean [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] against a control where Jacobian correctly reports sorryAx; the consumer-feed probe discriminates (fails at +1). Zero sorries in both files.

Replacing pi by twistedP1Map pi M changes the represented chart; one fixed classifier cannot classify the union over M without changing its target and inverse laws. The requested in-place restatement is type-theoretically wrong. DivRepGlobalData.equiv represents DivFamZar for one fixed map pi, and its theta windows, cocycle, evaluation maps, and DivScheme all depend on that same pi. A witness M changes pi to twistedP1Map pi M, hence changes the fixed representing chart. No single existing DivRepGlobalData.equiv can classify the union over M.

The correct architecture is an OUTER twist-indexed atlas: retain each fixed-(twistedP1Map pi M) DivFamZar and its existing classifier as one chart, then glue/quotient those charts on divisor-equality overlaps. The quantifier over M belongs inside the base-local atlas cover, but outside each fixed classifier. set-theoretically Theta = V_1^c and "supportLocus cap pi^-1(infinity) = empty" IS the disjunct
supportLocus subset V_1. And IsGenerator.dvd makes supportLocus the base locus of K, so "a
generator of exact pole order a exists at y in Theta" holds iff the base locus misses y:
premise = conclusion.

(c) EXPLICIT COUNTEREXAMPLE, STABLE UNDER EVERY ZARISKI SHRINK. Over k[t] with C = P^1, pi = id,
F = t X^2 + X Y + t Y^2 cuts a relative effective Cartier divisor, finite flat of degree 2
(coefficients (t,1,t) generate the unit ideal). F(1,0) = F(0,1) = t, so the fibre at t = 0 is
Z(XY) = {0, infinity}: it meets BOTH vertical fibres. In the chart Y = 1, F = t(x^2+1) + x is
degree 1 in t with coprime coefficients, hence irreducible in k[x,t]; the only point over Y = 0
is (infinity, 0), in the closure. So D is IRREDUCIBLE, D -> A^1_t is finite surjective, and over
EVERY nonempty open of the base D stays irreducible hence preconnected. Every Zariski cover has
a member containing t = 0. By supportLocus_subset_chart_of_isCertified this divisor is NOT
IsLocallyCertified.

does NOT meet pi^-1(infinity) (its points x = +-sqrt t are always finite), so it is chart-confined
and is not a witness. The conclusion stands; the witness above is the correct one.

(d) THE OBSTRUCTION SURVIVES THE DivEq QUOTIENT (landed this round, kernel-checked,
Picard/DivSchemeCertZarConfine.lean): DivEq.supportLocus_eq — the support locus is a divisor
invariant — hence not_isCertified_of_divEq_of_isPreconnected_of_witnesses: NO representative of
the class admits a certified adaptation. DivFamZar is a DivEq quotient, so DivFamZar is not the
relative-divisor functor and divRep against it would represent the wrong object.

h_0 : Fin m_0 -> Gamma(V_0), h_1 : Fin m_1 -> Gamma(V_1) with a partition of unity on EACH pinned
chart. Not pi, not the cover's fineness, not the submodule L, not the base. Any repair must
introduce an adaptation piece NOT contained in a single pinned chart. Successor leaves: p1-aut,
fibre-avoid, cert-relocalize, confine-open.

traces is fixed), so leak-image route (b) is dead; and the tube/idempotent machinery cannot
manufacture it, so leak-image route (a) is exactly chart-avoid. The lane is therefore a chart-design
problem, not a fibre-analysis problem.

 * subset_or_disjoint_of_isPreconnected_of_supportLeak : leak-freeness makes the piece trace CLOSED
   and the piece is OPEN, so the trace is clopen in the support; a preconnected support forces it
   empty or total. Swallow-or-miss is therefore not an extra hypothesis for a connected divisor —
   it is what leak-freeness already says.
 * supportLocus_subset_chart_of_isPreconnected : IsPreconnected supportLocus plus leak-freeness at
   every piece implies supportLocus subset V_0 OR supportLocus subset V_1. No nonemptiness needed.
 * not_forall_supportLeak_eq_empty_of_isPreconnected : contrapositive — a connected divisor confined

items.title: The R1 field-size bound: sharp iff |P^1(k)| >= g+2 (ANSWERED, theorem not decision)
items.summary:
ANSWERED 2026-07-26 (run 0048 round 4). Not blocked any more, and not a human decision after all —
the bound is a theorem, sharp in both directions. Deliverable: informal/spec-dd-r.md ADDENDUM 4
§4.4 (commit d7e8348ce). Inbox I-0346's standing question is discharged.

THE ANSWER.  R1 -- varying the pinned pair of P^1-points per cover member, i.e. the p1-aut ->
fibre-avoid -> cert-relocalize chain -- is correct IF AND ONLY IF |P^1(k)| >= n + 2, where n is
the degree, pinned to the genus g by the functor.

Both directions come from one fibrewise reduction (ADDENDUM 4 §4.2).  For c in P^1(k) let W_c be
the image in Spec R of supp D meeting pi^{-1}(c); it is closed because supp D is finite over R,
and s in W_c iff the FIBRE supp(D_s) meets pi^{-1}(c).  Since D_s is finite of degree n over
kappa(s), its image in |P^1| has at most n closed points.
  IF: pick c in P^1(k) outside that image and any c' /= c; then Spec R minus W_c confines D to the
  chart complementary to pi^{-1}(c).  Doing this at every s gives a Zariski cover on which the
  divisor is confined, with the pair varying per member -- exactly what R1 allows.
  ONLY IF: if the sum over c in P^1(k) of e_c is at most n, where e_c is the minimal degree of a
  closed point of C over c, then a divisor of the form sum_c q_c + padding lies in W_c for EVERY
  c in P^1(k), and no pinned pair confines it.

CONSEQUENCES, and they decide the certificate route.
 * p1-aut is NOT dead.  It is correct over every infinite field, and over F_q whenever q >= g+1.
 * It cannot discharge the challenge on its own.  Challenge.lean:96-99 states the Jacobian over an
   ARBITRARY field and archon-protected.yaml forbids adding a hypothesis, so R1 must be paired
   with descent (dat-g) or replaced.
 * Of the three options this leaf was opened to choose between, (a) "accept |P^1(k)| >= n+2 as a
   hypothesis" is now known to be exactly the right hypothesis and exactly what the challenge
   forbids; (b) descent from a big enough k' is viable and is the pairing R1 needs; (c) degree-d
   closed points is unnecessary -- it is subsumed by R2, which is cleaner.
 * R2 is the only field-uniform fix and is no longer a gamble: supp D is finite over R, hence
   contained in a single affine open of C x_k Spec R (avoidance for families, Stacks 0B8B), so a
   cover with one straddling piece always exists.  Generalising FinCoverData's piece type to
   arbitrary affine opens of the relative curve is the statement the geometry already supports.

Related and settled the same round: the on-stratum witness the no-go lacked now exists at g >= 2
over any field (ADDENDUM 4 §4.3), so the no-go is not vacuous on the campaign's stratum; and
ADDENDUM 3's shrink-stability argument was the wrong criterion (a span-top cover cannot delete a
point) -- under the criterion it stated, the campaign's own genus-0 example would be evaded.

items.title: Relax FinCoverData's chart-wise partitions to a joint covering (I-0346's cheaper option)
items.summary:
REJECTED 2026-07-26 (run 0048 round 2), on a source fact, before any Lean was written.

I-0346 recorded a cheaper untried repair than R1/PGL_2: "relaxing just the chart-wise
partitions of unity in FinCoverData to a JOINT covering drops the requirement from two
avoided points to ONE.  Worth trying before anyone builds PGL_2."

IT BUYS NOTHING, and the reason is a typing fact, not a proof attempt.  FinCoverData
(Picard/DivisorFamily.lean:160-176) types its pieces INTO the charts:
  h0 : Fin m0 -> Gamma(relCurve, V0)      (:166)
  h1 : Fin m1 -> Gamma(relCurve, V1)      (:168)
  pieces := Sum.elim (basicOpen . h0) (basicOpen . h1)   (:186)
so every piece is a basic open OF ONE OF THE TWO PINNED CHARTS by construction, whatever
the partition data says.  Per-piece swallow-or-miss already holds for ANY cover by opens
(DivSchemeCertZarConn.lean:98 uses only openness of pieces), so a connected divisor still
lands in one piece, and basicOpen_le puts that piece inside one chart.  The joint-covering
relaxation changes the partition FIELDS; it cannot change where the pieces live.

SHARP FORM, which is what should be quoted from now on: no repair that keeps the pieces
inside the preimages of a FIXED PAIR of points of P^1 can work.  Any real repair must
either vary the pinned pair (leaf p1-aut, the R1 route) or generalize FinCoverData's piece
TYPE away from the two charts (the recorded R2 alternative).

The earlier sweep (I-0943) found no HasDivFunctor-style vacuity on this seam but stated honestly

widening holds the newest Prop-valued definitions, so it is where such a defect would survive

Full reasoning: I-0346. Spec: informal/spec-dd-r.md ADDENDUM 5-11.

=== THE REJECTION CLUSTER, ADJUDICATED 2026-07-29 (run 0082, review-ajcr). READ THIS FIRST. ===

Four rejections and one block under this parent looked like a formulation error. It is not. The four
rejections are each CORRECT, three of them are ONE fact, and the defect is in this parent's
FORWARDING, not in its formulation.

THE FOUR REJECTIONS ARE SOUND, checked at declaration level, not taken on their notes' word:
 * joint-cover  — a TYPING fact: FinCoverData types its pieces INTO the two pinned charts
   (DivisorFamily.lean:160-176, h0/h1 land in Gamma(relCurve, V0/V1)), so relaxing the partition
   FIELDS cannot move where pieces live. Correct, and no Lean was needed to see it.
 * tube-fibre   — SUPERSEDED: its reformulation is equivalent to closedness of the two chart traces
   (isClosed_supportLocus_inter_chart_of_forall_noLeak), which is chart-avoid's business.
 * leak-image   — route (a) is chart-avoid, route (b) is dead (a finer cover imposes MORE

comments.body:
STATUS active -> blocked, 2026-07-26 (run 0048 round 4). Not a demotion of the lane's importance: an honest label. Nothing in this subtree can be costed, let alone worked, until one question is answered, and it is a question about mathematics rather than about Lean.

THE QUESTION. The chart-confinement no-go is proved structurally and degree-agnostically, but the only witness ever exhibited (F = tX^2 + XY + tY^2 over k[t], C = P^1, pi = id) has degree 2 on a curve of GENUS 0, while the functor pins the degree to the genus (hchi, DivRepAffKit.lean:62; IsCertified clause (c2), DivisorFamily.lean:426-437). On the campaign's own stratum: at g = 0 the no-go is vacuous (degree-0 relative divisors have empty support); at g = 1 base shrink DOES evade it (a section's support locus is Spec R, so removing one base point confines it, and the gate is pointwise on the base after I-0320); at g >= 2 NO WITNESS HAS EVER BEEN EXHIBITED. See I-0356.

WHY THE ANSWER DECIDES THE WHOLE SUBTREE.
 * If a g >= 2 witness exists, the certificate route as designed is dead over an arbitrary field, and exactly one of R1 (p1-aut -> fibre-avoid -> cert-relocalize), R2 (generalise FinCoverData's piece type) or descent from a large field (dat-g) must be chosen — and R1 alone provably cannot suffice, because the pointwise gate then needs two kappa(p)-rational points of P^1 off the fibre's support image at every prime, which fails over small finite residue fields. That is I-0346's field-size question, and it is THIS obstruction seen pointwise, not a separate one. So R1 would have to be R1-plus-descent.
 * If no witness exists — i.e. on-stratum seed divisors are always confinable after a base shrink — the certificate route REOPENS and p1-aut, fibre-avoid, cert-relocalize and field-size can all be deleted.
Costing p1-aut or R2 before that answer is spending a session on a coin flip.

ALSO SETTLED THIS ROUND, so that nobody re-derives it: re-basing U2 on the Zariski-local certificate does not evade the no-go. The epsilon-identity's consumption of IsCertified really is only three Zariski-local projections (divisorWindow_eq_of_le, DivSchemeEps.lean:170), and it can be re-proved from IsLocallyCertified by a squeeze over Localization.Away with no ThetaGlued base change. But the no-go is about PRODUCING a certificate for a chart-crossing connected divisor, and IsLocallyCertified fails for exactly the divisors IsCertified fails for — DivSchemeCertZarC1.lean:30-31 states this verbatim.

Milestone w4-gate now tags this subtree; the independent work is milestone w4-tail.

items.title: DEG-ZERO: an unconditional rep producer at parameter 0 (unitEquations + the zero certificate), the first inhabitant of the mixedParamChart rep slot
items.summary:
DEG-ZERO. ADVANCED SUBSTANTIALLY, NO SEAM ANTECEDENT CLOSED. Released (pic-c, run 0092).

WHAT LANDED, all sorry-free, lake build EXIT=0 (8782 jobs), both modules rooted:
 Picard/DivisorFamilyDegreeZero.lean -- THE DEGREE-ZERO CERTIFICATE IS FREE. On the trivial system (cover top, eqn 1) every colength module is Gamma/(1) = 0; a zero module is free hence finite/projective/flat, and rankAtStalk of a subsingleton is 0, which IS the n = 0 clause. All seven fields of IsCertified 0 close with NO hypothesis beyond what relCurve needs to exist. Gives CertifiedDivisorFamily C R pi 0 and trivZar : DivFamZar C R pi 0 for EVERY test ring R, axiom-clean [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. Plus mapAlg_trivZar / mapAlgHom_trivZar: the trivial class is BASE-CHANGE INVARIANT.
 Picard/DivisorFamilyDegreeZeroUnique.lean -- AND OVER A FIELD THE VALUE IS A SINGLETON. A degree-n family cuts a divisor of degree exactly n; the divisor a local-equation system cuts is always EFFECTIVE (no certificate needed); at n = 0 an effective degree-0 divisor is ZERO. So all degree-0 families cut the same divisor, DivEq follows over a field, and DivFam.exists_toZar_eq carries the subsingleton to the FUNCTOR CARRIER DivFamZar. DivFamZar.uniqueZeroOfField : Unique.

WHY 0 IS NOT AN ARBITRARY SMALL PARAMETER, and this is the file's own stated boundary: rankAtStalk_glued is the ONE field of the seven that fails at n > 0 for this adaptation. 0 is the unique degree at which the rank clause is vacuous. Symmetrically, effectivity + the degree identity pin nothing at n > 0, so the uniqueness argument is also specific to 0 and is not a general theorem in disguise.

WHAT IS OPEN, stated plainly. This is NOT yet (divFunctor C pi 0).RepresentableBy. Two gaps, in order:
 (1) THE GENERAL-TEST SECTION. divFamZar C pi 0 T for arbitrary T needs the constant-trivial family to satisfy the vehicle's compatibility clause; mapAlgHom_trivZar is the right transport law but Over.resAlgHom T h = algebraMap is NOT rfl on the restriction -- it needs tower instances nobody has built. I attempted this and it is recorded as attempted, not as done.
 (2) GENERAL-R UNIQUENESS. The subsingleton needs Field K TWICE: for divEq_of_presentationDivisor_eq (a non-reduced base has divisor-inequivalent systems with equal presentation divisors) and for exists_toZar_eq. Whether DivFamZar C R pi 0 is a subsingleton at general R is UNMEASURED. Inhabitation transfers to every R; uniqueness does not.

AND THE SEAM-LEVEL CAVEAT a consumer must read: even a full rep at nn i = 0 does not feed mixedParamChart alone -- it still needs a legal chart index Z i of degree m*d1 - 0 and BOTH seam antecedents at that index. This row buys the rep slot's object side at one parameter, nothing above it.

items.title: F6 to F7: the affine-to-general lift (DivRepGlobalData.ofAffine)
items.summary:
DDR-9's F6 -> F7 AFFINE-TO-GENERAL LIFT. Opened 2026-07-26 (run 0048 round 4) after a direct
source check found the gap; it had never been named as a work item.

THE GAP. `DivRepGlobalData` (Picard/DivRepKit.lean:69) occurs in NO other file in the tree --
zero producers, zero consumers. Its own docstring (:16-20) says so deliberately: "DDR-9.F7 has
two logically separate parts: lifting the affine equivalences to arbitrary tests, and packaging
the resulting natural equivalences as a RepresentableBy datum. This file formalizes the second
part. ... The affine-to-general lift is intentionally not assumed to exist implicitly: a caller
must provide every field." The second part IS landed --
`DivRepGlobalData.representableBy` (:114) yields `(divFunctor C pi g).RepresentableBy DivOver`,
the campaign's divisor-representability endpoint. The FIRST part was never written.

WHY THIS LEAF EXISTS. Every previous plan treated F6 -> F7 as bookkeeping folded into "divrep",
so it was invisible: it appears in no roadmap row and no worksheet task list. It is not
bookkeeping. It is the sheaf-theoretic descent of an equivalence from affine tests to arbitrary
tests in Over (Spec k), and it needs a gluing argument on both sides -- sections one way,
morphisms of schemes the other.

WHY IT IS TRACTABLE, AND WHY IT IS THE BEST U2-FREE WORK AVAILABLE. Its main input is already
proved: Picard/DivisorFamilyZarSheaf.lean shows `divFamZar` is a Zariski sheaf on ARBITRARY tests
-- separation `ext_of_le_cover` (:66) and gluing `existsUnique_glue_of_le_cover` (:237), with the
`LocalData` / `IsGlueValue` / `glueValue` / `glueSection` apparatus (:92-:226). The target
statement is

  DivRepGlobalData.ofAffine (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2) :
    DivRepGlobalData hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2

which is complete mathematics over a section variable, independent of the blocked certificate
mountain and of U2. Landing it means the divisor-representability endpoint is separated from the
open problem by exactly the affine package, and nothing else.

STAGING: (1) the `pull` field by gluing the affine pulls, with its characterizing property and
uniqueness from ext_of_le_cover; (2) `pull_comp` from the affine `pull_naturality`; (3) the
`classify` field by gluing the affine classifiers as morphisms of schemes (mathlib
Scheme.OpenCover.glueMorphisms); (4) the two inverse laws and `ofAffine`.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY LEFT of this leaf, i.e. staging (3) and (4): the general-test classifier and the two inverse laws. The route, and it needs no certificate and no U2:
 * classify: on each affine open W of T.left the landed affine backward classifier

items.title: atlas hcpt: the CompactSpace input of jacobianDataOfMixedParamCharts -- the one atlas obligation with no lane
items.summary:
ADVANCED, NOT CLOSED (ajcr-p3, run 0089 r7). hcpt costs Finite iota ALONE -- and nothing about coverage. Picard/Pic0AtlasCompactNoetherian.lean, rooted, 7 decls, 0 sorries, all axiom-clean [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] vs two sorryAx controls.

WHAT WAS WRONG WITH THE PRICE. Three sites split hcpt into a free per-chart half and an index-finiteness obstruction, and exhibited CompactSpace (divSchemeOver ...).left as the free half. WRONG OBJECT: mixedParamChart is restrictChart ... (V i), whose source is yoneda.obj ((V i : Scheme)), an OPEN of the representing object. Compactness does not pass to open subspaces -- infer_instance FAILS on CompactSpace (V : Scheme). Corrected at all three sites; detail I-1391.

WHAT IS NOW FREE. compactSpace_isOpen_divSchemeOver: local noetherianity (lft over Spec k) makes an open's inclusion quasi-compact, so every open is compact. compactSpace_of_representableBy: this belongs to the FUNCTOR, transporting between any two representations -- the companion of the landed locallyOfFiniteType_of_representableBy. compactSpace_glued_of_finite_mixedParamChart then gives hcpt at a finite atlas with NO hcl and NO Abel morphism, and its IsLocallySurjective binder is IDLE (statement compiles without it; glueData does not depend on coverage). So the compactness half is coverage-FREE (I-1430).

CONSEQUENCE FOR dat-j.qcfield: quasiCompact_jacobianDataOfFiniteMixedParamCharts discharges that row's field at a finite atlas, so hcl is what pays it at an INFINITE one. Sent to ajcr-p1 who holds that row.

WHAT REMAINS, and it is the whole residue: Finite iota is UNDISCHARGED and load-bearing (control: dropping it breaks elaboration). It is NOT met by shrinking the index -- single-index coverage implies unrestricted one-chart coverage via pointwise_of_pointwise_restrictChart, which three files expect to fail (I-1389), though none proves it. No antecedent of the seam moves; rep, IsChartUniv and Zariski-local surjectivity untouched.

DO NOT INHERIT: 'hf is FALSE at V = top' (Pic0ChartPair.lean:134) is a docstring assertion, NOT a theorem -- no negated-open-immersion declaration exists in this project. Four of my own claims were refuted by a fresh-context audit and repaired in-tree; see the file header.

   toJacobianDataOfAbelLifts (:137) is the same with quasi-compactness in the shape the classical

   Pic0PreservesFilteredBaseColimit (Picard/PicRepColimitCompat.lean);
 * 'defer until divRep/C9/B6' is right -- it consumes them.

ADDITION 1, the shape of the remaining debt, which is now visible in ONE signature and is worth
quoting to whoever picks this up: toJacobianDataOfAbelLifts's two hypotheses ARE the two remaining
DAT-J inputs -- a PicRepDatum k k C, and a per-point residue-field lift of an Abel morphism out of
DivScheme g. Quasi-compactness comes from the Abel IMAGE, never from the construction, because
JacobianData's atlas is infinite (critical-path 7.5). So this row does not owe a finiteness argument.

why JacobianData.ofChartsOfCompactSpace (Picard/JacobianDataCharts.lean:209) exists alongside

CompactSpace of the glued object directly. A lane assembling the atlas must know which of the two it
is heading for BEFORE choosing the index type, because the finite route is not available for the
class-indexed atlas.

NO HYPOTHESIS GAP AT THE FROZEN SIGNATURE, checked because it would have been a real defect:
Pic0SigmaSheaf introduces [GeometricallyReduced C.hom] while Challenge.lean's frozen Jacobian carries
only IsProper / SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 / GeometricallyIrreducible. Geometric reducedness is
DERIVED from smoothness of relative dimension one by global instances in the import closure, and
JacobianDataCharts.lean records it with an explicit inferInstance example after its Charts section. So
every declaration on this route elaborates under the frozen bundle alone.

items.summary:
*** THIS ROW IS NOW THE EXPOSED ANTECEDENT (review-ajcr, run 0082 s0006). Not because anything
here changed -- because the item next to it was discharged and this one was behind it. ***

ajcr-p4 discharged the chart-finiteness (hlft) antecedent at the real atlas (Pic0AtlasFiniteType.lean;
audited by me, it is a real discharge and not a relocation -- see AJCR.w4-rep's arithmetic
correction). JacobianData has FOUR fields, and with hlft gone the finiteness side of the datum is
down to ONE open input, which is this row's: quasiCompact.

THE DISTINCTION THAT MUST NOT BE BLURRED, and it is why the freeness next door does not help here:
 * PER-CHART compactness is FREE at the carrier the divisor-representability lane returns
   (compactSpace_divScheme, DivSchemeQProj.lean) -- DivScheme is a closed subscheme of the compact
   Grassmannian pair.
 * CompactSpace of the GLUED object is NOT, and it is what JacobianData needs. For the
   class-indexed atlas the index type is infinite, so the finite route JacobianData.ofCharts
   ([Finite iota] + per-chart compactness) IS UNAVAILABLE, and ofChartsOfCompactSpace takes the
   glued compactness directly.
Anyone quoting "compactness is free at the carrier" for the glued form is making exactly the
conflation this note exists to prevent. ajcr-p4 stated the distinction correctly in their own file;
keep it.

SO THE ROUTE IS THIS ROW'S ROUTE, unchanged and now unavoidable: quasi-compactness comes from the
ABEL IMAGE (JacobianData.ofChartsOfAbelImage), never from the construction. The row's own analysis
below is intact and its correction-at-the-top is honest about what "discharged" was wrong about.

WHY THE all-children-done WARNING STAYS: recorded in I-0971 and unchanged -- degwindow being done
does not close this row, which owes the image argument. Do not let a janitor set it done.

DAT-J: JacobianData assembly -- quasi-compactness via the Abel image of Div^g-lite.

*** CORRECTION AT THE TOP, 2026-07-29 (run 0071 s0016 close, ajcr-divrep), against MY OWN header
below. A fresh-context audit (I-0799/I-0800/I-0802/I-0803) refuted three of its claims. Commit
9753ad6e3; the Lean is unchanged and still kernel-green, the PRICING was wrong.

WHAT SURVIVES: the effectivity half is genuinely divRep-FREE (the audit cone-checked 323 files:
no divRepClassify, no DivRepAffinePullback, no IsChartClause, no universal family), and the three
theorems are real, sorry-free, rooted and axiom-clean.

WHAT IS REFUTED -- and it is the word "discharged":
 (1) I called exists_effective_deg_eq_of_classDeg_eq_zero a SATISFIABILITY PROBE and claimed the
     degree map hits g "unconditionally on the curve". FALSE, arithmetically: CurveDivisor.deg is
     weighted by residue degrees (Divisor.lean:61), so its image is index*Z. On a genus-1 curve of
     index 3 over Q no divisor of degree 1 = g exists and the theorem is a VACUOUS TRUTH. The
     campaign reference does not escape it: deg (m . fiberWeilDivisor) = m*delta (WindowLedger:133)
     requires delta | g. So the face RELOCATES the hypothesis (Z is an ARGUMENT), it does not
     discharge it. Exactly the reduction-to-a-possibly-false-hypothesis trap this project has
     recorded twice -- passes every census because it IS then a theorem.
 (2) THE BINDING LIMIT IS NOT THE DESCENT ONE I DISCLOSED. Since the splitting field L is
     existential inside the proof, the reference binder is UNIFORM: forall L, deg L (Zof L) = g,
     over every extension including L = k. Strictly stronger than the degree-0 face asks, and it
     has NO PRODUCER anywhere in the tree.
 (3) THE CONE IS NOT Challenge-FREE, which w4-datj 0.5/3.4 make BINDING for a DAT-J producer:
     DivisorDatumRankOne -> Cohomology/H1BaseFieldInvariance:6 -> Challenge. So "available today"
     does NOT mean "consumable by DJ-2/DJ-3 today". Separately: 0.5's own claim that FLVClass is
     Challenge-free is also false at HEAD (Degree.lean:7 -> ChiCurve -> Challenge), so the standing
     "never riemann_inequality_curve" rule no longer avoids the cycle. Tree-wide, pre-existing,
     and it needs its own decision.
 (4) A docstring advertised PicRepDatum.exists_effective_deg_eq_at_point, which DOES NOT EXIST.
     So the one face that would consume the Pic^0 universal property is absent; lam/hlam remain
     caller-supplied.

SO THE HONEST STATE OF THE EFFECTIVITY HALF: divRep-free, and CONDITIONAL on an arithmetic
hypothesis about the curve's index that nothing produces. Not discharged.

WHAT DAT-J OWES NOW: (a) a degree-g divisor over the relevant field -- an index condition, newly
visible and genuinely open; (b) descent from the splitting field to kappa(y) (dat-g); (c) the Abel
square at an INDEPENDENTLY PINNED pt (the s0012 retraction stands); (d) a PicRepDatum from DAT-G
(divRep-gated); (e) a Challenge-free route for the whole producer cone. DJ-0 remains landed.

THE GAP WAS ONE CONJUNCT, AND IT WAS A STATEMENT GAP. Every effectivity lemma in the tree stops
at "0 <= E and picClass E = picClass W" with NO claim about deg E (exists_effective_of_picClass
FLVClass:208, exists_effective_of_h0_pos SectionBound:175), while effectiveDivisorClassifyZar

   It does not. The five steps from a POINT to a divisor are all landed and all divRep-free:
   Over.testPoint (Pic0ChartTestPoint:176), mem_pic0Subgroup_iff, exists_splitting_of_picEt
   (Pic0ChartSplit:143, UNCONDITIONAL on the curve), classDeg_presenting_eq_zero
   (Pic0ChartCoverageDegreeStep2:98), then the brick.
 * The same docstring predicted a fiberTwist shift. NONE is needed: at degree exactly g the RR
   entry condition 1 <= deg W + chi(O) reads g <= deg W, so the class sits ON THE BOUNDARY and
   fires with no slack.

SO THE TWO HALVES OF STEP 3 WERE NEVER GATED ALIKE, and this row priced them together -- hiding
a discharged half behind a gated one. Only the Abel SQUARE is divRep-gated, because naming abel
at all requires the representation.

WHAT REMAINS, exactly:

     field L, while hlift wants a morphism out of Spec kappa(y). That is dat-g's work.
 (2) the Abel-compatibility square at a pt PINNED INDEPENDENTLY (the s0012 retraction below

The Riemann-Roch half produces D; the compatibility half is the honest residue. The split into

CURRENT STATE, READ THIS FIRST (review-ajcr r4, 2026-07-30). Everything below
this block is the audit HISTORY: five layers of correction and self-correction,
in which the actual costing does not appear until roughly halfway down. It is
kept because each retraction is evidence, but a lane picking a target should
read this block and then jump to the header "THE COSTING, RE-RANKED".

THE MACHINE IS SOUND AND HAS NOTHING TO FEED IT. pic0RepresentableByOfCharts
(Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161) and mixedParamRepresentableBy
(Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree.lean:125) are sorry-free, kernel-confirmed, non-circular,
and WOULD produce a representing scheme. All three antecedents are undischarged
and no sorry-free witness exists for any of them.

 3. rep i (a representation of divFunctor at each parameter) -- the divisor-

RIDERS THAT ARE NOT SEPARATE OBLIGATIONS, both established by retraction below:

chi = 1 - n. With n free and no chi hypothesis the goal FAILS, and it still fails

the conversion (I-1177).
   THE STANDING PRICE is ajcr-p2's: n > g is unreachable for a chart built on a
producer IN THIS TREE, because each such producer carries an hchi at its own
index. That is a claim about producers and a lane must keep them in view.
Whether an inhabitant exists at n != genus C is an OPEN inhabitation question

SORRY COUNT IS NOT DEBT HERE: 17 sorries, all in Challenge.lean (15, the

================================================================================

*** hcpt CLAUSE RETRACTED 2026-07-29 (review-ajcr, run 0082 s0006), refuted by ajcr-p4 (I-1007)
within minutes of my writing it. THE DEGENERACY OBSERVATION IS REAL; MY CAUSAL READING WAS
CONFOUNDED. ***

I wrote, in the self-correction below, that "hcpt is NOT an independent gate but a CONSEQUENCE of
coverage", inferred from hcpt being free at iota := PEmpty while all content sat in the
IsLocallySurjective instance. p4's refutation is decisive and I verified its pivot myself (EXIT=0):
PEmpty IS FINITE. So freeness of hcpt there is explained by the FINITE-INDEX route
(JacobianData.ofCharts with per-chart compactness at an empty cover), with coverage contributing
nothing. A degenerate index attributes to whichever hypothesis happens to vary, and I varied the
wrong one.

WHAT p4 MEASURED, more useful than my claim was: feeding the openCover route directly,
(glueData hf).openCover.compactSpace fails on EXACTLY ONE goal --
Finite (glueData hf).openCover.I0. Not chart compactness, not the cover being a cover, not
coverage. Add [Finite iota] plus per-chart CompactSpace and the same term closes. p4 also applies my
own I-0978 correctly: a failing synthesis measures the instance graph, so this does NOT prove hcpt
independent of coverage -- it shows no route in scope derives it, and the single gap on the
available route is INDEX FINITENESS, which the class-indexed atlas provably lacks.

CONSEQUENCE, and it strengthens the item rather than weakening it: DO NOT schedule "derive hcpt
from coverage". The two honest options are the ones the tree names -- a finite atlas, or the Abel
image (JacobianData.ofChartsOfAbelImage out of a quasi-compact DivScheme). The class-indexed atlas
needs the second, and PRICING IT is the unowned work. Row AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-j points there.

*** SELF-CORRECTION 2026-07-29, SAME SESSION (review-ajcr, run 0082 s0006, after a fresh-context
review of my OWN correction below). THE FOURTH ITEM IS NOT AN ANTECEDENT AT ALL -- IT IS A RIDER
ON antecedent 3, AND I PROVED IT RATHER THAN ARGUED IT. Read this before the arithmetic
correction that follows; that correction's CONCLUSION survives but its UNIT OF PRICING was wrong. ***

WHAT I GOT RIGHT AND WHAT I GOT WRONG. Right: the count was 3-of-3 where the goal needs more, the
"derived, not assumed" sentence was misleading, and ajcr-p4's discharge is real. WRONG: I priced
hD : forall i, LocallyOfFiniteType (D i).hom as a FOURTH INDEPENDENT ANTECEDENT that p4 removed,
and justified its cheapness by the CARRIER the divRep lane happens to return today
(locallyOfFiniteType_divSchemeOverHom). That argument is CONTINGENT -- it would need re-measuring
if divRep ever returned a different object.

THE UNCONDITIONAL FACT, PROBED, `lake env lean` EXIT=0, axioms [propext, Classical.choice,
Quot.sound]: if divFunctor C pi n is representable by D and by D', and D'.hom is locally of finite
type, then D.hom is. Three lines -- e := rep.uniqueUpToIso rep', e.hom.left is IsIso via
Over.comp_left on hom_inv_id, then rw [<- Over.w e.hom] and infer_instance.

SO hD IS AN INVARIANT OF THE FUNCTOR AT THE PARAMETER, not a property of the chosen carrier. No
producer of rep can choose a D that fails it, and none can be blamed for one that does. The right
place for it on this board is as a RIDER ON THE rep ROW (divrep), not as an item of its own -- a
row that lists it separately INFLATES the antecedent count, which is the same error in the
opposite direction from the one I was correcting.

THE ANTECEDENT LIST OF THE GOAL, corrected again and now on unconditional grounds:
 1. hf = IsChartUniv. OPEN (chart-restrict, ajcr-p1).
 2. Zariski-local surjectivity of Sigma.desc. OPEN (dat-b, ajcr-p2).
 3. rep i, divisor representability -- CARRYING hD as a rider that costs its producer nothing.
    OPEN (divrep.u2).
 4. quasiCompact. OPEN, and see the degeneracy note below, which reprices it.

AND A DEGENERACY THAT REPRICES quasiCompact, measured on the same pass. At iota := PEmpty EVERY
explicit input of jacobianDataOfMixedParamCharts is free -- hf/hdeg/V/hD/m/Z/nn by PEmpty.elim,
and hcpt free too because an empty family glues to an EMPTY space (IsEmpty => CompactSpace by
inferInstance). ALL the content sits in the single IsLocallySurjective instance. The output is
nevertheless NOT vacuous, and that was also probed (EXIT=0, same axioms): that instance at PEmpty
implies False, because JacobianData.rep yields a point of J over every test (homEquiv.symm 1)
while J.left is empty. TWO CONSEQUENCES: (a) the assembly is sound and falsifiable, so nothing
here is a HasDivFunctor-style vacuity; (b) hcpt is NOT an independent gate of this shape but a
CONSEQUENCE of coverage -- and any future "hcpt discharged" measured at a small atlas measures
nothing at all.

ALSO CORRECTED, and it is a false absolute I repeated from p4's file: "the only declaration in
Picard/ whose conclusion is LocallyOfFiniteType is locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom". There are FIVE
non-local ones plus 38 local re-derivations; the omitted ones include the very instance
(DivSchemeQProj.lean:199) that Pic0AtlasFiniteType.lean imports and cites to make hD free, so the
absolute is refuted by that file's own closing section. THE DEFENSIBLE FORM, which is what a board
row should say: no producer AT A CHART. Same absolute is live on row
AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-glue.atlas-lft ("exactly ONE declaration") -- narrow it there too.

*** ARITHMETIC CORRECTION 2026-07-29 (review-ajcr, run 0082 s0006). THE ANTECEDENT COUNT ON THIS
ROW WAS THREE-OF-THREE WHERE THE GOAL NEEDS FOUR-OF-FOUR, AND ONE SENTENCE BELOW IS MISLEADING
IN THE DIRECTION THAT MATTERS. Audited ajcr-p4's finding (I-0967/I-0977); it is CORRECT. ***

THE SENTENCE TO FIX IS MINE. Below, this row says the big-site sheaf condition, the 01JJ gluing

locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom (JacobianDataCharts.lean:154) TAKES

ARBITRARY window data, via the global instance locallyOfFiniteType_divSchemeOverHom
(DivSchemeQProj.lean:199), and DivOver (DivRepGlobalClassify.lean:113-116, :308) is an instance of

WHAT REPLACES THE THREE-ITEM LIST, as the antecedent list of the GOAL:
 1. hf = IsChartUniv. OPEN (chart-restrict, ajcr-p1).
 2. Zariski-local surjectivity of Sigma.desc. OPEN (dat-b, ajcr-p2).
 3. rep i, divisor representability. OPEN (divrep.u2, ajcr-p3).
 4. hlft, chart finiteness. DISCHARGED at the real atlas, free at the rep carrier.
 5. quasiCompact. OPEN and GENUINELY A-POSTERIORI, and this is the item to watch now that 4 is

THE VERDICT IS UNCHANGED: none of the three OPEN antecedents closes this week (I-0873). Item 4

Pic0AtlasFiniteType.lean:65 claims "everything in it other than hf, the local-surjectivity

*** SELF-CORRECTION 2026-07-29, SAME SESSION (review-ajcr, run 0082 s0004, after a fresh-context
review of my own work). THE IsPlusHonest FINDING BELOW IS OVERSTATED ON THE STEP THAT CARRIES IT.
The route-decision conclusion SURVIVES, for a different and better-evidenced reason. ***

WHAT I GOT WRONG. I argued: relPicToPicEt lands in PicEtAff.unit, unit is mk at the TRIVIAL cover
`.self A` alone, therefore honesty asserts that no nontrivial etale cover is needed. That step is
FALSE. PicEtAff.unit_eq_mk (Picard/RelPicCoverInjective.lean:48) proves a unit class is presented on
EVERY cover E, not only on `.self` -- so "mk at the trivial cover" describes one PRESENTATION, not
the RANGE, and nothing follows about which classes the range contains.

AND THE ABSOLUTE FORM IS REFUTED BY A LANDED THEOREM IN THIS TREE:
PicEtAff.unit_surjective_of_section (Picard/EffectivityClose.lean:141) proves the unit SURJECTIVE
over a field test K admitting a curve point sigma, upgraded to a MulEquiv by
PicEtAff.unitEquiv_of_section (:186). Over such tests honesty is DISCHARGED OUTRIGHT -- vacuously
true, no etale cover needed anywhere. So "IsPlusHonest is the sheafification gap asserted of an
arbitrary section" is wrong as an absolute.

THE CORRECTED CLAIM, which is narrower and better supported. The gap is at a GENERAL AFFINE BASE
WITH NO SECTION, and the tree documents exactly why:
 * the field route closes only through etale-cover cofinality in finite separable field extensions
   (Algebra.EtaleCover.exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom, EtaleCover.lean:287) -- there is NO
   general-base analogue of that cofinality;
 * EffectivityMoving.lean:41-48 states plainly that for a merely quasi-finite (non-finite) etale
   cover the moving statement is FALSE, with a counterexample sketch (B = A_u x A_v over a
   2-dimensional normal local A with nontrivial local class group). So the [Module.Finite A B]
   hypothesis in the effectivity layer is load-bearing, not convenience.

SO THE OBSTRUCTION IS BASE-SHAPE, NOT ARBITRARINESS OF THE CLASS. Two consequences:
 1. the split to hand a prover lane is NOT "chart value (cheap) vs arbitrary section (blocked)" but
    "field test with a section (FREE) vs general sectionless affine base (OPEN)". The delta between
    the chart side and the coverage side is NARROWER than I priced it;
 2. antecedent 2 still owes a route decision -- which site coverage is local for -- because the
    repair still refines covers and descends, and Zariski-local surjectivity still will not absorb
    that. The conclusion stands; cite the module-finiteness counterexample, NOT the trivial-cover
    claim, when repeating it.

Also corrected, same review: I called DivisorFamilyAffThetaTyping.lean UNROOTED. It is ROOTED --
AlgebraicJacobian.lean:346 imports it at HEAD (commit 2b8cef366) and its .olean exists, so it IS
kernel-checked. Another lane rooted it while I was auditing it and I did not re-run the grep before
publishing. I-0941's step (i) is therefore already done; its step (ii) stands.

--- the original finding follows; read its trivial-cover reasoning as retracted ---

*** RANKING AMENDMENT, second reviewer pass 2026-07-29 (run 0082 session 0004, review-ajcr).
ANTECEDENT 2 IS NOT A GEOMETRY BILL, IT IS A SITE DECISION -- so the #2 slot below is
MIS-JUSTIFIED even though its position may be right. Issue I-0920. ***

The costing below is otherwise intact and should be read as it stands. This amendment changes ONE
thing: the reason antecedent 2 (dat-b B-5/B-6, local surjectivity) is expensive.

BELOW IT SAYS: "It carries the content, and its packaging is complete ... What it owes is geometry:
the per-point datum, plus the chart-parameter/threshold reconciliation."

MEASURED, tracing the per-point datum through its own producer chain rather than through the rows'
prose. The producer exists (exists_isChartDatumPlusFibre_of_mem_range, rooted, sorry-free), and what
it needs reduces to ONE hypothesis: IsPlusHonest (Pic0ChartPlusFibreProducer.lean:200). Read as a
statement, that says: for every affine open U of the test, the class restricted to U lies in the
RANGE of relPicToPicEt -- i.e. Zariski-locally the class comes from the UN-sheafified relPic.

That is the etale-sheafification gap, structurally:
 * picEt is built on PicEtAff (PicEt.lean:9-21), and PicEtAff C A (PicEtAff.lean:218) is a QUOTIENT
   OVER ALL ETALE COVERS -- elements are PicEtAff.mk E x;
 * PicEtAff.unit (:377), the target of relPicToPicEt (PicEtUnit.lean:126), is mk at the TRIVIAL
   cover `.self A` alone.
So honesty asserts that no nontrivial etale cover is needed on that piece -- precisely what the
one-step plus construction exists to permit to FAIL. The tree's only honesty mechanism agrees:
Pic0ChartHonest.lean's own "does not give" says honesty holds over Spec E.Carrier and NOT over
Spec A, bought by CHANGING THE BASE, with "Nothing here performs that descent".

WHY THE CHART SIDE IS UNAFFECTED, which is what makes this a real distinction rather than a blanket
pessimism: chartValue = abelDiv * sigmaFamily * (thetaFamily^m)^{-1} (DivSchemeAbel.lean:351, read
from the definition), and honesty is discharged for each factor and closed under the group
operations. Coverage is different because chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise
(Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise.lean:128) quantifies over EVERY s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T);
arbitrariness is the content of coverage, and narrowing s to chart-value shape makes it circular.

CONSEQUENCE. Antecedent 2 splits into a cheap half and an out-of-reach half, and the rows conflate
them: honesty of coverage's own WITNESS is already covered; honesty of the class coverage must HIT
is the gap. The repair -- refine to the etale carrier, then descend -- changes the site from Zariski
to etale, and pic0RepresentableByOfCharts' antecedent is Zariski-local surjectivity. No leaf settles
that. It is a route question for the human/reviewer layer, and it is the third antecedent-level
obstruction found on this seam after the unrestricted-certificate fork (antecedent 1) and U2.

NOT A REFUTATION. Proving IsPlusHonest false for an arbitrary class needs a class not
Zariski-locally in relPic's image; this tree has no Brauer or nontrivial-etale-class machinery to
build one, and I did not build it. The claim is the weaker sufficient one: it is not a lemma about
the tree's own constructions, and a lane sent at it will not find a proof.

THE VERDICT BELOW ("none of the three antecedents closes this week") is unchanged and, if anything,
better supported: the antecedent that looked closest to being a bounded geometry bill is the one
that turns out to need a decision above the leaf layer.

*** THE COSTING, RE-RANKED 2026-07-29 (run 0082, review-ajcr). THE THREE ANTECEDENTS ARE NOT THREE
INDEPENDENT PRICES, AND NONE OF THEM CLOSES THIS WEEK. Read this before picking a leaf. ***

WHAT IS GENUINELY SOUND, and it is worth stating first because it is unusual: pic0RepresentableByOfCharts
(Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161) and mixedParamRepresentableBy (Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree.lean:125) are
sorry-free, rooted, and honest. Given the three antecedents they WOULD produce a representing scheme.
The machine is correct. Nothing feeds it.

THE THREE ANTECEDENTS DO NOT COMPOSE AS THE ROWS IMPLY. Measured, `lake env lean` EXIT=0 (probes in
run 0082 session dir /probes):
 (1) `hf` = IsChartUniv (Pic0ChartPair.lean:173) is stated at a FREE `V : D.left.Opens`. At ι = PEmpty
     the whole seam call elaborates with `hf := fun i => PEmpty.elim i` -- no charts, no rep, no

     So `hf` at an arbitrary V carries NO CONTENT.
     QUALIFIED by ajcr-p1 (I-0890), correctly: 'free at V = bottom' is true of the INJECTIVITY clause
     and of exists_factor, and FALSE of the fibre DATUM -- its sq field at an empty test needs
     Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C ..) over an empty base, which is true, separate, and absent from the

     SATISFIABLE come apart, and several rows on this leaf have been priced by exactly that

 (2) The seam is nonetheless NOT vacuous: at ι = PEmpty the sup sieve is BOTTOM, and the bottom sieve
     is Zariski-covering only for an EMPTY test. So ALL the content forcing the atlas to be an atlas
     sits in the LOCAL-SURJECTIVITY instance -- antecedent 2, not antecedent 1.
 (3) THE UNPRICED OBLIGATION, which no row owned before this pass: coverage
     (chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise, Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise.lean:128) must produce
     `x : (W : Scheme) ⟶ X i`, i.e. INTO `(V i : Scheme)`. So coverage must hit the SAME V at which

     files in the tree mention both IsChartUniv and ChartsCoverLocally. Now owned by
     AJCR.w4-rep.datum.chart-restrict (ajcr-p1, I-0869/I-0872).

WORSE, AND INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED WITH ajcr-p1: the only non-circular producer of `hf`,
isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre (Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean:170), goes THROUGH the unrestricted
certificate -- its body is `isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented` with the restriction
applied afterwards. So IsChartLocusFibre implies IsOpenImmersion.presheaf of the UNRESTRICTED Abel
chart, which three headers call false (|D| is not a point). QUALIFICATION I add: that falsity is a
HEADER CLAIM, unproved -- isEmpty_forall_chartFibrePresented_of_not_injective
(Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean:219) takes non-injectivity as a HYPOTHESIS and is never
instantiated. So the tree holds a reduction and its conditional refutation and has connected neither.

THE RANKING, corrected. Not by ease -- by what a discharge would actually buy:
 1. chart-restrict (the V-coupling + a fibre criterion at the RESTRICTED chart). Held by ajcr-p1.

 2. Antecedent 2, local surjectivity (dat-b B-5/B-6). It carries the content, and its packaging is

Independently re-derived this round before reading ADDENDUM 4, and it agrees: for every g >= 2 take a pencil of degree g on C containing a divisor E >= s_0 + s_infinity. Such an E exists because l(E) = 1 + l(K-E) and any E with s_0 + s_infinity <= E <= K' for a canonical K' >= s_0 + s_infinity has l(K-E) >= 1; the required K' exists since l(K - s_0 - s_infinity) >= g - 2 >= 1 for g >= 3, and for g = 2 exactly when s_infinity is the hyperelliptic conjugate of s_0. The total space of the pencil is an open subscheme of the irreducible C, hence irreducible, hence connected after every Zariski shrink of the base -- which is why the shrink evasion that kills the g = 1 case does not apply. So the fixed-pair route is dead on the campaign's own stratum, and the live question is only R1-versus-R2.

items.summary:
S3 (WORKSHEET-FIRST, risk R3): SmoothOfRelativeDimension (genus C) d.J.hom -- the frozen numeral.

THE CRITERION IS LANDED (run 0073 r5), AbelianVariety/RelativeDimensionLocal.lean, lake env lean EXIT=0. SmoothOfRelativeDimension n is IsLocalAtSource at the Zariski precoverage (verified by inferInstance, with Smooth as a control), so IsLocalAtSource.of_zeroHypercover applies: the obligation is 'cover d.J.left by opens on which the count holds', not 'exhibit a chart at every scheme point'. Landed: smoothOfRelativeDimension_comp_iso (the source-iso transport, named because infer_instance does NOT find it -- the instance is on the property, not the composite), smoothOfRelativeDimension_of_zeroHypercover plus its iff form, and the two Jacobian shapes JacobianData.smoothOfRelativeDimension_of_translation_cover / ..._pointTranslationIso.

TWO INPUTS REMAIN AND -- CORRECTED r8 -- BOTH COST SOMETHING.
 (1) THE NUMERAL: n = g at the identity is T5, itself conditional on the T3/T4 eps-kernel count, which needs the SEMILINEAR comparison and not just the kernel bijection. Still gated.
 (2) THE COVER (hcov): that translated identity charts cover d.J.left.

WHY (2) IS A GENUINE OPEN INPUT AND NOT BOOKKEEPING -- this row and worksheet 3.1 previously said the covering demand 'is met by the same X2 transport 3 already cites'. THAT CLAUSE IS STRUCK (r8, worksheet 3.2, struck at its own site in 3.1 as well). Two halves:

 * What X2 gives: per rational point, an iso, hence via smoothOfRelativeDimension_pointTranslationIso the count on ONE translated chart. It does NOT give that those charts COVER.
 * What the sibling proved: ajc-pic0av (cross-project thread I-0495) REFUTED ITS OWN reduction of dim Pic0 = g, whose 'orbit condition' -- every point of Pic0 is a translate of the identity by k-RATIONAL sections -- is CONTRADICTORY for g >= 1. A translation is an iso hence a homeomorphism; the identity point is closed (a section of a map to Spec k is a closed immersion); homeomorphisms preserve closed points; so every point is closed, i.e. T1, and a nonempty sober T1 space has topologicalKrullDim 0. So the natural route to hcov (rational translates exhausting the points) is not merely unproved but FALSE in the range that matters.

THE GOOD HALF OF THE SAME MESSAGE, and it confirms this row's shape from the other side: ajc-pic0av observes that smoothOfRelativeDimension_of_translation_cover quantifies over a ZeroHypercover, i.e. over OPENS, and is therefore IMMUNE -- 'restate it over POINTS and the theorem is lost'. So the opens-form is not merely sufficient, it is NECESSARY, established by a lane that reached the contradiction the point-form implies. Keep the ZeroHypercover binder.

SIZING UNCHANGED: S3 stays [M]. If (2) fails outright, worksheet 3's kbar route plus the t4-5 codescent brick is the documented contingency; r5's locality work does NOT retire that brick, it removed only the third input (pointwise reachability).

METHOD NOTES worth keeping: (i) inbox I-0695 -- r5's caveat was a CORRECT reading of the class's unfolded statement that priced a consequence the statement does not have; unfolding a class says what must be PRODUCED, not what machinery exists to produce it. (ii) r8's addition -- and a correct reading can also OVERSTATE who supplies an input; 3.1 was right that the demand is weaker and wrong that X2 meets it.

items.summary:
Wave 5: Pic^0 is an abelian variety of dimension g. STATE at run 0073 r8: 11 of 16 children done. Open: T3's COMPOSITE, T5's numeral, S1, S3, and the DD-gated P1.

THE T-CHAIN IS COMPLETE EXCEPT FOR THE COMPOSITION, and r8 closed the last named non-composite residue. Landed statements: (T3-1) h1AddEquivTruncExpCechKernel, (T3-2) EpsArrowIdentification, (T3-3) TwoChartKernelComparison (twoChartClass is a BIJECTION of the two kernels), (T3-4) CechPicIsoTransport, (T3-5) CollapseCechH1, (T3-6a) EpsReductionSquare (the section equation plus the opens/family transport), and hchart DISCHARGED at the Wave-5 charts (EpsChartTrivialInstance). Composing them into H1(C,O) ~+ ker(CechPic(C_eps) -> CechPic(C)) is written nowhere and is T3's entire residue.

THE STRUCTURAL LESSON OF THIS WAVE, and r8 is the fourth session to meet it: rows repeatedly say 'the pieces are landed, what remains is assembly' while the ARROWS between the pieces are absent. The one-second test is a CONSUMER GREP -- count occurrences of each landed carrier OUTSIDE its defining file. Run over the whole Wave-5 surface at r8: EIGHT landed declarations with ZERO external consumers (the four S3 lemmas, twoChartKernelEquiv, collapseCechH1Equiv, cechPicMapEquivOfIso, appLE_dualNumberSections), and the hchart producer with FOUR external occurrences that were ALL PROSE. A level check comparing CARRIERS cannot see this; only a consumer grep can. I-0711 / I-0630.

AND THE SECOND HALF, sharpened by r8 into a rule about MEASUREMENT rather than about naming. r7 established: a residue named accurately is not thereby measured -- write the Lean statement and read the leftover goals before writing a size. r8 establishes the limit of that method: READING THE LEFTOVER GOALS MEASURES THE DIFFICULTY BUT DOES NOT ENUMERATE THE INGREDIENTS. r7's 7.8 read the goal text, reported '[S], NO MISSING INPUT IDENTIFIED', and was right about the content and wrong about the list: its square spelled one open in relCurve C k's own form, so a non-rfl transport (relCurveMap ^-1 fst_{k[eps]} ^-1 W vs fst_k ^-1 W) sat inside the elaborated TYPE and never surfaced as a goal. Probe the equalities a statement ASSUMES, not only the goals it LEAVES.

A THIRD METHOD POINT, new at r8 and cheap to miss: a rw that changes nothing and reports no error is a wrong DEFINITION, not a failing tactic. An open-equality transport built as h |> RingEquiv.refl typechecks and then silently blocks every rewrite (lean_goal identical before and after, no error message). Build transports from the API's own restriction maps -- resHom at le_of_eq -- as Cohomology/RelThetaTransportCore.presheafCongr already does.

CHILD STATE, one line each:
 * .data .g1 .p2 .p3 .x1 .x2 .x3 .t1 .t2 .t4 .s2 -- done.
 * .t3 -- seven arrows landed (r8 added the section equation and hchart's instantiation); residue is the COMPOSITION only, plus the separate question of whether it comes out ADDITIVE. Two cautions in the row: the elaborated square's cost is UNMEASURED (the timeouts were under load ~60 with swap exhausted), and MulEquiv.toAdditive does not give the intertwining law.
 * .t5 -- ACTIVE. Spine landed. Conditional on hdim, which needs the SEMILINEAR comparison (AddEquiv + intertwining across kappa(e) ~+* k). A bare kernel bijection does NOT give it. Same residue AJC isolated as semilinearComparison_cotangentSpaceDual_h1Cok.
 * .s1 -- pending, a HYPOTHESIS by design: S2/S3 take GeometricallyReduced as an instance argument, so keeping S1 open blocks nothing.
 * .s3 -- pending. Criterion landed (the obligation is a COVER, not a chart at every point). CORRECTED r8: BOTH remaining inputs cost something. The numeral is T5; and hcov is a genuine open input, not bookkeeping -- X2 gives the count on each translated chart but NOT that they cover, and ajc-pic0av has since shown the natural route (rational translates exhausting the points) is CONTRADICTORY for g >= 1. The ZeroHypercover/opens shape is what makes the S3 criterion survive that; do not restate it over points.
 * .p1 -- BLOCKED, cross-wave gate on the DD shapes freeze. Not attempted, not built against a guessed shape.

CRITICAL PATH TO THE PARENT: T3's composition -> T5's numeral -> S3's assembly. S1 is off it; P1 is gated elsewhere; nothing in the T-chain waits on the DD freeze.

D6 of informal/w6-port-worksheet.md gates the Sym^g fork, not this leaf; the lane table gives genus0 the dep 'far gate', and nothing in 'd.J is terminal' mentions a DD-layer declaration. REPRICED: the recon (row S11) budgeted 'Jacobian C iso 1_ + Milne I 3.9 (rational maps P1 -> A constant)'. Milne I 3.9 buys EXISTENCE of the factorisation only. Uniqueness is cancel_epi, and the Epi input is DISCHARGED not assumed: terminal d.J => IsIso J.hom (Over.mkIdTerminal) => Over.w right-cancels Surjective AND Flat from C.hom onto (ofCurve P).left, and every morphism to Spec of a FIELD is flat, so the only real input is that C is nonempty. THE DEBT, honestly: the hypothesis is pic0Subgroup C T = bot for ALL T, NOT genus C = 0. Deriving the former from the latter is real curve theory (relative 'genus 0 with a rational point is P1') and is NOT proved. Residue is now ONE implication about Picard groups plus Milne I 3.9 for existence.

items.title: B-2: PicEtAff base-field shuffle — D2-ii core + B-1 instantiation (Picard/PicEtAffBaseFieldShuffle.lean); gate D2-ii core (F-2 lane)

comments.author: horizon
comments.body: D2-ii SHARED CORE LANDED (by the F-2 lane, commit 2e2ee3c41, file Picard/PicEtAffTransport.lean, wired) — B-2 consumes this interface, do not rebuild the plumbing. THE INTERFACE: structure AlgebraicGeometry.RelPicTransportFamily (kT : Type u) [Field kT] [Algebra kD kT] [Algebra kE kT] (D : Over (Spec (.of kD))) (E : Over (Spec (.of kE))) — kD kE are implicit Field variables; DIRECTION CONVENTION: the scheme family points D-side -> E-side and the induced Pic maps go E -> D. Fields (each over the per-B pack [CommRing B] [Algebra kD B] [Algebra kE B] [Algebra kT B] [IsScalarTower kD kT B] [IsScalarTower kE kT B]): hom B : (D (x) overSpec kD B).left --> (E (x) overSpec kE B).left; hom_snd : hom B >> (snd E (overSpec kE B)).left = (snd D (overSpec kD B)).left; hom_naturality : for (fD : B ->a[kD] B') (fE : B ->a[kE] B') with (forall b, fD b = fE b): hom B' >> (E <| Over.overSpecMap fE).left = (D <| Over.overSpecMap fD).left >> hom B. DERIVED (namespace RelPicTransportFamily, T a family): T.relPicHom B : relPic E (overSpec kE B) ->* relPic D (overSpec kD B) with @[simp] relPicHom_mk; T.relPicAlgMap_relPicHom (the bilateral square, same-function-pair form — feed it (j.restrictScalars kD, j.restrictScalars kE, fun _ => rfl) for any A-algebra map j); T.relPicHom_mem_descentClasses; T.descentHom U : descentClasses E U ->* descentClasses D U with @[simp] descentHom_coe; T.descentHom_descentMap (refinement compat); T.picEtAffHom A : PicEtAff E A ->* PicEtAff D A with @[simp] picEtAffHom_mk (SAME cover index) and picEtAffHom_unit; T.map_picEtAffHom (instance form; needs [Algebra A A'] [IsScalarTower kD A A'] [IsScalarTower kE A A'] plus the pack on A'); T.mapAlg_picEtAffHom (phi : A ->a[kT] A'; relates mapAlg E (phi.restrictScalars kE) and mapAlg D (phi.restrictScalars kD)); T.relPicHom_relPicHom and T.picEtAffHom_picEtAffHom (S : RelPicTransportFamily kT E D with forall B [pack], S.hom B >> T.hom B = id (E (x) overSpec kE B).left implies S.picEtAffHom A (T.picEtAffHom A a) = a) — the MulEquiv engine: instantiate BOTH directions and apply it twice. B-2 RECIPE per worksheet D2-ii: forward family Tfwd : RelPicTransportFamily L C_L C (i.e. kD := L, kE := k, kT := L; over-fields [Algebra L L]=id and [Algebra k L] ambient): hom B := (crossBaseIso k L C (overSpec L B)).hom >> (C <| (mapOverSpecIso k L B).hom).left — the per-B pack gives exactly [Algebra k B] [Algebra L B] [IsScalarTower k L B], the hypotheses of B-1's mapOverSpecIso; hom_snd from B-1's crossBaseIso_hom_snd + mapOverSpecIso_*_left = id; hom_naturality from B-1's crossBaseIso_naturality at t := Over.overSpecMap (L-side map) + the matching triangle. Backward Tbwd : RelPicTransportFamily L C C_L with the inverse composites. INSTANTIATION GOTCHA (only relevant when two of kD/kE/kT coincide SYNTACTICALLY, as in F-2; B-2's fields have genuinely distinct instances so this should NOT arise): the per-B pack has separate instance binders; if they coincide propositionally, collapse by the algebra_eq_of_tower + obtain-rfl pattern in Picard/PicEtAffCurveMap.lean. Also note: do NOT hand pullback.map terms with Spec-typed identity legs into the hom field — such terms are not type-correct at instances transparency and break all downstream rw/simp (this was diagnosed the hard way in the F-2 lane); build hom from B-1's iso composites (already correctly typed) or whiskers.

items.title: Codim-one & Thm 3.2 rational-map extension
items.summary:
**Codim-one & Thm 3.2 rational-map extension.** A rational map from a smooth variety to an abelian variety extends off a locus of codimension $\ge 2$:
$$X\dashrightarrow A\ \Longrightarrow\ X\setminus Z\to A,\ \operatorname{codim}Z\ge 2.$$
Milne 3.1 (codim-$\ge2$ indeterminacy, valuative) and the empty-locus extension theorem are proved; `Thm32RationalMapExtension` is sorry-free. The chain is now gated on the single remaining leaf **Milne 3.3** (`indeterminacy_pure_codim_one_into_grpScheme`): a pure-codim-$1$ indeterminacy point of a map into a group scheme forces the difference-map contradiction.

tasks.objective:
CLOSE THE ALBANESE LEG. Roadmap AJC.albanese and its three children (.codim1, .symmetric, .universal). The headline universal-property theorem is ALREADY sorry-free — what is missing is the construction layer beneath it, so this task is about supplying real inputs to a statement that already stands, not about restating anything.

THREE FRONTS, with the actual sorry sites.

 (a) CODIMENSION-ONE RATIONAL-MAP EXTENSION (AJC.albanese.codim1). Albanese/CodimOneExtension.lean: CodimOneFree (:216, :218), gammaSpecField_ringEquiv (:752), localRing_dvr_of_codim_one (:1402), indeterminacy_pure_codim_one_into_grpScheme (:1751). Finish the diagonal-intersection and function-field pullback steps showing a rational map to an abelian variety has no codimension-one indeterminacy. The blueprint frontier flags Milne Lemma 3.3 (pure-codim-1 structure of the indeterminacy locus into a group variety) as 22 unlocks / 23 uses — the highest-leverage node in this cone, and the sibling Rebuild has a whole Albanese/CodimOne* family (CodimOneMilne31, CodimOneStalkRegularity, CodimOneDVRStalk, CodimOneSmoothReduced) covering the same ground. READ THOSE FIRST.

 (b) ABEL-JACOBI AND SYMMETRIC POWERS (AJC.albanese.symmetric). Albanese/AlbaneseUP.lean: abelJacobi (:335), SymmetricPower (:382), symmetricPowerAVMap (:416), symmetricPowerToJacobian (:453), descentThroughBirationalSigma (:496), albanese_eq_iff_symmetricPower_eq (:533). Six honest construction and bridge gaps: Abel-Jacobi, the symmetric-power carrier and quotient API, symmetric sums, the map to Pic0, birational descent, the factorisation connector. The characteristic-free symmetric-power route is already specified cleanly in the blueprint — follow it rather than inventing a route.

 (c) THE UNIVERSAL PROPERTY (AJC.albanese.universal). Complete descent through the birational g-th symmetric power and the factorisation biconditional. The connector now has the correct two directions: pointed rigidity plus quotient uniqueness forward, restriction along Q -> Q+(g-1)P0 backward. Two typed-sorry bridges; once they close, the existing theorem stands unconditionally.

RIGIDITY IS YOURS TOO, if it blocks you: RigidityLemma.lean has three open obligations (:481 saturated-open-to-affine, :673 dense-open, :764 rigidity_core) and pointed rigidity is a direct input to (c).

DISCIPLINE. Search before proving — horizon search spans your project, the sibling Rebuild, the standalone SubProjects/Albanese, and mathlib. The Rebuild Albanese/ directory is 24 files / 7.3k lines and its codim-one family is more developed than yours in places. Use the LSP loop between edits, lake build at session boundaries.

COORDINATION. You are one of four AJC teams. You consume Pic0 facts from ajc-pic0av (degree map, Pic0(k) = ker degree) — ask on the AJC conversation thread rather than proving them yourself or editing Picard/. Your files are Albanese/ and RigidityLemma.lean. Never edit files outside Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge.

Fresh-context audit ran and found a REAL DEFECT, now repaired (commit 1c12efcaf).

The audit's finding: the rank leaf was FALSE as first stated. It quantified over every finitely presented M with no flatness and no engine conclusions -- cohomology-and-base-change with its hypotheses deleted. Counterexample: A = k[x], M = O/x = coker(O --x--> O), finitely presented; Gamma(P^1_A,M) = A/(x) = k is torsion, so Module.rankAtStalk at t=(x) is the junk value 0, while the fibre is P^1_k with M_t = O and fiberH0 M t = 1. A false leaf compiles, reports clean axioms, and silently makes every consumer vacuously true -- which is exactly what had happened to my two headline assembly theorems.

Repair: Adelic.P1RankIdentity now carries the engine's own conclusions (d surjective, ker d finite, ker d PROJECTIVE, kerBaseChange bijective). Projectivity is what excludes the counterexample: for a finite projective module Module.rankAtStalk_eq identifies the stalk rank with finrank kappa(t) (kappa(t) tensor H0), and the base-change conclusion at B = kappa(t) identifies that with the fibre h0. All four hypotheses were already in scope at the single use site, so the proof body is unchanged.

Two docstring corrections from the same audit: IsIntegral (P^1_k) is INCOMPARABLE with Gamma(P^1_k,O)=k, not weaker (a double line in P^2 has H^0=k and is not reduced); and the leaves are not co-equal -- RigidPushforwardBaseChange is one of the gate's two fields and plausibly exceeds the other three combined.

tasks.objective:
You are prover lane `ajc-p1` on Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge. This round the objective is deliberately FREE: nobody has told you which declaration to prove. Your objective is to identify the MOST important open item standing between this project and Picard/Pic^0 representability, claim it publicly, and discharge it.

READ FIRST: protection item `I-0838`. It is the claim protocol for this round's ten parallel lanes and it is not optional — steps 2 through 5 (check ownership, claim with `roadmap set --owner ajc-p1`, announce, release on exit) are what stop four lanes proving the same lemma. Also read `I-0491` and `I-0492`, the two binding human decisions, before touching the seam.

YOUR RANK. You take the MOST important item. Rank is a tie-break so four lanes do not converge on one target, not a fence: if your item turns out to be blocked on another lane's, say so in the inbox and swap. On a contested item you first refusal on any contested item.

YOUR PEERS this round are ajc-p1, ajc-p2, ajc-p3, ajc-p4 plus the reviewer `review-ajc`. The reviewer is auditing route and organisation and will be correcting the board in its first hour — read its inbox items before you fix your target, and re-read them if you are about to start something large. It may direct-message you a proposal; weigh it against what you hold, and take it if it is genuinely worth more. You may propose work to the other lanes the same way (`inbox add --kind hint --to task:<lane>`), naming declaration, file, and why it beats what they hold.

HOW TO CHOOSE, since this is the part I am delegating to you. "Most important" means: measured against the project's representability headline, what does discharging this buy? A leaf that unblocks three others beats a leaf that is merely nearest. A leaf whose stated prerequisite turns out to already exist in the file beats both — earlier sessions' costings in this workspace have been wrong in that direction more than once, so read the actual Lean hypothesis, not the prose about it. Use `horizon graph -p Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge frontier` for the ranked view, `horizon roadmap list --focus AJC.picrep / AJC.jacobian` for the board, and `horizon search` (which spans both projects AND mathlib) before you prove anything — the premise you need is often already next door under a name you would not have grepped.

THE BAR, and it is higher than usual this round. An audit on 2026-07-29 sampled 101 representability claims across both projects and refuted 99: 67 were sorry-reachable, 17 VACUOUS, 12 proved something adjacent to what they claimed, 3 did not exist. So:
- Sorry-free is necessary, not sufficient. Before you report a gate closed, exhibit a witness for EVERY antecedent, or state plainly which antecedent remains undischarged. "The implication is proved" and "the conclusion holds for some curve" are different claims and I want to know which you have.
- Never introduce a class, structure field, or side condition whose statement does not mention the object it is about. The cautionary case is `HasDivFunctor`: its field asserted only that a presheaf category is nonempty, the curve did not occur, and the blueprint advertised it as the existence of the divisor functor with `\leanok`. It survived because nobody read the statement.
- Never discharge an obligation by projecting the hypothesis you assumed. `choose_spec.1` of your own binder is `P → P`.
- A green build is not evidence of non-vacuity, and `lean_multi_attempt` reports every snippet as closing the goal when the file's imports are stale. Check imports before believing a probe.
- Do not restate an obligation more weakly to make a count go down. If you cannot close it, leave it open and say why.

ONE SHARED LEDGER, ten writers. Another lane's integrate sweep can commit your half-written file before you have measured it once — write risky proofs as explicit `sorry` first, measure, then fill. Stage explicit files, never `add -A`. Commit at every coherent point; an interrupted lane loses only what was uncommitted. Follow the `lean-check` LSP loop for edits and keep `lake build` for the session boundary — nine other lanes want the build lock too.

WHERE THIS PROJECT ACTUALLY STANDS, so you do not rediscover it. The entire Jacobian tower rests on ONE bare `sorry`: `fgaPicardRepresentability` at `AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean:347`. Its unique consumer chain runs through `instHasPicSchemeEt` (an unconditional producer that is a projection of that sorry) to the headline. The legacy `HasPicScheme` class has NO instance, so the ~45 declarations taking `[HasPicScheme C]` currently prove nothing about any curve. `instPicSharpRepresentable` and `instPicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType` are `choose_spec` projections of their own hypothesis. `smoothProperQuotient` proves `P.IsRepresentable → P.IsRepresentable` with all four Kleiman hypotheses unused and zero call sites. `HasDivFunctor` is vacuous as described above.

The line-347 docstring says discharging it needs Kleiman §4 — the Abel-map slice `Div^d → Pic^d` as a smooth proper equivalence relation with scheme quotient, plus `Div` representability via Quot — while the board marks BOTH `AJC.picrep.quot` and `AJC.picrep.serre` `rejected`. That contradiction is the reviewer's first assignment; if it resolves before you fix your target, use its answer.

Board caveat: `AJC.picrep` is marked `done` and its advertised deliverable `instHasPicScheme` exists in no `.lean` file — deleted 2026-07-28 under `I-0491`, not discharged. Do not read `done` on that subtree as truth until the reviewer has corrected it. Open non-done items you might weigh: `AJC.picrep.tensor` (pullback-tensor and fibre base change), `AJC.rr.extuniform` (extension-uniform H1 vanishing, one threshold serving every fibre), `AJC.fbc.cosimplicial.twisted` (the twisted Čech nerve naturality square that separates this project from Stacks 02KH), `AJC.pic0av.tangent` / `.structure` / `.identity`, `AJC.albanese.symmetric` / `.universal`. Body-position sorries live in `Albanese/AlbaneseUP.lean` (6), `Jacobian.lean` (4), `Picard/Pic0AbelianVariety.lean` (3), `Picard/SerreFiniteness.lean` (2), `Picard/QuotFunctorDef.lean` (2), `Picard/Pic0Et.lean` (2), `Picard/IdentityComponent.lean` (2), `Picard/QuotRepresentability.lean` (1), `FGAPicRepresentability.lean` (1), `Cohomology/CechHigherDirectImageUnconditional.lean` (1).

A real option, and I want you to consider it seriously rather than defaulting to a leaf: the sibling project Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild has a genuinely sorry-free representability engine (`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`, `Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161`) whose inputs are chart data rather than Quot. `horizon search` spans both projects. If AJC's route is blocked on Quot and the sibling's is not, the highest-value thing a lane can do here may be to import or transcribe that route rather than push on Kleiman §4. Price it before you commit to it — a cross-project object-level match can be true and still irrelevant if the carrier the statement binds differs.

WHAT I WANT AT THE END. Your report should answer three things without me having to ask: which item you claimed and why it was the most important one, what its state is now (closed sorry-free with all antecedents witnessed / closed as an implication with named antecedents still open / advanced with the remaining obligation stated / blocked, with the blocker), and what you learned that changes another lane's plan. If you found a costing wrong, a vacuity, or a route problem, that goes in the inbox as an `issue` at the site that made the claim — not only in your report, which nobody downstream reads.

If your first-choice item collapses on inspection — the prerequisite already exists, or the statement turns out vacuous, or another lane got there first — that is a finding, not a wasted session. Record it, release the claim, and take the next item. Do not sit on a claimed item you are not working.

CORRECTION to my own claim from earlier this session, found by checking it instead of shipping it.

I wrote in b65f25d6a that leaf B owes 'the passage from a tangent-space dimension to Mathlib's
presentation-based SmoothOfRelativeDimension, which has no bridge in either direction' and
called it missing mathematics. That is FALSE. Mathlib v4.31 carries

  Algebra.IsStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension.iff_of_isStandardSmooth
    [Nontrivial S] [IsStandardSmooth R S] (n) :
      IsStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension n R S <-> Module.rank S Omega[S/R] = n

an IFF characterising relative dimension by the rank of the Kaehler differentials
(RingTheory/Smooth/StandardSmoothCotangent.lean). So leaf B's second obligation is a
TRANSLATION between two invariants of smoothness -- rank Omega versus tangent-space dimension,
dual over a field -- plus the affine-local-to-scheme-level passage over a cover of Pic0. That
is a materially smaller and better-specified obligation than 'missing mathematics'.

Why the search missed it, which is the part worth keeping: grepping SmoothOfRelativeDimension
for 'tangent' or 'finrank' returns nothing, and that is TRUE about the name. The bridge does not
mention tangent spaces because mathlib states smoothness through Omega. Recorded as memory
I-0446 with the general rule: when a statement seems absent, check whether the library says the
same mathematics in a different INVARIANT before recording it as missing.

Corrected in three places: the Lean docstring, the blueprint remark
(rem:tangent_versus_relative_dimension), and an hgraph comment on
lem:pic0_relative_dimension_genus so the next session working that leaf finds it on the node.

EXECUTE THE HUMAN DECISION OF 2026-07-28 (protection I-0492, inbox I-0346, roadmap AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-d.ddr.certificate): DivFamZar is widened so its cover pieces are ARBITRARY AFFINE OPENS rather than basic opens of a fixed pair of pinned P1 charts. THE STRUCTURAL MOVE, and it is the whole content of the task: THE CHART-WISE PARTITIONS OF UNITY HAVE TO GO. Per-piece swallow-or-miss needs only openness (DivSchemeCertZarConn.lean:98 uses only openness); it is the partitions that upgrade inside one piece to inside one chart. Consumers WILL break — repair them deliberately. Do not smuggle the old typing back in by typing pieces INTO the charts: DivisorFamily.lean:166/168/186 (h0 into V0, h1 into V1, pieces := Sum.elim (basicOpen . h0) (basicOpen . h1)) is exactly the pattern that made the previously-refuted joint-cover option vacuous, and changing partition FIELDS cannot change where the pieces LIVE.

TWO OBLIGATIONS THE WIDENING RELOCATES RATHER THAN REMOVES. Discharge both explicitly; neither may hide inside a LocalEquations: (i) fibrewise-finite support, which must come from the seeds own degree data and is NOT implied by anything a LocalEquations carries; (ii) whatever the old fixed-pair confinement was silently supplying to the certificate clauses.

 * DO NOT build the GL_2(k) / Aut(P1) action on P1 (leaf ...p1-aut is deprioritised, priority low). No consumer against it.
