tasks.objective:
You are prover lane `ajcr-p1` on Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild. This round the objective is deliberately FREE: nobody has told you which declaration to prove. Your objective is to identify the MOST important open item standing between this project and Picard/Pic^0 representability, claim it publicly, and discharge it.

READ FIRST: protection item `I-0838`. It is the claim protocol for this round's ten parallel lanes and it is not optional — steps 2 through 5 (check ownership, claim with `roadmap set --owner ajcr-p1`, announce, release on exit) are what stop four lanes proving the same lemma. Also read `I-0491` and `I-0492`, the two binding human decisions, before touching the seam.

YOUR RANK. You take the MOST important item. Rank is a tie-break so four lanes do not converge on one target, not a fence: if your item turns out to be blocked on another lane's, say so in the inbox and swap. On a contested item you first refusal on any contested item.

YOUR PEERS this round are ajcr-p1, ajcr-p2, ajcr-p3, ajcr-p4 plus the reviewer `review-ajcr`. The reviewer is auditing route and organisation and will be correcting the board in its first hour — read its inbox items before you fix your target, and re-read them if you are about to start something large. It may direct-message you a proposal; weigh it against what you hold, and take it if it is genuinely worth more. You may propose work to the other lanes the same way (`inbox add --kind hint --to task:<lane>`), naming declaration, file, and why it beats what they hold.

HOW TO CHOOSE, since this is the part I am delegating to you. "Most important" means: measured against the project's representability headline, what does discharging this buy? A leaf that unblocks three others beats a leaf that is merely nearest. A leaf whose stated prerequisite turns out to already exist in the file beats both — earlier sessions' costings in this workspace have been wrong in that direction more than once, so read the actual Lean hypothesis, not the prose about it. Use `horizon graph -p Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild frontier` for the ranked view, `horizon roadmap list --focus AJCR.w4-rep` for the board, and `horizon search` (which spans both projects AND mathlib) before you prove anything — the premise you need is often already next door under a name you would not have grepped.

THE BAR, and it is higher than usual this round. An audit on 2026-07-29 sampled 101 representability claims across both projects and refuted 99: 67 were sorry-reachable, 17 VACUOUS, 12 proved something adjacent to what they claimed, 3 did not exist. So:
- Sorry-free is necessary, not sufficient. Before you report a gate closed, exhibit a witness for EVERY antecedent, or state plainly which antecedent remains undischarged. "The implication is proved" and "the conclusion holds for some curve" are different claims and I want to know which you have.
- Never introduce a class, structure field, or side condition whose statement does not mention the object it is about. The cautionary case is `HasDivFunctor`: its field asserted only that a presheaf category is nonempty, the curve did not occur, and the blueprint advertised it as the existence of the divisor functor with `\leanok`. It survived because nobody read the statement.
- Never discharge an obligation by projecting the hypothesis you assumed. `choose_spec.1` of your own binder is `P → P`.
- A green build is not evidence of non-vacuity, and `lean_multi_attempt` reports every snippet as closing the goal when the file's imports are stale. Check imports before believing a probe.
- Do not restate an obligation more weakly to make a count go down. If you cannot close it, leave it open and say why.

ONE SHARED LEDGER, ten writers. Another lane's integrate sweep can commit your half-written file before you have measured it once — write risky proofs as explicit `sorry` first, measure, then fill. Stage explicit files, never `add -A`. Commit at every coherent point; an interrupted lane loses only what was uncommitted. Follow the `lean-check` LSP loop for edits and keep `lake build` for the session boundary — nine other lanes want the build lock too.

WHERE THIS PROJECT ACTUALLY STANDS, so you do not rediscover it. AJCR is the architecturally sound one. `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` (`Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161`) and `mixedParamRepresentableBy` (`Picard/Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree.lean:125`) are genuinely sorry-free and kernel-confirmed on `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]` — honest, non-circular implications that WOULD produce a real representing scheme. The problem is that all three antecedents are undischarged, with no sorry-free witness for any: `IsChartUniv`, Zariski-local surjectivity of `Sigma.desc f`, and `rep i`. A correct machine with nothing to feed it.

That makes your choice unusually concrete: pick whichever of the three missing inputs you judge closest, or the leaf that most directly produces one. Do not treat the sorry count as the map — the 17 body sorries are 15 in `Challenge.lean` (the statement-only headline file, so those ARE the north star, not debt) and 2 in `Pic0ThetaCocycle.lean`. The real work is antecedents that no sorry marks.

The board under `AJCR.w4-rep` (51/74 done) has a deep tail worth reading with suspicion: under `datum.dat-d.ddr.certificate`, four siblings are `rejected` (`cert-relocalize`, `joint-cover`, `leak-image`, `tube-fibre`) and one is `blocked` (`away-kerspan`). Four rejections clustered under one parent usually means the parent's formulation is wrong, not that four different approaches each independently failed. The reviewer is determining which; read its finding before you spend a session inside that tail. Other open items to weigh: `datum.dat-b` (coverage + injectivity — every pic^0 point is hit), `datum.dat-c.c9-chartlocus` and its `chart-u` child (the co-signed chartLocus and its openness — the sole gate of dat-b B-6 AND the whole dat-glue), `datum.dat-d.ddr.divrep.u2` (the DDR9-U epsilon-identity at the universal point), `datum.dat-glue` (the 01JJ RepresentableBy assembly), `datum.dat-j`, `datum.dat-g`, `w4-rep.build-reach` (93 of 620 modules unrooted, so the axiom probe does not see them — a file nobody imports is a file nobody has measured, which may matter to whichever "sorry-free" claim you are relying on).

Costings in this project have been wrong before, in the expensive direction: a handoff demanded a new structure field where the localization lemma it asked for was already in the file. So for whatever leaf you pick, read its actual Lean hypothesis before accepting its stated price. An over-priced leaf is where you win this round.

The sibling project Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge is readable and `horizon search` spans both. comments.body:
Round 6: reframed the certificate obligation and removed a whole class of attempted routes, with everything kernel-checked (lake env lean per file; full lake build green, 9071 jobs).

1. TESTED THE OBVIOUS ESCAPE AND PROVED IT BOUNDED. The pointwise gate accepts any adaptation, so one
can choose a SUPPORT-SEPARATED one; that really does trivialize the hard part (the Cech difference
becomes literally zero, so both flat-cokernel clauses AND the kernel-spanning hypothesis are free --
isCertified_of_separated). But the premise is essentially always false, now a theorem:
supportLocus_disjoint_chart_inter_of_separated. Both pinned charts carry a partition of unity, so a
support point of V0 cap V1 lies in a piece of EACH chart. Separation therefore holds only for divisors
confined to the two vertical fibres of pi. Also refuted the specific shape the tube-fibre leaf was
chasing (not_exists_unique_support_piece).

2. IDENTIFIED THE REAL CONDITION. Proved both directions that the assembler's per-piece no-leak clause
IS the Z-clopen principle of I-0209: the piece trace is always open in the support, so leak-freeness is
exactly clopen-ness of the trace in the divisor scheme. This explains why several sessions of fibre
analysis never closed it -- the clause is not fibrewise.

3. BUILT THE MISSING BRICK'S ALGEBRAIC CORE. Cutting by an idempotent yields a direct summand
(multiplication by e is a linear section), so the quotient inherits projectivity AND flatness with no
finiteness input. The flat version is the one that applies, since piece section rings are known flat
(not projective) over R. Assembled the chain: clopen trace => no-leak => Module.Finite colength, plus
landed fibrewise regularity => the entire (c1) input, with no fibre containment and no Cech-cokernel
flatness.

4. FOUND AND FIXED A BUILD GAP: the five DivSchemeCertZar* files from this run's earlier sessions were
unreachable from the root module, so plain  had never elaborated any of them. One import

RUN 0048 ROUND 0 — the certificate lane's satisfiability question is answered, in Lean.

THREE THEOREMS (commits 49866bdd1, 206967379, 40f357de8; three new files in the default build, all kernel-checked warning-free by lake env lean):
1. The assembler's per-piece hnoLeak clause FORCES the chart traces supportLocus cap V_b to be closed in the relative curve — a statement with no adaptation and no pieces in it. Because a FinCoverData has a partition of unity on EACH pinned chart, the union of a chart's piece traces IS the chart trace, and a finite union of closed sets is closed. So refining the cover provably cannot help, and shrinking the base only restates the condition over the smaller base.
2. 'Swallow or miss' (every piece contains the whole support or misses it) produces hnoLeak and clause (c1) with no fibre, tube or idempotent; a missing piece has a UNIT equation so its colength vanishes outright.
3. THE VERDICT: leak-freeness makes each piece trace clopen in the support, so a CONNECTED divisor with a leak-free adaptation satisfies supportLocus subset V_0 or supportLocus subset V_1. IsCertified is therefore satisfiable for a connected divisor only if the divisor avoids pi^-1(0) or pi^-1(infinity) — and base localization cannot repair it, since it does not disconnect the divisor (Spec R[x]/(x^2-t) over k[t] is connected over every basic open).

WHAT THIS CHANGES. Seven rounds were spent proving hypotheses of an interface whose satisfiability had never been checked, for the adaptation (exists_divisorAdaptation ...).some — about which nothing is known. The obligation is now one design question: does the Z(diamond) chart confine its divisors to a single pinned chart? spec-dd-r.md ADDENDUM 1 item 2 asserts it does ('honestly certified over each Z-chart ring') but never proved it. If yes, the rest is bookkeeping via ofAnchors and the Cech complex collapses, retiring the hinj wall (hinj IS clause (c4)) rather than solving it. If no, the atlas needs a carve, or IsCertified/DivFamZar must be redesigned — a functor blind to chart-crossing divisors is not the divisor functor.

Roadmap re-based: chart-trace DONE; tube-fibre, leak-image REJECTED; away-assemble DONE as written; away-kerspan BLOCKED (likely an artifact); new chart-avoid (urgent), swallow-adapt, cert-collapse (urgent), cert-assemble. tasks.objective:
You are the REVIEWER lane for Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge. Four prover lanes (`ajc-p1`..`ajc-p4`) work this project in parallel this round, each picking its own target. Your job is the thing none of them will do: judge whether the project's ROUTE to Picard representability is sound, whether its files and roadmap are organised so four lanes can work without tripping, and whether its Lean is of a quality that will still hold in a month. Read protection item `I-0838` first — it is the claim protocol, and you are its enforcer.

You are READ-MOSTLY on Lean source. You may edit: the roadmap, the inbox, hgraph nodes, docstrings that state something false, and blueprint prose. You may NOT take proof work off the provers — if you find a proof worth doing, propose it to the lane whose rank fits (`inbox add --kind hint --to task:ajc-pN`).

START WITH THE BOARD, because it is known-wrong. An audit on 2026-07-29 found `AJC.picrep` marked `done` while its advertised deliverable `instHasPicScheme` exists in no `.lean` file — it was deleted on 2026-07-28 under decision `I-0491`, not discharged. The roadmap's cited anchor `FGAPicRepresentability.lean:259` points mid-docstring. `AJC.jacobian.assembly` returned NONEXISTENT on two independent lenses. Three parent/child status warnings are live (`AJC.picrep` done with `AJC.picrep.tensor` open; `AJC.rr` done with `AJC.rr.extuniform` open; `AJC.jacobian.assembly` all-children-done but itself open). Verify each of these yourself rather than trusting my summary, then fix the board so the four provers plan against reality: correct statuses, re-point stale anchors, and write a summary on `AJC.picrep` that names the actual open obligation. Do this in your FIRST hour — the provers are reading the board to choose their targets, and every minute it lies costs four lanes.

THE ROUTE QUESTION, which is the real one. The whole AJC Jacobian tower rests on ONE bare `sorry`: `fgaPicardRepresentability` at `AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean:347`. Its own docstring says discharging it means formalising Kleiman §4 — the Abel-map slice `Div^d → Pic^d` as a smooth proper equivalence relation whose quotient is a scheme, plus `Div` representability via the Quot scheme — and that neither input is available. Meanwhile `AJC.picrep.quot` and `AJC.picrep.serre` are both marked `rejected`. So: the file says the route needs Quot and Serre finiteness, and the board says both are rejected. Resolve that. Either there is a different route (and the docstring is stale and should say so), or the route is the rejected one (and rejecting it while keeping the sorry is incoherent). This is the single most valuable thing you can determine this round, and no prover lane will determine it, because each of them is inside one leaf.

Then audit for the failure modes the 2026-07-29 pass found, in the parts of the project the provers are NOT looking at:
- VACUITY. `HasDivFunctor` asserted only that a presheaf category `(Over (Spec k))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (u+1)` is nonempty — `C` did not occur in the statement — and the blueprint advertised it as "the existence of the relative divisor functor" with `\leanok`. Find the others. Read the STATEMENT of every class, structure field, and gate on the representability seam and ask what would falsify it. A hypothesis that nothing can falsify is a hole with a docstring.
- SELF-PROJECTION. `smoothProperQuotient` proves `P.IsRepresentable → P.IsRepresentable`, with all four Kleiman hypotheses unused, zero instances, and zero call sites. `instPicSharpRepresentable` and `instPicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType` are `choose_spec.1` / `.2.1` of the hypothesis they assume. These are not defects to fix by proving something — they are defects to LABEL, so no consumer is written against them and no blueprint node claims them.
- DEAD CONSUMERS. Roughly 45 declarations take `[HasPicScheme C]`. If that class has no instance, all 45 are about no curve. Count them, check whether `HasPicSchemeEt` (which does have an unconditional producer, `instHasPicSchemeEt`, itself a projection of the line-347 sorry) has actually replaced it, and report how much of the project is downstream of an uninhabited class. That number is the honest state of AJC, and someone should write it down.
- ORGANISATION. `Picard/QuotScheme.lean` is over 6000 lines. `AlgebraicJacobian` has 24 body-position sorries and 172 modules, 66 still on a bare `import Mathlib`. Say which of these actually costs the provers time this round and which is cosmetic; do not file a refactor that buys nothing.

WHAT TO PRODUCE. Not a report for me to read — changes the four provers will hit. A corrected board. An inbox `issue` per genuine defect, naming declaration and file. A direct hint to each prover lane whose target your findings change. Where you find a vacuous or self-projecting declaration, put the finding on its hgraph node and in its docstring, so the next reader cannot miss it. If your route analysis concludes AJC's representability is not reachable this round by any of the four lanes, say that plainly to `--to human` with the reasoning — that is a valuable finding, not a failure, and I would rather know it than have four lanes spend a day proving lemmas into a dead route.

Use `ground` and `work-reviewer` subagents freely for independent lenses; they are yours, and this task is exactly what they are for. Commit your board and prose changes as you go.

tasks.objective:
You are the REVIEWER lane for Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild. Four prover lanes (`ajcr-p1`..`ajcr-p4`) work this project in parallel this round, each picking its own target. Your job is the thing none of them will do: judge whether the project's ROUTE to Pic^0 representability is sound, whether its roadmap and files are organised so four lanes can work without tripping, and whether its Lean will still hold in a month. Read protection item `I-0838` first — it is the claim protocol, and you are its enforcer.

You are READ-MOSTLY on Lean source. You may edit: the roadmap, the inbox, hgraph nodes, docstrings that state something false, and blueprint/worksheet prose. You may NOT take proof work off the provers — if you find a proof worth doing, propose it to the lane whose rank fits (`inbox add --kind hint --to task:ajcr-pN`).

THE GOOD NEWS AND THE PROBLEM, both established by the 2026-07-29 audit. AJCR is the architecturally sound project: `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` (`Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161`) and `mixedParamRepresentableBy` (`Picard/Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree.lean:125`) are genuinely sorry-free, kernel-confirmed on `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`, honest non-circular implications that WOULD produce a real representing scheme. The problem is that all three antecedents are undischarged — `IsChartUniv`, Zariski-local surjectivity of `Sigma.desc f`, and `rep i` — and not one sorry-free witness exists for any of them. A correct machine with nothing to feed it.

So your central question is a costing question, not a correctness question: **of the three missing inputs, which is actually closest, and is the roadmap's ranking of them right?** The `AJCR.w4-rep` subtree has 74 leaves with 51 done and a five-to-seven-deep tail under `datum.dat-d.ddr.certificate` where several siblings are `rejected` (`cert-relocalize`, `joint-cover`, `leak-image`, `tube-fibre`) and one is `blocked` (`away-kerspan`). Four rejections and a block clustered under one parent is a signal: either the parent's formulation is wrong and each rejection is a symptom, or the rejections are correct and the parent should be restated. Determine which. That is worth more than any single leaf, and no prover will see it because each is inside one leaf.

Then, specifically, audit the PRESCRIPTIONS. This project's leaves carry costings written by earlier sessions — "this gap needs bricks X and Y", "needs a new structure field", "CERT-Σ-gated". Those costings set the price for every later round and nothing re-checks them. There is a documented case in this workspace of a handoff demanding a new structure field where the localization lemma it asked for was already in the file. So: for each of `dat-b`, `dat-c.c9-chartlocus`, `dat-d.ddr.divrep.u2`, and `dat-glue`, read the actual Lean hypothesis rather than the prose about it, and check whether the stated prerequisite is real. Report any leaf whose price is wrong in either direction — over-priced leaves are where a prover lane can win this round.

Also check for the failure modes the audit found across the workspace:
- VACUITY. Read the STATEMENT of every gate class and structure field on the chart/certificate seam and ask what would falsify it. The cautionary case is AJC's `HasDivFunctor`, whose field asserted only that a presheaf category is nonempty — the curve did not occur in the statement — while the blueprint advertised it as the existence of the divisor functor. AJCR's audit came back cleaner than AJC's, but "cleaner" is not "clean", and the deep `certificate` tail is where a quietly-vacuous side condition would survive longest.
- HYPOTHESIS DRIFT. 12 of the 101 audited claims proved something adjacent to what their name and docstring said. On this seam that means a lemma about `IsChartUniv` at *some* open where the consumer needs it at the chart locus, or a certificate clause quantified over the wrong family. Check that each chart-side lemma's conclusion is the one `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` actually consumes — price the consumer's carrier, not the object in isolation.
- BUILD REACHABILITY. 93 of 620 modules are unrooted (`AJCR.w4-rep.build-reach`), so an axiom probe does not see them. Establish whether that is still true and whether it invalidates any "sorry-free" claim on this seam. A file nobody imports is a file nobody has measured.
- The 17 sorries here sit in `Challenge.lean` (15) and `Pic0ThetaCocycle.lean` (2). `Challenge.lean` is the statement-only headline file, so its sorries are the north star, not debt. Make sure the board reflects that distinction — a naive sorry count reads AJCR as nearly done, and that is how the last round got misread.

WHAT TO PRODUCE. Not a report for me — changes the four provers will hit. A roadmap whose ranking under `w4-rep` reflects real cost, with the rejection cluster either restated or explained. An inbox `issue` per defect naming declaration and file. A direct hint to each prover whose target your costing changes. Findings on the hgraph node of the declaration they concern. If you conclude the three antecedents are all multi-round and none closes this week, say so to `--to human` with the reasoning — I would rather know than have four lanes each report partial progress on a leaf.

Use `ground` and `work-reviewer` subagents freely for independent lenses. Commit your board and prose changes as you go.

v4.31.0 migration fix patterns (Cech + GR push-pull/pullback proofs)

Effective repairs for the **v4.31.0 defeq-transparency-wall** breaks in these projects:

- **Port from the AJC copy first.** `MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/.../<same file>` is often already sorry-free (e.g. `PresheafCech.lean`, `CechSectionIdentificationBase.lean`). `diff` the subproject vs AJC; if they differ only in the sorry regions, copy the AJC file wholesale.
- **`set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in`** before a lemma fixes most "type mismatch under instances transparency" / stuck defeq. **Placement matters**: it must go BEFORE the docstring `/-- … -/`, never between docstring and `lemma` (that is a parse error: "unexpected token 'set_option'; expected 'lemma'"). Stacks with `set_option maxHeartbeats N in`.
- **`erw [Category.comp_id]` / `erw [Category.id_comp]`** closes residual `A ≫ 𝟙 = A` / `𝟙 ≫ A = A` when the `𝟙`'s object is only defeq (e.g. `(𝟭).obj M` vs `M`, or a `⋙`-form) so `simp`/`exact Category.comp_id _` fail. `erw` matches through the wall then auto-`rfl`.
- **`rw [reassoc_of% h1, reassoc_of% h2]` ordering**: cancel the INNER hom≫inv pair first so the outer pair becomes adjacent.
- **`subst h; simp <;> rfl`** for eqToHom-transport lemmas whose two sides reduce to defeq-but-not-syntactic `map = map`.
- **LSP is dead** on these full-`import Mathlib` files (server crashes / broken pipe). Iterate with `lake build <module>` and read the printed unsolved-goal state from the error output. `GlueDescent` ≈ 2.6 min/build; `CechHigherDirectImage` ≈ 8.5 min/build.

**Session 0015-horizon-T4 — diagnosis + 1 of 8 errors fixed.**

Fixed **error 1546** (`W_isMonoidal.whiskerLeft`): the v4.31 braiding-naturality form changed. Replaced `by simp [BraidedCategory.braiding_naturality_right]` with `by exact (BraidedCategory.braiding_naturality_right Z g).symm` — the exact fix the AJC copy already uses. Rebuild confirms 1546 gone, no regressions.

**Remaining 7 errors (`lake build AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.SectionGradedRing`, ~1 min/build, deps cached):** `1664` (`rfl`), `1704` (term-mode `Category.assoc` type mismatch), `1888`/`1935`/`2640` (`rw` pattern-not-found), `3173`/`3840` (instance synth).

**Single root cause identified:** v4.31 made `TopCat.Sheaf C X` a *semireducible `def`* (`:= Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) C`, `deriving Category`) that no longer reduces under `instances` transparency. So every `X.ringCatSheaf.obj`-threaded goal in the monoidal-bridge lemmas becomes **ill-typed at `instances` transparency** (error note: `X.ringCatSheaf : TopCat.Sheaf RingCat` vs expected `ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory (Presheaf.IsSheaf …)`). This blocks (a) the `dsimp only [whiskerLeftIso_hom, whiskerRightIso_hom, tensorIso_hom]` reductions (leaving `⊗ᵢ`/`◁ᵢ`/`▷ᵢ` iso-forms un-reduced, so the follow-up `rw [← hwnat]` cannot match `F ◁ e.hom`), and (b) `rw` motive type-checking.

**Ruled out (mechanical fixes insufficient — tested this session):**
- `set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in` on `tensorObjUnitIso_eq`/`tensorBraiding_eq`/`tensorObjWhiskerLeftIso_eq`/`tensorObjWhiskerRightIso_eq` → **no effect** (errors identical). Note `tensorObjAssoc_eta_factor_sheaf` (2640) *already* has this option and still fails.
- `set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 8 in` on `tensorPowAdd_assoc`/`tensorPowAdd_comm` → **no effect** on 3173/3840.

**3173/3840 are cascades, not roots:** `3840` is `typeclass instance problem is stuck: Category ?m` (an unresolved metavar), and `3173` fails to synth `MonoidalCategory (LocalizedMonoidal …)` even though that same synthesis *succeeds* at the `monoidalCategory` def (line 1565). Both are downstream of the 5 sorry-typed bridge lemmas (`tensorObjIso`/`tensorObjAssoc`/`tensorPowAdd` args become entangled with metavars). **Fix the 5 bridge lemmas first → 3173/3840 should resolve.**

**Recommended next-session plan:** re-plumb `X.ringCatSheaf.obj` into the v4.31 sheaf API so goals are type-correct under `instances` transparency (the true migration). This needs interactive goal states — **LSP is dead on this full-`import Mathlib` file** (server crash), so iterate via `lake build <module>` reading printed goal state, or extract minimal reproductions into a small-import scratch file to regain LSP. The full goal states for all 7 errors are in the session log.

comments.author: horizon
comments.body:
**T8 session: root cause sharpened, 1 of 9 errors fixed, repair recipe validated.**

Fresh 61s build of GR `SectionGradedRing.lean` shows **9 errors (I-0006 line list is stale)**: `1666` rfl, `1707` congr-fallout, `1892`/`1940`/`2646` rw-pattern-not-found, `3147`/`3179` no-goals, `3180`/`3833` whnf timeouts. The `LocalizedMonoidal` synth failure is GONE.

**Root cause (deeper than the monoidal API):**
- `TopCat.Sheaf` is a semireducible `def` (`Topology/Sheaves/Sheaf.lean:108`) over the *reducible* `CategoryTheory.Sheaf` abbrev, and Mathlib's own `Scheme.PresheafOfModules` abbrev embeds `X.ringCatSheaf.obj` (a `FullSubcategory` field projection) through it — so **every goal in this file is type-incorrect at `instances` transparency**.
- v4.31 `simp`/`dsimp`/`rw`/`erw` congruence then refuses to descend into subterms: `dsimp only [Iso.trans_hom, tensorIso_hom]` silently no-ops and keyed matching never sees the `⊗ₘ`/`◁` heads under `(… ≪≫ …).hom`. `respectTransparency false` does NOT help (it relaxes defeq, not the congruence type-check).
- Also the transported `⊗ₘ` (lifted bifunctor on the `LocalizedMonoidal` type synonym) is no longer defeq to the whisker composite in the `tensorHom_def'` orientation — the old `rfl` closers relied on that.

**Validated recipe (`tensorObjUnitIso_eq` now FIXED in-file, 9 → 8):**
1. `show <goal with the defeq head exposed, e.g. (f ⊗ₘ g) ≫ …> = _` — `show` checks at default transparency and bridges what dsimp cannot;
2. plain top-level `rw [MonoidalCategory.tensorHom_def']` (top-level rw still works — only subterm congruence is dead);
3. `simp only [Category.assoc]; rfl` (`rfl` absorbs `𝟙_ X.Modules ≡ unitModule X`).

**Remaining 8 sites are mechanical but verbose** (each `show` must spell the full goal), plus 2 whnf timeouts of unknown depth — sized for the dedicated GRQ.graded session Ground proposed; not forced in T8.

Recipes: closing GeometricallyReduced / GeometricallyIrreducible scaffold sorries (v4.31 Mathlib has the full API)

Mathlib v4.31 ships `AlgebraicGeometry/Geometrically/{Basic,Reduced,Irreducible}.lean` — these scaffold instances are now provable, not gaps. Proven patterns (see `Points.lean` `gm_geometricallyReduced`, `ChartIso.lean` `projectiveLineBar_geomIrred`, both axiom-clean):

- **Affine case** (`Spec A ⟶ Spec k̄`): `rw [geometricallyReduced_iff / geometricallyIrreducible_iff]`, intro the `IsPullback`, `obtain ⟨φ, rfl⟩ := Spec.map_surjective y; algebraize [φ.hom]`, then `h.isoPullback ≪≫ pullbackSpecIso k̄ A K` reduces to `IsReduced/IsDomain (A ⊗[k̄] K)`. Needs `set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in` (the `(Gm k̄).hom`-to-`Spec.map` defeq).
- **Ring step for localizations**: `IsReduced (Localization.Away t ⊗[k̄] K)` via `Algebra.TensorProduct.cancelBaseChange k̄ P P _ K` (`≅ Loc ⊗[P] (P ⊗[k̄] K)`), instance `IsLocalization.tensor`, and `isReduced_localizationPreserves` (apply with `by exact` + explicit S — beta-reduction quirk). `MvPolynomial.algebraTensorAlgEquiv` + `Algebra.TensorProduct.comm` give `P ⊗[k̄] K ≅ MvPolynomial σ K`.
- **Proj / non-affine case** (ℙ¹): cover the base change by pulled-back chart opens. Per chart: `Proj.awayι_toSpecZero_assoc` + `← Spec.map_comp` + `change` collapses `awayι ≫ hom` to `Spec.map (algebraMap k̄ (Away 𝒜 (X i)))`, then the affine recipe. Covering: `Proj.iSup_basicOpen_eq_top` with the (now named) `projectiveLineBarAffineCover_span`. Intersection: any preimage of the generic point `⟨⊥, Ideal.isPrime_bot, …⟩` under `pullback.fst` (surjective — `Surjective` is `IsStableUnderBaseChange`, `MorphismProperty.pullback_fst`). Assemble with the new `irreducibleSpace_of_two_irreducible_opens` (ChartIso).
- **Traps**: inside `namespace AlgebraicGeometry`, ring-level `IsReduced` must be `_root_.IsReduced`; `⊗[k̄]` notation needs `open scoped TensorProduct in` BEFORE the docstring; avoid `ObjectProperty.prop_of_iso _` (leaves an unsynthesizable eta-expanded `IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms` goal — use `isReduced_of_isOpenImmersion (iso).hom` or `.homeomorph.irreducibleSpace_iff` instead); the affine cover's `I₀`/`𝒰.f i` are semireducibly opaque — work with `Proj.awayι (X i)` + `fin_cases` normalization (`projectiveLineBar_smooth_chart_aux` idiom) rather than cover indices.

**Recipe: ValuativeCommSq for rational-map extension (Milne 3.1 codim-≥2 CLOSED); over-k̄ hypothesis is required.**

`indeterminacy_codimGe2_of_smooth_of_complete` (Albanese `CodimOneExtension.lean`) is proved axiom-clean — Mathlib v4.31 has ALL the plumbing; do not hand-roll rational-map/valuative machinery. Reusable recipe:

- **Pipeline**: `f.fromFunctionField : Spec K(X) ⟶ Y` + Mathlib `IsFractionRing (stalk z) K(X)` (integral schemes) + DVR stalk ⇒ `ValuativeCommSq Y.hom`; extract the lift from `IsProper.eq_valuativeCriterion` (`rw at hP; exact hP.1.1.1`); spread out with `PartialMap.ofFromSpecStalk X.hom Y.hom L hfacr` (`[X.IsGermInjectiveAt z]` automatic for integral) + `mem_domain_ofFromSpecStalk`; identify with `f` via `RationalMap.eq_of_fromFunctionField_eq` + a small glue lemma `fromFunctionField = Spec.map (stalkSpecializes gen⤳z) ≫ fromSpecStalkOfMem` (prove by `cancel_mono g.domain.ι` + `Opens.fromSpecStalkOfMem_ι` + `SpecMap_stalkSpecializes_fromSpecStalk`).
- `CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (stalk z) functionField) = stalkSpecializes ((genericPoint_spec X).specializes trivial)` is **rfl** (`stalkFunctionFieldAlgebra` def) — exploit by defeq (`exact`), do NOT `rw` (higher-order pattern fails).
- **Structure-literal trap**: inside a `ValuativeCommSq { ... }` literal the stalk term gets unfolded past `Scheme.presheaf`, so keyed instances (`IsDomain (stalk z)`, `Field functionField`, `IsFractionRing`, `stalkFunctionFieldAlgebra`) STOP firing. Materialise them OUTSIDE the literal and pass as explicit fields (`domain := hdom` etc.).
- **Field-poisoning trap**: bind those facts with plain `have`/`let`, NEVER `haveI/letI` — an opaque local `Field functionField` fvar shadows the CommRing path and makes `Algebra (stalk z) K(X)` unsynthesizable. Also needs `set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in` BEFORE the docstring (IsField.toField / CommRingCat.of-eta walls).
- **Over-k̄ is mathematically necessary**: the valuative square's base compatibility needs `hf : f.compHom Y.hom = X.hom.toRationalMap` (Milne's maps are k̄-maps). The whole Thm-3.2 chain now threads this hypothesis; future consumers must supply it (for maps built from k̄-morphisms it follows via `Hom.toRationalMap`/`compHom_toRationalMap`). Push it to the function field via `exists_rep` + `compHom_toRationalMap` + simp with `fromSpecStalkOfMem_compHom/toPartialMap`.
- Coheight conventions: scheme points carry `specializationPreorder` (Mathlib instance, `x ≤ y ↔ y ⤳ x`); coheight 0 ⇔ `IsMax` (`Order.coheight_eq_zero`) ⇒ generic point via `Specializes.antisymm ...|>.eq`; `ENat.lt_two_iff` for the ≤1 split.
- Remaining CodimOneExtension gaps are NOT valuative: Stacks 0AVF (depth-≥2 H¹, Milne 3.1 Step 2) and Milne 3.3 difference-map machinery.

**`pullback_preservesFiniteLimits` (FBC leaf, `CechHigherDirectImageUnconditional.lean:186`) is NOT a cheap adjointness win — Ground's recommendation had the variance backwards. Route analysis (session 0013), do not re-derive.**

- The recommendation claimed "flat `g^*` is a left adjoint, so left-exactness follows from adjointness" — **false**: left adjoints preserve COLIMITS. Left-exactness of flat pullback is genuine flatness content, checked on stalks.
- No dodge exists at the presheaf level: `PresheafOfModules.pullback` is a bare `leftAdjoint` with no pointwise description; the sections-level formula `colim_{U ⊇ g(U')} M(U) ⊗_{O(U)} O(U')` is only RIGHT-exact (the ring maps are not flat — flatness lives on stalks). Sheafification + `SheafOfModules.forget` both preserve finite limits (Mathlib), so the irreducible core really is stalk-level.
- **Viable honest route** (est. 400–800 LOC of new infra): (1) combinators exist — `Functor.preservesFiniteLimits_tfae` / `preservesFiniteLimits_of_preservesKernels` (`Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/ShortComplex/ExactFunctor.lean`); (2) Mathlib 2026 has module structure on stalks (`Mathlib/Algebra/Category/ModuleCat/Stalk.lean`, `PresheafOfModules.germ_smul`) and stalk⊣skyscraper at plain-category level (`Topology/Sheaves/Skyscraper.lean`), plus `mono_iff_stalk_mono`/`isIso_iff_stalkFunctor_map_iso` (`Topology/Sheaves/Stalks.lean`); (3) the missing brick is **stalk-of-pullback**: `stalkModule_x ∘ pullback g ≅ extendScalars(stalkMap) ∘ stalkModule_{g x}` — provable by adjoint uniqueness IF a module-level skyscraper right adjoint is built (pushforward of skyscraper = skyscraper at the image); then flat stalk maps (`AlgebraicGeometry.Flat.iff_flat_stalkMap`-adjacent, `RingHom.Flat` appLE definition) + `ModuleCat.preservesFiniteLimits_extendScalars_of_flat` (`ModuleCat/Descent.lean`) finish via kernel-comparison-on-stalks.
- **Cheaper architectural alternative** if the instance stays stuck: the only consumer is `pullback_mapHC_homologyIso` at line 1545 (`cech_flatBaseChange`, affine S/S'), applied to the Čech complex whose terms are iso to tildes — a complex-specific homology-commutation via `tilde`-exactness (`TildeExactness.lean`) + `pullback_spec_tilde_iso` could replace the general instance, at the cost of a termwise-tilde chain-iso.

pullback_preservesFiniteLimits: prove via flat extendScalars, NOT adjointness

`pullback_preservesFiniteLimits` (`CechHigherDirectImageUnconditional.lean:193`, instance, `[Flat g]`) is a **true** statement but a genuine open `sorry` — do not attempt a cheap adjointness proof.

- The statement is sound: module pullback $g^*$ = inverse image $g^{-1}$ (exact) followed by $-\otimes_{\mathcal O_S}\mathcal O_{S'}$, which is left-exact **because** `[Flat g]`. Finite limits are preserved.
- The trap: `g^*` is a **left adjoint**, so it preserves colimits / is right-exact — that gives you nothing for finite *limits*. "Left adjoint $\Rightarrow$ left-exact" is backwards. The flatness hypothesis is doing all the work and must be used.
- Intended route (per the leaf's own docstring): transfer along `SheafOfModules.pullbackIso`, discharge `forget`/`sheafification` (already limit-preserving in Mathlib), reduce to `ModuleCat.preservesFiniteLimits_extendScalars_of_flat` stalkwise. Reference Stacks 02KH.
- Note it is a global `instance` carrying a sorry; `pullback_preservesHomology` (line 197) derives from it by `inferInstance`, so the whole flat-homology chain rests on this node.

v4.31 recipes round 3 (MR0555258 migration): convert descends deeper, Type-hom funext wall, structInst binder-field parse quirk

New patterns from migrating `MR0555258/Basic.lean` v4.30→v4.31 (all verified green, complement the existing v4.31 memories):

- **`convert h using N` descends one level deeper in v4.31**: proofs shaped `convert h using 4; exact congrArg f e` break with a type-mismatch whose 'expected' is the *argument-level* equality. Fix: keep `convert h using 4` but supply the **inner** bridge directly and mop defeq side goals: `convert h using 4 <;> first | rfl | exact e` (drop the outer `congrArg`). Extra side goals are object/category equalities closed by `rfl`.
- **Type-category hom equality: `funext`/`apply funext` does NOT unify** with `f ≫ g = h ≫ i` even under `respectTransparency false`. Mathlib's own idiom (see `FullyFaithful.homNatIso`): `fun f => by ext g; exact hF.map_injective (by simp)`. If simp stalls on `hG.homEquiv.symm` (v4.31 displays via `ConcreteCategory.hom ... .toFun`), run `simp` first, then `show`-restate with `hG.preimage` (defeq to `homEquiv.symm`), then `simp` (fires `map_preimage`).
- **StructInst binder-style field + comma**: `{ app V := e, naturality := ... }` fails to parse ('unexpected identifier; expected }'). Use lambda + newline-separated fields: `{ app := fun V => e\n  naturality := ... }`.
- **`Scheme.Hom.appIso_inv_naturality` exists in v4.31 Mathlib** — exact match for presheaf-map-vs-appIso.inv naturality squares of open immersions; no hand proof needed.
- **`lake update` with a dep pinned to `main` (doc-gen4) silently bumps `lean-toolchain`** (to v4.32.0-rc1 here) and then the mathlib cache refuses to fetch. Pin doc-gen4 to `0bc516c1b9db` (the AJC rev) and rewrite `lean-toolchain` back before re-running.

**Ops (run 0009 session 0013): idle-box build speed, `horizon commit` gotchas, zombie sessions.**

- **Build costs are LOAD artifacts, not constants.** At load ~0.07 (16 cores idle): `lake env lean` on the 1861-line `CechHigherDirectImageUnconditional.lean` = **33 s**; incremental full `lake build` (8642 jobs) ≈ 1 min. The 'hours per build' memories (LegMid1 5h40m etc.) were load-65 measurements. Check `uptime` before budgeting builds.
- **`horizon commit` fails with an EMPTY error** in two cases: (a) no git identity — export `GIT_COMMITTER_NAME='Archon Horizon' GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL='archon-horizon@local'` (+ AUTHOR pair) first; (b) nothing to commit — the workspace ledger's end-of-run sweep (`workspace[NNNN] run finished`) may have already integrated files you think are stranded. Diagnose with `git --git-dir=.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git --work-tree=. diff HEAD --stat -- <project-path>`. Per-project journals under `.archon-horizon/vcs/<project>.git` can lag several runs behind — that's the orchestrator's job.
- **Zombie Horizon sessions are real**: the harness can reconcile and launch a successor while the previous session's `claude` process (reparented to init, transcript flush frozen) is STILL editing files and launching builds in the same project. At session start check `pgrep -af claude` + parent PIDs; terminate a same-project claude whose horizon runner is dead, but read its transcript tail first and inherit its pending intent (session 0011's uncommitted surgery was sound and became the session's main result).

local_inbox.body:
Recipe: building ModuleCat-R morphisms into sheaf-of-modules section objects (v4.31) — the ConcreteCategory.ofHom + presheaf-obj pattern, and the let-fvar IsIso gotcha

Landed in `tildeIso_of_isQuasicoherent_isAffineOpen` (`QuotScheme.lean`, T12 run 0010). When you need `f : ModuleCat.of R M ⟶ <sections object>` (e.g. to feed `tilde.map`):

- **Target the honest `ModuleCat R` object** `(modulesSpecToSheaf.obj G).presheaf.obj (Opposite.op ⊤)` — this is literally the domain module of Mathlib's `fromTildeΓ`/`toOpen`. Do NOT target `moduleSpecΓFunctor.obj G` via `ModuleCat.ofHom`/`→ₗ` type ascriptions: elaboration whnf-unfolds the carrier past `restrictScalars`, and `Module R <unfolded carrier>` synthesis then fails (no refold; a letI at the folded form does not match either).
- **Construct via `ConcreteCategory.ofHom { toFun := ..., map_add' := ..., map_smul' := ... }`** with the expected hom type ascribed — the instances come from the objects via the `(· →ₗ[R] ·)` FC family, no synthesis. A bare `let blin : M →ₗ[R] <object> := ...` fails; skipping the standalone LinearMap and going straight to the categorical hom works.
- **map_smul' across compHom-vs-restrictScalars actions**: `change` the goal to the native-action form `(ΓSpecIso R).inv.hom r • f x`, then `rw [← hact]; exact h1` where `hact : appLE V ⊤ e = (ΓSpecIso R).inv` (proved by `rw [Scheme.Hom.appLE, fromSpec_app_self, Category.assoc, ← Functor.map_comp, ← op_comp, Subsingleton.elim _ (𝟙 ⊤), op_id, map_id, comp_id]`).
- **IsIso of `tilde.map b'` for a `let`-bound b'**: `haveI : IsIso (tilde.map b') := by rw [show tilde.map b' = (tilde.functor _).map b' from rfl]; infer_instance` FAILS (zeta-expansion mismatch between goal and local instance). Use `inferInstanceAs (IsIso ((tilde.functor _).map b'))` — works even without `clear_value`.
- **Unit-component bijectivity at open immersions**: `Adjunction.unit_leftAdjointUniq_hom_app (restrictAdjunction j) (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction j) N` + `restrictAdjunction_unit_app_app` (plain presheaf restriction along `j''ᵁj⁻¹ᵁV = V`) + component of `restrictFunctorIsoPullback`. When `rw [← AddCommGrpCat.comp_apply]` fails with "target not type-correct under instances transparency" (`Γ((𝟭 X.Modules).obj N, V)` forms), do `change`-restatement at the type-correct form, then close with `exact congrArg (fun φ => (AddCommGrpCat.Hom.hom φ) y) hcomp` where `hcomp : f ≫ g = 𝟙 _` — both sides defeq, no rewriting in the wall.
- **Σ-pair trace**: `tilde.toOpen_map_app` (naturality) + `toOpen_fromTildeΓ_app` at `⊤` (+ `homOfLE le_top = 𝟙 ⊤` by `Subsingleton.elim`) give `(tilde.map b' ≫ fromTildeΓ).app ⊤ ∘ toOpen = b'` elementwise, via `congrArg`-chains only.

**Recipes: module-level dévissage in Lean v4.31 (landed in FlatteningStratification GenericFreeness, run 0010 T12 r2) — reuse for any prime-filtration/SES argument.**

- **ModuleCat SES arguments need ONE universe**: `ModuleCat.ofHom {X Y : Type v}` forces all modules of a `ShortComplex (ModuleCat R)` into the same universe. Binders `{M₁ M₂ M₃ : Type*}` give distinct universes and produce baffling failures — instance goals displayed as raw `Quot ⇑(OreLocalization.oreEqv ...)` (LocalizedModule unfolded past its instance heads) plus universe-mismatched `Eq.{max u_1 u_4}` vs `Eq.{max u_1 u_2}`. Pin `Type v`. The dévissage eliminator is single-universe anyway.
- **`set S := Submonoid.powers (f*g)` breaks instance unification** in localized-module types (same family as the known let-fvar IsIso gotcha): instance search will not zeta-unfold the set-fvar when unifying `Localization S'` heads. Write the submonoid term explicitly everywhere; `let`-bound MAPS (data) are fine — only types/instances mind.
- **Quantified-instance motive** for `IsNoetherianRing.induction_on_isQuotientEquivQuotientPrime` when the property lives over a DIFFERENT ring A than the induction ring B: `motive N _ iMB _ := ∀ (iA : Module A N), @IsScalarTower A B N Algebra.toSMul iMB.toDistribMulAction.toMulAction.toSMul iA.toDistribMulAction.toMulAction.toSMul → @P A N _ _ iA`. Cases: subsingleton via @-application; quotient case transports along `(e.restrictScalars A).symm` (canonical tower on B⧸p is instance-found); exact case builds `letI iA₁ := Module.compHom N₁ (algebraMap A B)` + tower `⟨fun a b n => by change (a • b) • n = algebraMap A B a • b • n; rw [Algebra.smul_def, mul_smul]⟩`; B-linear maps restrict via `LinearMap.restrictScalars A` and inj/surj/Exact transfer definitionally. Final application `... ‹Module A M› ‹IsScalarTower A B M›` unifies. Compiled essentially first-try.

**T12 r5: fourth false pinned statement found and repaired — finite-strata flattening statements need a noetherian base (`IsNoetherian`), not merely locally noetherian.**

- **The defect**: `flatLocusReduction`, `flatLocusAssembly`, `flatteningStratification`, `flatteningStratification_universal`, `.ofCurve` all hypothesised `[IsLocallyNoetherian S]` while concluding a *finite* flat stratification. Counterexample: on $S = \coprod_{n\ge 1}\mathbb A^n$ give component $n$ the coherent sheaf $\bigoplus_{k\le n}(i_{V_k})_*\mathcal O_{V_k}$ for a strictly nested flag $V_1\supset\cdots\supset V_n$; a flat locally-closed stratum through the generic point of $V_k$ cannot contain another level's generic point (local freeness forces relatively clopen intersection with each $V_j$, against the dense lower level), so component $n$ forces $\ge n+1$ strata and no finite family covers all components. Nitsure and the blueprint's main-theorem body correctly say **noetherian**; the lemma-node bodies and the Lean had drifted to locally noetherian.
- **Repair** (commit `f2e8a3c67c`): Lean hypotheses strengthened to `IsNoetherian` (Mathlib's loc-noeth + compact class); blueprint bodies of `lem:flat_locus_reduction_lean`, the assembly node and the universal node aligned; the counterexample recorded as a blueprint remark and in the `flatLocusReduction` docstring. The ℕ-indexed $n=0$ case (`flatLocusStratification`) is *correct* at locally noetherian (the fibre rank is the global countable index) and was left unchanged. All existing derivations (`flatteningStratification`/`flatLocusAssembly`/`ofCurve` from Lemma 6) recompile; `lake build` green.

**Concurrency incidents from the 2026-07-16 evening continuation wave (5 parallel lanes) — protocol fixes recommended**

1. **Shared-index commit race (SERIOUS, caused transient data loss in HEAD).** All lanes commit through one `workspace.git` index; G-D8's `6197c9676` interleaved with DAT-1's commits and recorded spurious DELETIONS of DAT-1's two freshly-committed files (862 lines vanished from HEAD; byte-identical restore in `a640fef5b`). **Recommended house protocol for concurrent lanes:** commit via a private index — `GIT_INDEX_FILE=$(mktemp)` + `read-tree HEAD` + add only your paths + `write-tree`/`commit-tree` + compare-and-swap `update-ref` (G-D8's final commit used exactly this and it was clean) — and always verify `git show --stat HEAD` afterward touches only intended paths.

2. **Stale mutex FILE deadlock.** An agent killed by the 15:18 session limit left `/tmp/claude-1001/ajcr-locks/lake.lock` as a 0-byte FILE; the documented mkdir acquire spins forever against a file, so every lane deadlocked at its build step until the human deleted it (~19:10). Recommendation: the acquire loop should detect a lock that is a plain FILE (protocol violation by definition — mkdir creates directories) and report it as stale immediately rather than waiting.

3. **/tmp quota outage (~19:00–19:20).** uid-1001 tmpfs quota exhaustion (EDQUOT) bricked every Bash call machine-wide, mid-build for several lanes; recovered after human cleanup. Watch /tmp usage when >3 lanes run concurrently.

4. **Foreign-workspace mutex abuse.** An OpenGA-Horizon (Evans) agent held the AJCR lock path for its own `lake cache get` for ~25 min. The AJCR mutex is for AJCR lake invocations only; cross-workspace squatting silently serializes our lanes against unrelated work.

Context: incidents observed and worked around by the five continuation lanes (DD-0, DAT-1, G-D8 closed; DAT-6, DD-F in flight); full details in the lane reports quoted in the respective commit messages.

Lean pattern: 'set x := e' + external lemma outputs = syntactic atom mismatch (omega/rw fail)

When a proof does 'set Fd := fiberWeilDivisor π' and then invokes external lemmas (rank_normalization etc.), the lemma outputs carry the UNFOLDED spelling while set-folded context carries Fd — defeq but syntactically distinct, so omega/rw silently lose hypotheses (they atomize by syntax). Robust fix used throughout DD-F's PFib.lean: wrap each external application in a 'have h : <set-spelled statement> := <application>' — the have coerces by defeq and downstream syntactic tools see consistent atoms. Also: CurveDivisor.deg_single only rw-matches the Finsupp.single spelling; bind it through a defeq 'have' at CurveDivisor.single first.

- **Repaired:** each collided name now has exactly **one** declaration site — `pointPullbackEquations` (`AlgebraicJacobian/RiemannRoch/DegreeIsoTransport.lean:288`), `pointPullbackUnit` (`:297`), `coe_pointPullbackUnit` (`:304`); `DegreePullback.lean` and `ClassDegMapIso.lean` only consume them. - **Workflow changed:** the memory is written against the multi-lane fleet model (same-wave lanes mirroring one model file, worksheet-assigned shared vocabulary, post-commit root build under a mutex). Runs `0043`-`0047` execute one horizon session per task per round; the two live runs sit on different projects and different root modules, so two lanes cannot coin the same name in the same environment.

The reachability half of that rule is now carried by the live `I-0324` (a bare `lake build` need not elaborate a new file; name the command that actually checked it).

THE Z-CLOPEN CERTIFICATE PRINCIPLE (DD-1/DD-2 lanes, 2026-07-17 — three independent sightings in one day; treat as a standing design constraint for every DAT-D brick).

A DivisorAdaptation piece carries an R-finite-projective colength — clause (c1) of IsCertified — IFF the piece's trace on the divisor scheme Z = V(D) (finite flat over Spec R) is CLOPEN in Z. Any construction that slices Z along the base (basic-open refinement of pieces, denominator-cleared pieces from a localization cover, Z-blind extraction) produces section rings like R_u that are NOT finite over R, and the certificate is unrecoverable — the localization-span descent lemmas' hypotheses are FALSE, not merely hard. **Mathematically.** The Z-clopen principle asserted here — a piece of a `DivisorAdaptation` carries an $R$-finite colength (clause (c1) of `IsCertified`) **iff** its trace on the divisor scheme is clopen, equivalently iff the piece leaks no support — is proved in both directions as
$$\operatorname{supportLeak}(A_j)=\emptyset \iff \text{$R$-finiteness of the colength at } j,$$
`supportLeak_eq_empty_iff_finite_colength` (`Picard/DivSchemeCertZarC1.lean`, commit `5651710d6`). CHECK THE CONSUMER'S PREDICATE BEFORE GRINDING A HYPOTHESIS: the DD-R certificate gate was over-strong for ~7 sessions.

**TRIMMED 2026-07-27 (janitor hygiene pass, run 0048 round 5).** Two appended annotation layers had grown this item to roughly triple its useful length, and both restated `I-0360` rather than adding to the rule. The rule and its evidence are kept; the "what the relaxation does not buy" narrative now lives in one place. Do not grow this item again — file a new item and cross-reference.

**THE RULE (this is the durable part).** Before grinding a certificate/finiteness hypothesis in this project, check what the actual CONSUMER's predicate is. The project has both a global notion (`IsCertified`, over the whole chart ring $R_Z$) and a Zariski-local one (`IsLocallyCertified`, `DivisorFamilyZar.lean:71`), and **every** downstream interface was built on the local one: `divRepPullAt` (`DivRepAffKit.lean`), `DivRepAffinePullback.pull`, `divRepClassifyZar` (`DivRepClassifyZar.lean:244`) all take `DivFamZar`, never `IsCertified` over $R$.

**WHAT WENT WRONG.** The lane attacked `(D.divisorAdaptation hD).IsCertified g` via `divisorAdaptation_isCertified_of_noLeak_kernel_spanning(_degree)` (`DivSchemeCertUniv.lean:144`, `DivSchemeCertSeed.lean:61`). Its `hnoLeak` input is FALSE for arbitrary extracted pieces (`I-0209`), so the lane sat blocked on an unprovable hypothesis that no consumer ever required.

**THE RELAXATION THAT LANDED** (commits `2709f44d9`, `b959b798b`, `612b5fae0`, `f868c9425`; files `Picard/DivSchemeCertZarSeed.lean`, `DivSchemeCertZarPointwise.lean`, `DivSchemeCertZarTube.lean`; all kernel-checked warning-free):

- `isLocallyCertified_of_forall_exists_away` — span-top production rule.
- `isLocallyCertified_of_forall_prime_exists_away` — the POINTWISE gate, via quasi-compactness of $\operatorname{Spec} R$.
- `isLocallyCertified_of_forall_prime_exists_certified_adaptation` — the adaptation is free, so only the certificate over the shrunken base remains.
- `exists_basicOpen_supportTube` / `exists_notMem_supportLocus_subset_of_fibre` — the support tube refined to the basic-open (Away) shape the gate consumes.
- `isLocallyCertified_of_isCertified` — the old global gate is a special case, so this is a genuine weakening, not a parallel track.

Round 4 pushed it one interface further: `divRepPullAt` now takes a `DivFamZar` class per chart instead of a `CertifiedDivisorFamily` (commit `1e4ac5b52`), which is exactly what this item asked for.

**WHAT IT DOES NOT BUY — read `I-0360`, do not re-derive here.** The relaxation does not unblock U1: the chart-confinement no-go is about PRODUCING a certificate, not consuming one, and `IsLocallyCertified` fails for exactly the divisors `IsCertified` fails for. THE TEMPTING ROUTE. The pointwise gate (isLocallyCertified_of_forall_prime_exists_certified_adaptation,
DivSchemeCertZarPointwise.lean:162) accepts ANY adaptation over the shrunken base. So one is tempted
to choose an adaptation that is SUPPORT-SEPARATED (off-diagonal ovlColength i j all subsingleton).
That really does trivialize the hard part: the Cech difference deltaLeft - deltaRight becomes LITERALLY
ZERO, the equalizer W(d) is the whole product, and both flat-cokernel clauses (c3)/(c4) plus the
kernel-spanning hypothesis are free. Landed as DivisorAdaptation.isCertified_of_separated
(Picard/DivSchemeCertZarSep.lean), needing only (c1) + a rankAtStalk sum.

WHY IT DOES NOT CLOSE THE LANE. The premise is essentially always FALSE. Proved as
DivisorAdaptation.supportLocus_disjoint_chart_inter_of_separated (same file): BOTH pinned charts carry
a partition of unity (FinCoverData.partition0/1, DivisorFamily.lean:174-176), so their pieces cover V0
and V1 respectively (cover0/cover1, DivisorFamily.lean:199-207). A support point z in V0 cap V1
therefore lies in a chart-0 piece AND a chart-1 piece — an off-diagonal pair — and both equations have
non-unit germ at z (isUnit_germ_eqn_iff, SupportTube.lean:245), so that overlap ideal is PROPER and its
colength is not subsingleton. Hence separation holds only if supp d avoids V0 cap V1, i.e. the divisor
is confined to the two vertical fibres of pi. Refining the cover cannot help; the pointwise gate cannot
help either (shrinking the base deletes fibres, it does not move a support point out of the overlap);
and supportLocus is DivEq-invariant, so re-spelling d cannot help.

ALREADY KNOWN FOR THE FIELD CASE. DivisorFamilyFieldSurj.lean:33-38 records the same obstruction in
prose and routes around it: over a field every module is free, so the certificate is discharged on the
PLAIN extraction adaptation via the unconditional CRT colength-degree identity
(DivisorAdaptation.isCertified_of_deg, DivisorFamilyFieldSurj.lean:104; deg_presentationDivisor,
DivisorFamilyFieldCRT.lean:365, I-0230). That escape is unavailable over a nonreduced base, which is
exactly why the flat-cokernel content stands.

RULE. Do not attack the DD-R certificate by choosing a cleverer adaptation. Two independent no-gos now
bound the packaging: cleverer submodule L is ruled out by divUniversalHighWindowKernelSyzygySpans_iff_flat_quotient
(DivSchemeHighWindowSyzygy.lean:298, spanning IFF the sought flatness), and cleverer PIECES are ruled out
by supportLocus_disjoint_chart_inter_of_separated. The honest analogue of the field escape is a RELATIVE
version of the stalk-CRT adaptation-independence of the glued rank, not separation. See [[I-0209]], [[I-0320]].

THE DD-R CERTIFICATE'S NO-LEAK CLAUSE IS A CHART-DESIGN CONDITION, NOT A FIBRE CONDITION
(proved in Lean 2026-07-25, run 0048, commits 49866bdd1 + 206967379; standing constraint for the
certificate lane).

THE THEOREM. A FinCoverData carries a partition of unity on EACH pinned chart, so the chart-b pieces
cover all of V_b and the union of their traces is the whole chart trace supportLocus cap V_b. A
finite union of closed sets is closed, hence

  the assembler's hnoLeak at every piece  ==>  supportLocus cap V_0 and supportLocus cap V_1 are
  CLOSED in the relative curve.

`DivisorAdaptation.isClosed_supportLocus_inter_chart_of_forall_noLeak`
(Picard/DivSchemeCertZarChartTrace.lean). The conclusion mentions neither the adaptation nor its
pieces — only the system and the two pinned charts.

FOUR CONSEQUENCES, all binding:
1. REFINING THE COVER CANNOT HELP. The union of the piece traces is the fixed set supportLocus cap
   V_b; a finer cover only imposes MORE closed-trace constraints on the same union. So roadmap leaf
   leak-image route (b) ("refine the adaptation near a bad prime") is DEAD, and so is any
   support-tube / packet-idempotent scheme aimed at producing hnoLeak piece by piece.
2. SHRINKING THE BASE CANNOT HELP EITHER, except by restating the same condition over the smaller
   base. The pointwise gate's freedom is real but it buys a different thing (see 4).
3. THE OBLIGATION IS: the chart's divisors avoid both vertical fibres of pi, i.e.
   supportLocus subset V_0 cap V_1. It is FALSE for a general degree-g divisor — model:
   V(t x^2 + x y + t y^2) in P^1 over k[t] has a DOMAIN section ring (no nontrivial idempotent after
   any base shrink) and fibre {0, infinity} at t = 0, so no adaptation of it can ever be certified.
   The DD-R atlas must arrange the avoidance. Roadmap leaf ...certificate.chart-avoid.
4. THE POSITIVE SHAPE IS "SWALLOW OR MISS": if every piece either contains the whole support or
   misses it, hnoLeak and clause (c1) follow with no fibre analysis, and a missing piece has a UNIT
   equation so its colength VANISHES (Picard/DivSchemeCertZarSwallow.lean). The pointwise gate
   `isLocallyCertified_of_forall_prime_exists_certified_adaptation` accepts ANY adaptation over the
   shrunken base — so CONSTRUCT this one instead of certifying
   `(exists_divisorAdaptation ...).some`.

RULE: before proving a clause of `IsCertified`, ask which adaptation you are proving it FOR. Seven
sessions were spent proving clauses for `ThetaGeneratorSeed.divisorAdaptation`
(= `.some`, DivSchemeFamily.lean:367), about which nothing is known. See also [[I-0209]]'s Z-clopen
principle, which this theorem identifies with the chart traces.

ANSWER TO I-0333 ITEM 1 (run 0048 round 1). The design decision you were asked to take is no
longer needed: the question is settled by mathematics, and the lane is now blocked on ordinary
work rather than on you. Deliverable of record: informal/spec-dd-r.md ADDENDUM 3; Lean:
Picard/DivSchemeCertZarConfine.lean (6 declarations, 0 sorries, axioms exactly
[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound], in the default build).

THE ANSWER IS (b), AND SHARPER THAN (b). The Z(diamond) chart does NOT confine its divisors:

 * the seed carries no exactness datum, and every universal instantiation of its `side` field
   picks an ARBITRARY chart containing the point, so a point of pi^-1(infinity) is legal;
 * option (a) was never available: Theta = fiberWeilDivisor pi is supported on V_0 \ V_1, so
   set-theoretically Theta = V_1^c and the "theta side" of ADDENDUM 2 §4 is one WHOLE disjunct
   of the verdict, not a tractable half of it — and its argument is circular;
 * there is an explicit counterexample: over k[t], F = t X^2 + X Y + t Y^2 cuts an IRREDUCIBLE
   relative Cartier divisor of degree 2 whose fibre at t = 0 is {0, infinity}, and which stays
   irreducible over every nonempty open of the base. No Zariski shrink separates the witnesses.
   (The witness the lane had been citing for this, Spec R[x]/(x^2-t), never meets
   pi^-1(infinity) and is chart-confined — it does not exhibit the phenomenon.)
 * and the obstruction is DivEq-invariant (landed this round), so it bites the DivFamZar
   QUOTIENT, not merely a chosen representative. DivFamZar is not the relative-divisor functor.

WHY YOU DO NOT HAVE TO CHOOSE. The two branches you were offered are not alternatives: the
carve IS the redesign, and it is legitimate for a reason that is now a theorem. The binding
constraint is FinCoverData (pieces are basic opens of the two PINNED charts, with a partition of
unity on each) — not pi, not the cover's fineness, not the submodule L, not the base. So a
repair must introduce a piece not inside a single pinned chart, and the cheapest such repair is
to let the atlas vary the P^1-coordinate (pi becomes gamma . pi). That is FREE in every landed
declaration, because the whole chain is generic in pi. Its one missing input is Aut(P^1), which
this project does not have (P1 k is a Proj; no PGL_2 action anywhere) — a self-contained piece
of ordinary mathematics, now roadmap leaf ...certificate.p1-aut.

And the carve does not lose points: chart confinement is an OPEN condition on the base
(isOpen_setOf_fibre_subset_chartInter, landed), and confinement at one fibre spreads to a
Zariski neighbourhood. That is exactly what distinguishes an atlas RECORDING avoidance from a
prover ASSUMING it, which §Discipline (2) rightly forbids.

WHAT REMAINS, AND IT IS NOT A DECISION: p1-aut (the GL_2(k) action on P^1) -> fibre-avoid (every
relative divisor avoids two k-points of P^1 Zariski-locally on the base) -> cert-relocalize

> Over a small finite field, where $|\mathbb{P}^1(k)| = q + 1 < n + 2$, **what is `DivFamZar` supposed to be?**

- **(a)** accept $|\mathbb{P}^1(k)| \ge n + 2$ as a hypothesis, and record that the challenge as stated is then not solved for small $q$;
- **(b)** plan a descent lane — `divQProj` (`Picard/DivSchemeQProj.lean`) is the right lever for fpqc descent from a big enough $k'/k$;
- **(c)** generalize the pinned charts to closed points of degree $d \ge 2$, paying `Gamma(P1 k, chartOpen k i) ≃ Polynomial k` (`Curve/P1Charts.lean:234,239`) and `isPrincipalIdealRing_chartSections` (`Curve/P1Points.lean:64`), since $\mathrm{Cl}(\mathbb{P}^1 \setminus \{\text{degree-}d\text{ point}\}) = \mathbb{Z}/d$.

It should be settled BEFORE anyone builds the $\mathrm{GL}_2(k)$ action on $\mathbb{P}^1$ (leaf `p1-aut`, still `pending`) — it decides whether that work is worth doing at all.

## 2. THE MATHEMATICAL HALF — ANSWERED, sharp, no longer yours

`informal/spec-dd-r.md` ADDENDUM 4 §4.4 answers the quantitative question in both directions, and the bound guessed originally is now known to be **sharp**: the pinned-pair route R1 works precisely when $|\mathbb{P}^1(k)| \ge g+2$, and fails exactly when $\sum_{c \in \mathbb{P}^1(k)} e_c \le n$ (with $e_c$ the minimal degree of a closed point of $C$ over $c$), where one can place $\xi_s$ so that $s \in W_c$ for **every** $c$ and no pinned pair confines. Roadmap leaf `...ddr.certificate.field-size` is `done`. **This half needs no human input** — it does not change the design question in §1, which is about what the object should BE, not about where the bound sits.

## 3. THE "CHEAPER OPTION" — REFUTED (2026-07-26, run 0048 round 2)

REFUTED: *"relaxing just the chart-wise partitions to a joint covering drops the requirement from two avoided points to ONE. Worth trying before anyone builds PGL_2."* It buys nothing, and the reason is a typing fact, not a failed proof. `FinCoverData` types its pieces INTO the charts — `h0 : Fin m0 -> Gamma(relCurve, V0)` (`DivisorFamily.lean:166`), `h1` into `V1` (`:168`), `pieces := Sum.elim (basicOpen . h0) (basicOpen . h1)` (`:186`) — so every piece is a basic open of one of the two PINNED charts by construction, whatever the partition data says. Per-piece swallow-or-miss already holds for any cover by opens (`DivSchemeCertZarConn.lean:98` uses only openness), so a connected divisor still lands in one piece, and `basicOpen_le` puts that piece inside one chart. Changing the partition FIELDS cannot change where the pieces LIVE. Recorded as roadmap leaf `...ddr.certificate.joint-cover`, status `rejected`, with the 10-file rebuild cost if anyone tries it anyway.

The sharp form to quote from now on: **NO repair that keeps the pieces inside the preimages of a FIXED PAIR of points of $\mathbb{P}^1$ can work.** Only R1 (vary the pinned pair — needs $\mathrm{Aut}(\mathbb{P}^1)$) or R2 (generalize the piece type) remain.

## 4. THE ORIGINAL CORRECTION TO I-0333 — historical record

CORRECTION TO MY ANSWER ON I-0333, filed in the same round after an adversarial pass. The NEGATIVE half of that answer stands unchanged: chart-avoid is NO, decisively, and you do not have to take that decision. The POSITIVE half — "the repair is cheap and it is not a decision" — was too optimistic in three ways, and one of them put the DIFFERENT question of §1 back to you.

WHAT SURVIVED. The $Z(\diamond)$ chart does not confine its divisors; the counterexample is real; the obstruction is `DivEq`-invariant and therefore bites `DivFamZar` itself; confinement is an open condition on the base, so an atlas may legitimately record avoidance. All kernel-checked or argued in `informal/spec-dd-r.md` ADDENDUM 3.

WHAT DID NOT.

1. The counterexample is FIELD-INDEPENDENT (irreducibility of $s(x^2+1)+x$ needs nothing of $k$), so it also kills the "assume $k$ infinite" escape originally proposed. Enlarging the field does not help.
2. The repair RELOCATES the forbidden geometric input rather than removing it: fibrewise-finite support is not implied by anything a `LocalEquations` carries, and must be discharged from the seed's own degree data.
3. The diagnosis "the binding constraint is `FinCoverData`" was too narrow. Per-piece swallow-or-miss follows from (c1)-finiteness for ANY cover by opens; only the chart-wise partitions of unity upgrade "inside one piece" to "inside one chart". (The "cheaper option" this point proposed is the one refuted in §3.)

A NEW MODULE WITH NO IMPORTER LOOKS GREEN AND IS INVISIBLE — this is how work gets done twice here.

**TRIMMED 2026-07-27 (janitor hygiene pass, run 0054).** The 93-module census and the per-family breakdown that used to open this item are superseded by roadmap row `AJCR.w4-rep.build-reach`, which carries the lake-authoritative triage, the per-module map to the rows whose `done` rests on them, and a staged rooting order. Kept here: the rules and the incident that earned them, because those are the durable part. Re-measured today: **627 on disk, 536 rooted, 91 unrooted** in AJCR.

WHY IT BITES. The lakefile`s `lean_lib` target builds the root module and its transitive imports only. A new `Picard/*.lean` whose commit does not also add an import line is never elaborated, never kernel-checked, and contributes zero jobs — so the job count does not move and nothing looks wrong. Its hgraph node can still carry `lean_status: lean_ok`, which is then unearned.

THE INCIDENT (run 0048, and it cost a whole lane). Round 0 landed `Picard/DivRepAffKitZar.lean`, 174 lines, doing exactly the `DivFamZar` weakening of the F5 kit, with a commit message claiming it — and no import line. Rounds 1-3 never saw it, roadmap leaf `...ddr.divrep.u2` went on calling that weakening "the CHEAP EDIT NOBODY HAS MADE", and in round 4 a lane was briefed to do it from scratch. The lane found the file and merged it away (commit `1e4ac5b52`); the full build stayed at 9,085 jobs, i.e. deleting 174 lines changed the job count by zero — which is itself the proof it was never a job.

RULES.
1. A commit that adds a module MUST add its import line to `AlgebraicJacobian.lean` in the same commit, or say in the message why not and open a roadmap item to root it.
2. Before claiming a declaration is verified, check it is REACHABLE, not just sorry-free. **The count of sorries is not the measure of what is verified.**
3. Before briefing a lane on a "missing" declaration, run `horizon search` — the index covers unrooted files, which is exactly where a previous session`s invisible work lives. `I-0349`s rule cuts both ways: verify ABSENCE as well as presence.
4. Job count is a bad green light: adding or deleting an unrooted module leaves it unchanged.

**The rule it adds:** *a MINUS line in the root-file diff is never yours.* Protocol section 4 tells you to run `git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD -- <project>/AlgebraicJacobian.lean` before committing the root. That check works; the failure mode is misreading it. The lane ran it, saw

The consequence is exactly this item's subject: the dropped module went silently invisible to the build and to any axiom probe written against the root.

**Practical form:** stage the root by building it from the ledger's current `HEAD` and inserting only your own import line (as the workspace README already says), rather than staging the on-disk root, which may carry another session's uncommitted lines in both directions.

WHERE THE DD-R GATE ACTUALLY BITES: NOT U2, NOT 'the certificate for the universal family' -- IT IS L8, LOCAL SURJECTIVITY. Established run 0048 round 5 by a seven-front recon with an adversarial refuter per front; the refuter on the 'single gate' front overturned the recon on exactly this point, and I re-verified it at source.

THE OLD FRAMING, which several roadmap rows and worksheets still use: 'the divrep tail is
independent of the certificate; the certificate only gates U2'. That is FALSE, and the reason is
structural rather than a failed proof.

WHAT IS TRUE.
 * DivFamZar C S pi g is BY DEFINITION a quotient of LOCALLY CERTIFIED divisor families
   (DivisorFamilyZar.lean:224,:235). Certificates are not consumed by the tail -- they come with
   the object.
 * So on the consuming side certificates are free, and DivFamZar.exists_certChartCover
   (DivRepClassifyZarKit.lean:433) is a landed THEOREM that produces a certified representative
   Zariski-locally from the vehicle itself. It is unfolded by every keystone of the classifier:
   DivRepClassifyZar.lean:128 (exists_isDivRepClassify), :176 (isDivRepClassify_unique),
   :230 (exists_overHom_isDivRepClassify), DivRepClassifyZarSep.lean:361 and :363
   (eq_of_isDivRepClassify).
 * IsDivRepClassify (DivRepClassifyZar.lean:90) universally quantifies over
   (G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C T pi g) in its body at :95-97 -- a hypothesis, so scarcity of
   certificates makes the predicate EASIER, not harder.

THE CONSEQUENCE, and it is the campaign's real shape. The no-go (DivSchemeCertZarC1.lean:30-31,
:131) says DivFamZar is BLIND to connected divisors meeting both pinned fibres. So divFunctor
C pi g is a PROPER SUBFUNCTOR of 'degree-g relative divisors'. Representing it is not the problem
-- the whole L9-L13 tail does that honestly, over a section variable, and round 5 nearly finished
it. The problem is that a representable but too-small divisor functor cannot cover Pic^0: the
Abel map out of it is not Zariski-locally surjective, because the classes whose only witnesses
are the invisible divisors are not hit. That is L8, the
Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective (Sigma.desc f) input of pic0RepresentableByOfCharts
(Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:165), roadmap dat-b B-6.

HOW TO APPLY.
 1. Stop describing U2 / the affine package as 'the gate'. They are tail work and they are nearly
    done. The gate is L8.
 2. Repairs R1 (twist by Aut(P^1)) and R2 (generalise FinCoverData's piece type) are correctly
    understood as WIDENING DivFamZar until it sees enough divisors for L8 to hold. Judge any
    proposed repair by that criterion, not by whether it makes a certificate easier to prove.
 3. Anyone proving L8 must check which functor the surjectivity is stated against. Local
    surjectivity onto Pic^0 from a subfunctor that misses classes is FALSE, not merely unproved,
    and no amount of work on the affine package changes it.

See also the roadmap rows AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-b and ...ddr.certificate.cert-relocalize, and
informal/w4-rep-critical-path.md section 7.

The project has a global notion (`IsCertified`, over the whole chart ring $R_Z$) and a Zariski-local one (`IsLocallyCertified`, `DivisorFamilyZar.lean:71`), and **every** downstream interface was built on the local one — `divRepPullAt`, `DivRepAffinePullback.pull`, `divRepClassifyZar` all take `DivFamZar`, never `IsCertified` over $R$. [persistent] w4-rep-critical-path §7.3 IS A SECOND, WEAKER WITNESS — NOT A CORROBORATION OF spec-dd-r ADDENDUM 4 (Ground, 2026-07-27).

§7.3 says its Riemann-Roch derivation was "independently re-derived this round, and it agrees" with ADDENDUM 4, and concludes "the fixed-pair certificate route is dead on the campaign own stratum, OVER ANY FIELD". The conclusion is true, but ADDENDUM 4 §4.3 is what establishes it; §7.3 does NOT.

They are different witnesses over different bases:
* ADDENDUM 4 §4.3 (spec-dd-r.md:809-838): base = an affine open of T = Sym^g C, family = the universal divisor D_univ. Irreducibility input is "supp D_univ is the image of the finite surjection C x Sym^(g-1)C -> C x Sym^g C" (:819-821).
* §7.3 (w4-rep-critical-path.md:226-234): base = (an affine open of) a PENCIL parameter line; the family is the graph of a degree-g map phi : C -> P^1, so supp D = phi^{-1}(U) is literally an open subscheme of C. Needs no Sym^g at all. That is a genuinely CHEAPER witness and worth keeping — but it is a new result, not agreement.

WHERE §7.3 IS STRICTLY WEAKER (two places, both load-bearing for the "over any field" claim):
1. It is not field-uniform. §7.3 writes the divisor "s_0 + s_inf" and computes l(K - s_0 - s_inf) >= g - 2, i.e. it treats s_0, s_inf as DEGREE-1 (rational) points. Over a non-closed field the minimal closed points q_0 in pi^{-1}(p_0), q_1 in pi^{-1}(p_1) have residue degrees e_0, e_1 >= 1, and an effective E >= q_0 + q_1 of degree g exists only if e_0 + e_1 <= g. Over F_2 with g = 2 and e_0 = e_1 = 2 there is NO such E and §7.3 witness does not exist. This is exactly the regime ADDENDUM 4 §4.4 "only if" isolates (sum_c e_c vs n). ADDENDUM 4 §4.3 step 3 dodges it deliberately — base-change to L = a residue field of kappa(q_0) tensor_k kappa(q_1), pad by (g-1)Q_0 — and says so in terms ("No rational-point hypothesis is used anywhere", spec-dd-r.md:826).
2. Its g = 2 sub-case needs s_inf to be the hyperelliptic conjugate of s_0, defended by "which one is free to arrange, since pi is a choice". ADDENDUM 4 §4.3 holds for "pi any finite dominant map" (:812). §7.3 g=2 witness exists only for specially chosen pi.

The shrink-stability step itself is FINE in both, and §7.3 phrasing "an open subscheme of the irreducible C, hence irreducible" is literally correct under the pencil/graph reading (a nonempty open of an irreducible space is irreducible hence connected). That is not the weak point; the residue-degree bookkeeping is.

ACTION: do not strike §7.3 — strike its "over any field" and its "it agrees". Relabel it as the cheap pencil witness with the side condition e_0 + e_1 <= g. Strategy is unaffected (ADDENDUM 4 §4.3 still kills the fixed pair over any field, and §4.5 "do not formalise the witness" still stands).

AJC B3 gate: the reusable ℙ¹ template and three tooling gotchas from the rigid-pushforward campaign

**TRIMMED 2026-07-27 (janitor hygiene pass, run 0054 s0010).** This item was written as a frontier record and was WRONG TWICE IN THE SAME DIRECTION within one day — "the gate needs FOUR statements", then "there is deliberately no `instance : HasRigidPushforward`". Both false. Per this item's own meta-lesson and `I-0439`'s corollary, the state half is now deleted rather than corrected a third time: **the gate's status lives in roadmap row `AJC.picrep.rigidpushforward`** (done, pinned `02ae27824`/`744a74bf2`), which is the artifact designed to be re-set. What is kept below is the mathematics and the tooling, which do not go stale.

**HOW ℙ¹ INTEGRALITY FELL — the durable template.** Not by cohomology. Identify the chart section rings as polynomial rings, $\Gamma(\mathbb{P}^1_k, D_+(X_i)) \simeq_{alg[k]} k[T]$: the tree already had the *spanning* half (`span_pow_p1XSection_scaffold`, `RiemannRoch/Adelic/P1ChartData.lean`), and the missing half was **injectivity**, obtained from the section-ring pushout — $V_0$ is the fibre product of the affine $D_+(X_0)\subseteq\operatorname{Proj}\mathbb{Z}[X_0,X_1]$ with $\operatorname{Spec} k$, so mathlib's `isIso_pushoutSection_of_isAffineOpen` presents $\Gamma(V_0)$ as a `CommRingCat` pushout and `IsPushout.desc` yields a retraction. Then "both chart rings are domains" gives integrality by `IsReduced.of_openCover` plus density of the overlap. Reusable wherever a hand-built projective object needs a ring-level identification.

**WHY THE DISCHARGE WAS BELIEVABLE, and this is the part to copy.** Measure at the **SYNTHESIS SITE**, not at the theorem: restate the consumers *without* the `[HasRigidPushforward C]` binder, so Lean must synthesize the gate to elaborate them, and read `#print axioms` there. The same measurement applied to `HasPicScheme` is what exposes `instHasPicScheme` as poisoned. Non-vacuity is a separate question again, and needs a witness object (`Picard/RigidPushforwardP1Witness.lean` exhibits ℙ¹ satisfying all three binders). Catalogue of what each check does and does not see: `I-0442`.

**THREE TOOLING GOTCHAS, in descending order of reuse:**

1. `lake env lean <file>` does **not** run this project's style linters (`linter.style.maxHeartbeats`, `linter.style.setOption`). A file can be silent under `lake env lean` and still warn under `lake build <module>`. Always finish a new module with a single-module `lake build` (~20-35 s warm) before calling it warning-free. Never run a bare `lake build` (43 min — see `I-0319`).
2. The direct route to the chart identification through `HomogeneousLocalization.val_injective` **`isDefEq`-times-out** at the concrete grading — write it `Away.mk`-first.
3. Mathlib v4.31 still has **no** integrality/irreducibility/reducedness API for `Proj` at all, while it has all three for affine space (`AlgebraicGeometry/AffineSpace.lean:392/402/419`). Do not go looking; the pushout route above is why this was closable anyway.

**AND THE META-LESSON, earned by this item's own two corrections.** A memory that records "the frontier is N statements" against a lane being actively worked goes stale within hours, and a stale frontier count is then quoted as authority. Record the *technique* and the *tooling*; point at the roadmap row for the count.
