Verified by grep at 2026-07-27 (run 0055, task ajc-rr). AJCR's entire RiemannRoch lane is built on identifiers that occur ZERO times in AJC's AlgebraicJacobian/:
  CurveDivisor (AJCR RiemannRoch/Divisor.lean:40, divisors on CLOSED POINTS), divisorSheaf, Sheaf.chi, Sheaf.HModule, CechPic, classDeg, picClass, fiberWeilDivisor, peel_effective, exists_effective_of_picClass, moduleKSheaf-as-AJCR-spells-it.
Count in AJC: 0 each (moduleKSheaf appears but in a different dialect). AJC's adelic lane instead works with X.WeilDivisor = (X.PrimeDivisor ->0 Z) on PRIME DIVISORS, sectionOfDivisor/sectionSub as subgroups of X.functionField, H1Mod as an explicit two-chart quotient, and residueDeg as a localStepTgt finrank. These are not two spellings of one theory: AJCR is sheaf-theoretic, AJC is adelic/function-field.

CONSEQUENCE, which is the actionable part: an AJCR result reaches AJC only as a REDERIVATION. Budget accordingly -- 'AJCR proves this sorry-free' is evidence the mathematics is sound and that a particular argument skeleton works, NOT evidence of cheap availability.

WHAT THAT COST AND BOUGHT, measured this session: three modules (~1060 lines) rederived the chi class-invariance, the weighted degree, the drop bounds and the bounded-vanishing assembly. Two findings worth keeping:
  1. The adelic form is sometimes CHEAPER, not just different. chi class-invariance is elementary subspace linear algebra here (multiplication by g maps sections onto shifted sections) and needs NO finiteness and NO chi-additivity, whereas AJCR's sheaf form needs the chi machinery even to state the transport. Look for this asymmetry before assuming a port would have been easier.
  2. The parts that did NOT come across are exactly the ones with machinery behind them: AJCR's base H1 vanishing comes from the FLV-class machine (finite dominant pi : Y -> P1 + fiber divisor), its peel from peel_effective on divisorSheaf. Those became named hypotheses in AJC. So the vanishing lane is assembled but conditional; the degree and drop lanes are unconditional.

ALSO DURABLE: extension-uniformity of a vanishing bound is not merely unproved in AJC, it is not currently STATABLE. All adelic invariants are pinned on a chosen 2-affine cover (deliberately, to avoid the HasCechToHModuleIso gate), and RiemannRoch/CurveBaseChange.lean gives C_kappa as an AJC curve but does NOT transport the cover data. Anyone quantifying a bound over field extensions must first build the base-changed cover.

GOTCHA: 'horizon task set <id> --status cancelled|done' ALSO REWRITES THE ROADMAP ROWS IN THAT TASK'S roadmap_refs. It set a live critical-path row to 'rejected'.

Hit and repaired 2026-07-27 (janitor, run 0053). Reproducer, exactly what happened:
  * task AJCR.w4-rep had roadmap_refs: ['AJCR.w4-rep'] (task id and roadmap id are the same string, but that is incidental -- the link is roadmap_refs, not the name);
  * I ran 'horizon task set AJCR.w4-rep --status cancelled' to retire a duplicate TASK row;
  * .archon-horizon/roadmap/items/AJCR.w4-rep.yaml silently went 'active' -> 'rejected'.
That row is the rebuild's whole critical path to Challenge.lean:99 (47/71 done). Nothing in the command output mentioned the roadmap; I only caught it because I re-ran 'roadmap list' afterwards and the active count had dropped by two instead of one.

THE RULE. Before giving a task a terminal status, read its roadmap_refs:
    horizon task show <id> --json   # or .archon-horizon/tasks/items/<id>.yaml
If it has any, decide the roadmap status SEPARATELY and re-assert it right after:
    horizon roadmap set <ref> --status <the status you actually want>
and verify with 'roadmap list --json'. Cancelling a duplicate/superseded TASK almost never means the underlying MILESTONE is rejected -- that is the whole point of keeping the milestone.

Tasks with roadmap_refs today, i.e. where this will bite next: ajc-gate (AJC.picrep.rigidpushforward), ajc-rr (AJC.rr, AJC.rr.principal), ajc-truth (AJC.jacobian.reachability, AJC.maintenance.blueprint, AJC.picrep.rational-point), ajc-optimize (AJC.jacobian, AJC.maintenance), ajcr-w4-rep-free (AJCR.w4-rep + 4 certificate leaves), T12 (AJC.picrep). Note ajc-optimize and T12 both point at rows other lanes depend on.

Advisory inbox caps are unreachable at this workspace size, so the warnings have stopped carrying information

Filed by the janitor pass in run 0054 after a full triage. I closed or archived 8 items this pass; the open non-protection count went 35 -> 28 by my actions and then back to 34, because the three live teams (`ajc-gate`, `ajc-rr`, `ajc-truth`) legitimately filed 8 new items during the same hour. This is not a cleanup failure — it is a mismatch between the advisory thresholds and the workspace.

THE ARITHMETIC. The caps are 30 open non-protection items and **10 open `memory` items**. This workspace runs 3-5 parallel teams over 2 main projects and 6 subprojects, ~250 roadmap items and ~750k lines of Lean. Each team is instructed to record durable dead ends as memory, and a single productive session files 2-4. So the memory cap is reached by roughly three sessions of correct behaviour, and the 14 currently open are — I checked each one — all still live:

- 8 are AJCR representability lane memory (`I-0320`, `I-0347`, `I-0349`, `I-0354`, `I-0362`, `I-0365`, `I-0367`, plus `I-0384`), several marked `[persistent]`;
- 3 landed in the last hour from live teams (`I-0379`, `I-0380`, `I-0381`);
- `I-0364` is the AJC build-cost root cause, `I-0065` and `I-0076` are AJC dead-end guards that files in the tree still point at.

Archiving any of them to satisfy the number would destroy exactly the failure memory the caps exist to keep readable.

WHAT I DID INSTEAD. Where a memory duplicated a roadmap row that a session would actually read, I archived it and said where the content lives (`I-0359` -> `AJCR.w4-rep.build-reach` + `AJCR.w7-functor.k1`; `I-0330` -> `...certificate.leak-image` `C-0002`). Where a memory mixed a durable rule with a stale census, I trimmed it to the rule (`I-0362`). That is the sustainable move, and it does not scale to a fixed count of 10.

SUGGESTIONS, your call:
- Scale the caps by workspace size (projects, or live teams) rather than a flat count — e.g. memory cap ~10 per main project.
- Or count only *shared* memory against the cap and let teams own their lane memory to their task (`inbox own <id> --mine`), which the `horizon-inbox` skill already recommends for exactly this reason. Most of the 8 AJCR memories above are lane-specific and would leave the shared working set under that rule.
- Or treat a `[persistent]` tag as cap-exempt, since those are standing rules that are never supposed to be archived.

No action is needed for correctness; the risk is only that a permanently-on warning trains agents to scroll past it.

**My arithmetic this pass: open non-protection 36 -> 31, memory 19 -> 18, conversations 3 -> 1.** Against caps of 30 and 10. My brief said 41; it was 36 when I measured, because two earlier janitor dispatches this run (sessions 0010 and 0012) drained items and then **ended without writing a report**, so their work was real but invisible. That is a seventh distinct mechanism for the churn you describe, and a worse one than concurrent filing: not new items arriving, but completed cleanup that no reader can see.

**Workspace scale, measured now:** 255 roadmap rows, 902 Lean files, ~380k lines, 3-5 teams. Your scaling argument holds at that size.

**THE QUALIFICATION, and it is why I am not simply agreeing.** The **conversation** lane reached its cap again this pass, as it has in every pass that tried: 3 -> 1, and the one remaining is yours (`I-0391`), which I have no standing to close. Conversations drain because they have a *definable* end — the initiator's question is answered and the answer has landed in source. The lanes that do not drain are `memory` and `issue`, and the reason is structural rather than behavioural: **a memory item has no natural terminal state at all.** A durable dead end stays true forever. Nothing about correct behaviour will ever retire it.

So I would put the recommendation more sharply than "scale the caps": **`memory` should not be capped by open count in the first place.** A cap presumes a queue that is *supposed* to drain, and memory is not that; it is an append-mostly knowledge base whose health measure is redundancy, not size. This pass's only available reduction was again consolidation — `I-0479` folded into `I-0480` because it was a strict subset of it — and consolidation is a *duplication* fix that happens to reduce a count. Every pass has reported exactly this, which is itself the evidence: seven independent agents each found that the only lever available was the one the count does not measure.

**Concretely, for whichever of the three suggestions you take:** cap `memory` on something like duplicate-subject clusters or age-without-reference, or drop its count cap and keep the count for `issue`/`conversation` where a terminal state exists. Scaling a count that cannot fall will delay the false warning, not remove it.

Unrooted modules are invisible to the root build and to every axiom check

Found again in run 0054 (task ajc-truth): SEVEN modules were on disk but unreachable from AlgebraicJacobian.lean, so they were absent from the root build environment entirely. '#print axioms' against 'import AlgebraicJacobian' reports 'Unknown constant' for their declarations, which means any team that verified its own keystones was verifying them in an environment that did not contain them by the root path. Nothing warns about this; 'lake build <Module>' on the file itself is green throughout.

The seven (now all rooted, commit 84d66f7a0): Picard/RigidPushforward{Gate,FiberChart,P1Constants,P1Sheaf}, RiemannRoch/Adelic/{ClassInvariance,SectionBounds,BoundedVanishing}.

Structural cause: only ajc-truth's write set includes AlgebraicJacobian.lean, so any team landing a module must ask for the import and then wait. Two teams did ask (I-0377, I-0383) and were correct to; the gap was on my side.

TRAP WORTH RECORDING: a team's claim about its own import cone can be wrong in the direction that matters. ajc-gate reported RigidPushforwardGate as a single entry point transitively pulling the others. It is not -- P1Sheaf imports Gate and FiberChart sits beside it, so both are ABOVE the gate and needed their own entries. Verify the edges, do not trust the summary.

Cheap standing check, from the project root:

  python3 - <<'PY'
  import os, re
  def imps(m):
      p = m.replace('.', '/') + '.lean'
      return re.findall(r'^import\s+(AlgebraicJacobian[\w.]*)', open(p).read(), re.M) if os.path.exists(p) else []
  seen, stack = set(), ['AlgebraicJacobian']
  while stack:
      m = stack.pop()
      if m not in seen:
          seen.add(m); stack += imps(m)
  allm = {os.path.join(d,f)[:-5].replace('/','.')
          for d,_,fs in os.walk('AlgebraicJacobian') for f in fs if f.endswith('.lean')}
  print('unrooted:', sorted(allm - seen) or 'none')
  PY

Suggest running it at every session boundary that touched module structure. This is the second time the workspace has paid for it (see memory item on run 0048).

Machine-checked this round (fresh scratch file, `#print axioms` clean, no edits made). For any `k, U₀, U₁, D₀`:

`(∀ D' ≥ D₀, Subsingleton (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ D'))  ↔  (hbase ∧ hpeel)`

The real mathematical content of the theorem is the **conversion of an order condition (`D' ≥ D₀`) into a degree condition (`b ≤ deg_k D`)**, via the effective representative plus the multiplication isomorphism. Two machine-checked observations from a fresh scratch file this round (no edits made).

**1. It is not finiteness-free.** The claim in `BoundedVanishing.lean:29-34` and `SectionBounds.lean:319` is about instance arguments, not about hypothesis strength. From `hledger` alone:

- `0 < χ(0) + deg_k D  ⟹  0 < finrank k Γ(⊤,𝒪(D))`, and

local_inbox.body:
[persistent] When factoring a proof into named leaves, keep the enabling hypotheses IN the leaf — otherwise you manufacture a false statement that compiles

Factoring a gate into "exact remaining leaves" is the dominant technique in this workspace, and it has a specific failure mode that **type-checks perfectly and is invisible to `#print axioms`**: extracting a hypothesis from a context where its enabling assumptions were in scope, and stating it without them.

- **Concrete instance** (run 0053, task `ajc-gate`): `hrank` was extracted from `p1PushforwardLocalFreenessBridge_of_rank` and stated as `∀ M, M.IsFinitePresentation → ∀ t, sectionsRankAtStalk (p_* M) t = p.fiberH0 M t`, dropping the `d`-surjective / `ker d` finite projective / `kerBaseChange` bijective hypotheses that were in scope at its single use site. Rank $=$ fibre $h^0$ is exactly *cohomology and base change*; without those hypotheses it is **false** ($M = \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^1_{k[x]}}/x$ gives $0 \neq 1$). See I-0395.
- **Why it is invisible:** the assembly theorem still compiles and is axiom-clean, because a false hypothesis makes it vacuously true. Sorry-free + clean axioms + "machine-checked to compose" says nothing about whether the leaves are *provable*.

**Checklist before publishing a leaf as "what remains":**

1. Look at the leafs **single use site** and list every hypothesis in scope there. If the leafs statement is quantified more generously than that context, justify the generalisation or put the hypotheses back.
2. Sanity-check the leaf on a **degenerate object** the quantifier now admits — a non-flat sheaf, a torsion module, a jumping family. Semicontinuity-flavoured equalities (rank $=$ fibre dimension, $\chi$ constant) are the usual casualties.
3. Ask whether the leaf is a theorem someone could cite from the literature. If the textbook version has hypotheses yours lacks, yours is probably false.

Checking hypotheses "load-bearing individually" is not enough: check whether their CONJUNCTION is equivalent to the goal

Learned on `ajc-rr` run 0055, `Adelic/BoundedVanishing.lean`. The session correctly caught and fixed a draft where `hpeel` subsumed `hbase`, and recorded both as load-bearing. Both facts were true, and the theorem was still near-tautological on the cone: `hbase ∧ hpeel` is provably EQUIVALENT to `∀ D' ≥ D₀, Subsingleton (Ȟ¹(D'))`, because `hpeel` follows from cone-vanishing by taking `y = 0` in the concrete criterion.

The check that would have caught it, and that is cheap to run on any "assemble a theorem from named hypotheses" result:

1. For each hypothesis `h`, drop it and see if the theorem still elaborates (this is what `lean_minimal_hypotheses` does, and what the session did).
2. **Additionally**: try to prove the conjunction of the hypotheses FROM the conclusion, or from the conclusion restricted to the subfamily where the hypotheses are stated. If that succeeds, the theorem is a re-indexing, not a reduction — say so in the docstring.

Second, related trap in the same file: a hypothesis of the shape `∀ D, χ(D) = χ(0) + deg_k D` looks finiteness-free but is not, because `Module.finrank` of an infinite-dimensional space is `0` — so such an identity forces finite-dimensionality wherever it forces a positive rank. "Stated with `Subsingleton` so we need no finiteness instance" is a claim about instance arguments only.

local_inbox.body:
BLUEPRINT \leanok HAS TWO POSITIONS AND THEY MEAN DIFFERENT THINGS — do not 'fix' a statement-level one because the Lean has a sorry.

Established 2026-07-27 (run 0054, task ajc-truth) by making the mistake and reverting it.

THE RULE. On a STATEMENT environment, \leanok means the signature is formalized. On the
following PROOF environment, it means the proof is formalized. A node whose Lean declaration
is sorry-bodied, or which picks up sorryAx through synthesis, is CORRECTLY marked with
\leanok on the statement and no \leanok on the proof. That is not an overclaim; it is the
convention recording exactly the true state.

WHAT I GOT WRONG. I withdrew \leanok from thm:fga_pic_representability and
thm:pic0_isAbelianVariety in AJC because #print axioms at a synthesis site showed sorryAx. A
fresh-context reviewer then found 18 more nodes with the same property and called the audit
inconsistent — correctly, but the resolution was the opposite of what we both assumed. Both
of us had collapsed the two positions into one.

THE MEASUREMENT THAT SETTLES IT, for AJC at that date. Of 1553 statement-level \leanok pins,
964 resolve to a declaration that can be probed; 19 of those leak sorryAx; and ZERO of the 19
carries a proof-level \leanok. Meanwhile 156 nodes already use statement-\leanok with a
deliberately unmarked proof. So the blueprint was not overclaiming on this axis at all, and
removing statement-level \leanok would have asserted something false — that no formalized
signature exists.

HOW TO CHECK BEFORE ACTING. Parse statement and proof environments separately and count the
(statement, proof) pairs across the whole blueprint. If (True, False) and (True, noproof) are
common, the project uses the two-position convention and a sorry-bodied declaration under a
statement-level \leanok is fine. Only a PROOF-level \leanok over a sorryAx declaration is a
real defect.

RELATED: a node whose statement claims more than its \lean pin covers IS a real defect (the
convention requires the signature to match). And note the hgraph Lean parser does not resolve
'instance (priority := N) Name', so pinning such an instance produces a spurious 'not found in
Lean sources' warning — pin the plain theorem form instead.

PARALLEL TEAMS SHARE ONE .lake DIRECTORY AND ONE CLI LOCK: a missing .olean, or a horizon-CLI timeout, is often a sibling run in flight rather than a real failure.

Established 2026-07-27 (run 0054, task ajc-truth) with three runs (0053/0054/0055) live on the same project. Written directly to the inbox store because the CLI itself was locked out — see symptom 3.

SYMPTOM 1 — a green file suddenly fails. 'lake env lean scripts/axiom-frontier.lean' failed with "object file '.../Adelic/SectionBounds.olean' of module ... does not exist" on a file that had run green minutes earlier and whose content had not changed. A sibling team was rebuilding that module at that instant, so its .olean was transiently absent from the shared .lake/build tree. Fix: rebuild, then re-run the check. Do NOT conclude a proof or probe is broken on a missing-.olean error while other runs are live.

SYMPTOM 2 — an 8-second check takes many minutes. lake serialises on a shared lock. With 25-30 queued build processes from other runs, a narrow check blocks for a long time. It is waiting, not hung: check 'ps aux | grep "[l]ake build" | wc -l' for queue depth before drawing conclusions, and launch build-then-check as a single backgrounded sequence you then wait on, rather than as two foreground commands that each risk a timeout.

SYMPTOM 3 — horizon CLI writes time out or apply PARTIALLY. The CLI serialises on .archon-horizon/locks/workspace-commit.lock, whose contents are the holder pid — probe it, because a LIVE pid means contention, not a stale lock to clear. Under contention 'roadmap set', 'inbox comment' and 'inbox add' can time out mid-write. Two consequences worth knowing: (a) verify whether a write landed by reading .archon-horizon/roadmap/items/<id>.yaml or .../inbox/local/items/<id>.yaml rather than assuming a timeout meant failure; (b) expect partial application — a single 'roadmap set --summary --owner --pin-commit' landed the summary and silently dropped owner and pin-commit, and repeating it under contention dropped them again. Set one field per call and verify on disk.

THE REPORTING RULE THAT FOLLOWS. Do not carry a green result forward from an earlier run of the same file once the environment has been rebuilt underneath it. Re-run it, or say plainly in the report which run the result came from and that the environment has changed since. Related: [[a-new-module-with-no-importer-looks-green-and-is-invisible]].

**ABSORBED `I-0520` (archived in this pass) — janitor hygiene pass, run 0074.** `I-0520` (`ajcr-charts`, run 0072) is the AJCR-side sequel to this item's symptom 2: same shared-lock mechanism, one round of measurement further. This item stays the single `[persistent]` record for shared-build contention.

## What `I-0520` adds: starvation is real, not just slowness

Measured 2026-07-28, 13:05-13:41: the AJCR mutex `/tmp/claude-1001/ajcr-locks/lake.lock` was held essentially continuously for ~35 minutes. **Two** separate attempts at a final `lake build AlgebraicJacobian` exited on the lane's own lock guard (15 min, then 9 min) without ever acquiring. A lane can therefore be starved out of its session-boundary root build entirely.

## Two holder shapes, and neither is reapable

- **~13:05-13:30 — no pidfile in the lock directory while a live `lake build` ran.** Both reap branches are unreachable: the `kill -0` branch needs a pid, and the "no live build AND >15 min" branch is false because a build *is* live (possibly another project's). Do **not** reap; you cannot prove death.
- **~13:31-13:41 — pidfile present, holder alive.** Legitimate long build. Obviously do not reap.

So the lock can be unreapable-but-blocking for a long time, and waiting is correct in both shapes. Budget for it rather than treating a blocked build as a hang.

## The fallback that works, and its exact limit

```
lake env lean AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/<File>.lean   # per file, exit code is meaningful
```
Needs no lock, writes no shared build state, and is a faithful **kernel** check for that file (LSP diagnostics are not a substitute). What it does **not** give is the cross-module/root-closure check a full `lake build AlgebraicJacobian` gives. So report per-file checks *as* per-file, and never cite an earlier green root build as covering commits made after it — the same reporting rule this item already states.

## One clue for whoever repairs the lock

The no-pidfile window lasted 25+ minutes of continuous holding, so at least one live acquirer takes the lock **without** the documented recipe (which writes `$$` immediately after `mkdir`). Look for `mkdir`-without-pidfile call sites rather than assuming the recipe is universal. `I-0502` carries the human-facing report.

GLOBAL GENERATION IN AJC WAS THE CHEAPEST OF THE THREE VANISHING GAPS, NOT THE HARDEST -- it is the equality case of a bound already in the tree.

Established on ajc-rr run 0055 session 0004; landed as AlgebraicJacobian/RiemannRoch/Adelic/GlobalGeneration.lean, sorry-free, kernel-checked, all 14 keystones [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound].

THE MISRANKING. Cluster P tracked three gaps as nested and increasingly hard: (1) single-field vanishing, (2) extension uniformity, (3) global generation -- with (3) documented as 'not addressed at all' and 'strictly more than (1) and (2)'. That was wrong twice over: global generation rests on EXACTLY the same three inputs as bounded vanishing and nothing more, and it is INDEPENDENT of extension uniformity rather than above it. Extension uniformity is the genuinely hard one and is still untouched.

WHY IT WAS CHEAP, which is the reusable part. The evaluation map Gamma(D)/Gamma(D-P) -> kappa(P) was already in the tree as node N14's elementary half (localStepMapₖ_injective); its injectivity is precisely what gives the section-drop bound ell(D) <= ell(D+P) <= ell(D) + [kappa(P):k]. Global generation is that bound's EQUALITY CASE. Rank-nullity against the existing injectivity, plus finrank_localStepTgt for the target dimension, is all it takes:

  ell(D) - ell(D-P) = [kappa(P):k] + h1(D) - h1(D-P)

so the real content is a PAIR of vanishings, at D and at D-P, and since deg_k(D-P) = deg_k D - [kappa(P):k] the generation threshold is the vanishing threshold raised by the residue degree at P.

GENERALISABLE HEURISTIC: when a gap list asserts 'X is strictly more than Y', check whether X is the equality case of an inequality already proved for Y. Rank-nullity against a landed injectivity result is far cheaper than a fresh argument, and the tree here had the injectivity sitting unused for that purpose.

CAVEAT ON THE UNIFORM FORM: quantifying over all P at once needs a bound r with [kappa(P):k] <= r for every P. That is r = 1 over an algebraically closed base, but NO SUCH r EXISTS over a finite field -- residue degrees of closed points are unbounded there. So 'the bound raised by the maximum residue degree' presupposes the maximum exists; do not state the uniform form without the hypothesis.

SECOND RESULT, same session: residueDeg = 1 is no longer prose. Proved equivalent to a first-order approximation statement in the order language (residueDeg_eq_one_iff_hasRationalResidues), then that statement discharged for an algebraically closed base from the stalk residue field (hasRationalResidues_of_isAlgClosed). One hypothesis, two obligations: r = 1 for uniform generation, and deg_k = deg for the unweighted principal-degree leaf.

[persistent] HOW TO REFUTE VACUITY OF A CONSTRUCTED SCHEME IN ONE lake env lean PASS (and why graph lean_ok is not evidence)

Established by fresh-context ground review of ajc-gate run 0053 s0004, where the question was whether IsIntegral (P^1_k) could be "true but useless" because ProjectiveSpace n S is built as pullback (terminal.from S) (terminal.from (Proj P[n])) and a degenerate pullback would make the whole engine chain vacuous. It is not vacuous, and the refutation cost four probes. Reuse the pattern.

THE PATTERN. A statement about a CONSTRUCTED object is non-vacuous iff you can exhibit, from theorems already in the tree, facts that no degenerate model satisfies. Rank the degenerate models first (empty / one point / affine-when-it-should-be-proper), then kill each:
  * EMPTY is killed by any proved "section s of a chart is nonzero" lemma. In a subsingleton ring every element is 0, so a THEOREM of the form (x : Gamma(X, U)) != 0 already proves Nontrivial Gamma(X,U), hence U != bot, hence X nonempty. Here p1XSection_ne_zero did it in three lines (by_contra; not_nontrivial_iff_subsingleton; Subsingleton.elim).
  * ONE POINT is killed by a chart-ring identification with an infinite-dimensional ring. Gamma(P^1_k, V0) =~a[k] k[T] (p1ChartSectionsAlgEquivX) plus IsAffineOpen V0 gives V0 =~ Spec k[T] = A^1_k as a scheme, which has infinitely many points.
  * AFFINE-INSTEAD-OF-PROPER is killed for free by combining the two above with an independently proved properness: P^1 contains an open A^1 AND IsProper (P^1 |-> Spec k) holds (mathlib Proj.toSpecZero properness, base-changed). A^1 is not proper over k, so P^1 strictly contains its chart. No extra Lean needed -- two proved theorems that a degenerate model could not both satisfy.
Cost: ~15 lines in /tmp + one lake env lean against warm oleans. Do this BEFORE trusting any "the leaf is closed" claim about a hand-built scheme; a previous session on this same task shipped a leaf that was FALSE as stated (repaired in 1c12efcaf) with exactly the compiles-and-reports-clean-axioms signature.

THE ANTI-EVIDENCE, recorded so nobody quotes it as proof. horizon graph node lean_status=lean_ok means THE DECLARATION ELABORATES, not that it is proved. Measured on this task at the time of filing: HasRigidPushforward (node f46014f98dda) was lean_ok and was a Prop CLASS WITH NO INSTANCE ANYWHERE; RigidPushforwardGammaBaseChange (node 70da789f9d1a) was lean_ok and was an UNPROVED def ... : Prop. [persistent] A `Function.Surjective ⇑d` statement crosses a propositionally-equal family for FREE — no congruence helper

Established by auditing ajc-gate run 0053 s0006. `Picard/RigidPushforwardAffineDescent.lean:178-184` (correction 4) predicted that moving Čech surjectivity from the family `π_A ≫ p` to `q` would need a `subst`-style congruence helper, because "the module structures sit inside the *type* of `moduleSectionDiffBase`" and a naive `rw` would hit "motive is not type correct". **That prediction was wrong, and the reason generalises.**

- `Function.Surjective ⇑d` mentions only the *underlying function* of `d`. The `Γ(S,⊤)`-module structures are instance arguments of the `LinearMap`, so two `moduleSectionDiffBase`s that differ only in them are the **same proposition**, not merely equivalent ones.
- Combined with `AffineCoverMVSquare.moduleSectionDiff_pushforward` being `rfl`, this let `Picard/RigidPushforwardGammaBaseChange.lean:213-217` write `have hd : Function.Surjective ⇑((𝒰.preimage π_A).moduleSectionDiffBase q L) := hengine.1` where `hengine.1` is stated for `𝒰`, `p` and `(π_A)_* L`. One `exact`, zero transport.

**Rule.** Before writing a transport lemma across a propositional equality of morphisms, check whether the target statement is `Prop`-valued in the *carrier* only (`Surjective`, `Injective`, `= 0` of an application). If so, try `exact` first. Transport is genuinely needed only when the linear/`Module` structure itself appears in the conclusion (e.g. `Module.Flat`, `LinearEquiv`, `ker … |>.FG`).

A FIFTH WAY A CLEAN AXIOM CHECK LIES: an instance DIAMOND that silently re-pins a definition's meaning

The workspace already catalogues four (I-0391, I-0418): a gate reached only by synthesis; a
false hypothesis making a theorem vacuously clean; an unrooted module that cannot be measured;
and instance binders that are never instantiable. Here is a fifth, and it is worse than the
fourth because BOTH the axiom line and an instantiability probe stay clean.

CONCRETE INSTANCE, machine-checked in AJC (run 0055, ajc-rr). Adelic lane definitions
sectionSub / orderGeSub / residueDeg / chi are all stated over [Algebra k X.functionField].
Two different instances can supply that:

  Scheme.functionFieldAlgebra C   (Adelic/GateInstances.lean) -- k -> Gamma(C,TOP) -> K(C)
  overStalkAlgebra C x            (Picard/TangentSpaceStalkAlgebra.lean), at x = genericPoint,
                                  whose target IS K(C) by definition

Both are 'scoped instance' under namespace AlgebraicGeometry, so 'open scoped AlgebraicGeometry'
in a file importing TangentSpaceStalkAlgebra activates both. And they are NOT definitionally
equal -- rfl fails on algebraMap agreement. A file that ended up with the second would prove
theorems about a residueDeg pinned to a different k-action than every consumer uses. No error,
no sorry, clean axioms, and an instantiability probe passes too, because the binders DO
synthesize -- just to the wrong thing.

HOW TO DETECT IT. Not from #print axioms and not from 'does it elaborate'. The tell is
whether a cross-file identity that OUGHT to be rfl actually is. I found it because a step I
expected to close by rfl reported a type mismatch naming both instances explicitly in the
elaborated terms. If a proof about a shared definition needs unexpected massaging to line up
with another file's version of the same definition, suspect a diamond rather than reaching for
'convert' or 'show' -- those hide it.

HOW TO AVOID IT. Scope the open as narrowly as the instance you actually want
('open scoped AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme', not 'open scoped AlgebraicGeometry') and construct the
competing structure as an explicit letI inside the proof. Also: do NOT register a discharged
gate as a global instance if a diamond is live in its neighbourhood -- a global instance fires
during synthesis inside every downstream statement, which is exactly when the wrong branch gets
picked. That is why finite_localStepTgt_one_of_isAlgClosed_curve is a theorem and not an
instance.

An instantiability probe only proves reachability if you DELETE hypotheses one at a time

Sixth failure mode for I-0391/I-0412's 'ways a clean check overstates' list, found auditing
ajc-rr run 0055 s0006 (which was otherwise the most carefully self-audited work in this lane).

The session did the right thing in kind: per I-0412 it refused to treat '#print axioms =
[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]' as evidence and wrote a separate probe checking the
binders SYNTHESIZE at AJC's headline hypotheses. The probe passed. The probe's comment said
'-- LocallyOfFiniteType must come from smoothness by SYNTHESIS'.

It did not. The probe's hypothesis list also contained [IsProper C.hom], and in mathlib
IsProper extends LocallyOfFiniteType (Proper.lean:42). Properness supplied it; smoothness was
inert. A passing probe over a hypothesis BUNDLE tells you the bundle is sufficient. It tells
you nothing about WHICH member did the work, and the commit message, the roadmap comment, the
DM to a sibling team, and two docstrings all then asserted the wrong member -- five copies of
one unverified attribution, downstream of one green check.

The cheap discipline: when you claim 'hypothesis H is free because it follows from H2',
elaborate the probe with H2 present and H absent AND with H2 absent. One extra 30-second
elaboration. If you only ever add hypotheses to a probe until it goes green, you learn
sufficiency and mistake it for necessity.

Corollary worth keeping separately: 'these are exactly the hypotheses the headline already
carries' is a claim about the headline, so check it against the headline's actual signature
(here WeilDivisor.lean:1161), not against a bundle you assembled yourself.

local_inbox.body:
[persistent] THE CONVERSE OF I-0349: a docstring that says a gate is OPEN is not evidence it still is — and this drift is measurably the most frequent defect in this workspace

Established by the janitor hygiene pass of run 0054 s0006, counting the actual defect
population rather than reasoning about it. `I-0349` warns that a docstring listing a
declaration is no evidence the declaration exists. **The opposite direction is more common
here and nobody was guarding it**: prose asserting "this class carries no instance", "the
frontier is these N leaves", "nothing produces this statement", left behind by the very
session that closed the thing.

THE COUNT, all on 2026-07-27, all in the AJC project, all filed as separate issues:

- `I-0385` — two docstrings said `HasFiniteMapToP1` / `ExistsNonconstantMapToP1` "carry no
  instance"; both had had proved instances for some time.
- `I-0420` — `hasRigidPushforward_of_leaves` advertised "the exact remaining frontier ...
  four named leaves"; two of the four were already theorems.
- `I-0428` — SIX sites in one cone said "no instances anywhere" / "one statement remains"
  the same day a global instance closed the gate. Third consecutive round of the same defect
  on one task.
- `I-0436` — three false comment blocks survived in the ONE file the fixing task could not
  edit (the root roll-up, another team's write set).
- `informal/pic-representability-campaign.md` — the campaign plan's own gate table still
  said "there is deliberately no instance", and its trap list still said THREE traps when
  the project had measured five.

WHY IT HAPPENS, mechanically. A gate discharge is a *local* edit — one new instance in one
new module — but the claim it falsifies is *distributed*: every consumer docstring, the
module docstring above it, the campaign plan, the axiom-probe section header, the root
roll-up's import comment, and the hgraph node synced from the docstring. Nothing links them,
so the closing session sees a green build and a correct new file.

WHY IT IS EXPENSIVE, and it is not symmetric with `I-0349`. Both directions mislead a
reader, but this one misleads the *planner*: "the frontier is four leaves" is the sentence a
later session quotes when budgeting, and it over-counts remaining work by a factor. Two
sessions were briefed against stale frontier counts before this was noticed. Over-counting
open work is the failure that wastes a lane; under-counting merely wastes a grep.

THE DISCIPLINE, for the session that closes a gate — cheap, and it is your job, not the
janitor's:

    grep -rn '<GateName>' <project> --include=*.lean --include=*.md --include=*.tex

Read every hit, not just the file you edited. Include `informal/`, `scripts/`, the root
roll-up module, and the blueprint. Any hit that describes the gate's STATUS (rather than
using it) is now suspect. A hit in a file outside your write set is an inbox ask to its
owner in the same session — do not leave it, and do not assume the owner will notice.

COROLLARY FOR MEMORY ITEMS THEMSELVES. `I-0381` recorded "the frontier is FOUR statements",
was corrected to ONE, then to zero — wrong twice in one day, in the same direction. Do not
put a frontier COUNT in a durable memory. Record the technique and the tooling; point at the
roadmap row for the count, which is the thing designed to be re-set.

A CLEAN `#print axioms` LINE LIES IN EIGHT DISTINCT WAYS — the workspace catalogue, keyed to `scripts/axiom-frontier.lean`

All eight measured in `Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge`, not hypothesised. The probe is the authority and its **section headers** are the content — do not read only its output lines. **Do not quote the number of traps from this item**: it grew 3 → 5 → 6 → 8 in four days, and per `I-0439`'s corollary a durable memory must not carry a count that a live lane can falsify. Read the probe's section headers for the current list.

      `[HasPicScheme C]` reports clean axioms, because the caller discharges the hypothesis. The
      leak appears one step later, where Lean must synthesize and the only producer is
      sorry-bodied. Measure with a `leakProbe`/`leakControl` pair: identical conclusion and proof
      term, differing only in whether the instance is synthesized. (§8)
  (b) **An UNPROVED named hypothesis in the statement.** Invisible. Most of the cluster-P vanishing
      lane is clean and carries the closed χ-ledger as a hypothesis. (§6b, §6d)
  (c) **A FALSE named hypothesis.** Worse: the theorem is vacuously true and reports clean like any
      other. Happened on the `hrank` leaf, refuted by `O_{P^1_A}/x`. The cure is a non-vacuity
      witness — exhibit an object satisfying the hypotheses and fire the theorem at it. (§6c)
  (d) **An INSTANCE BINDER nothing can instantiate for the ambient object.** The obligation sits in
      square brackets, so it is a hypothesis, so the axiom line is clean and always will be.
      `hasRationalResidues_of_isAlgClosed` had three such binders, two with no producer for a bare
      `Scheme`; an instance for a more structured cousin (`Over (Spec k)` rather than `Scheme`) is
      WORSE than none, because the grep succeeds. (§6e)
  (e) **An UNROOTED module is not probed at all:** `import AlgebraicJacobian` never reaches it, so no
      `#print axioms` line for its declarations can even be written, and nothing warns.
  (f) **AN INSTANCE DIAMOND**, where two non-definitionally-equal instances can supply the same
      binder, so a file proves correct-looking theorems about a definition pinned to the wrong one.
      This defeats an instantiability check too, because the binders *do* synthesise. The tell is a
      cross-file identity that ought to be `rfl` and is not. Absorbed from `I-0432`; met in the wild
      and now documented at `RiemannRoch/Adelic/ResidueField.lean:786-800` — explicit
      `[Algebra k C.left.functionField]` binders vs the scoped `Scheme.functionFieldAlgebra`, where
      the error message names `chi` rather than the instance. Note `open scoped AlgebraicGeometry`
      alone does not activate it; only `open scoped AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme` does.
  (g) **A REFUTABLE hypothesis** — sharper than (c), because the falsity is *derivable in-tree*: the
      project proves `H → C` and, at every instance anyone would use, `¬H`. The theorem is true,
      axiom-clean, instantiable, consistent, non-vacuous by every probe, and empty. Measured on the
      χ-ledger's `hbump` (probe §2b): iterating it down the anti-effective cone forces `h¹` to grow
      linearly, so it is false on every bounded-`h¹` cover and outright false at `U₀ = U₁ = ⊤` once
      one prime divisor exists. A consistency witness exists (`bump_of_isEmpty_primeDivisor`, on a
      scheme with no prime divisors) and proves nothing. **The only check that finds this**: read the
      PRODUCER's side conditions and ask whether the family the hypothesis quantifies over contains
      a member whose negation the tree proves. Corollary, absorbed from `I-0451`: when a hypothesis
      turns out usable *more generally* than believed, audit the widened quantifier for members
      where the project derives the negation — widening one reading can make it strictly stronger
      exactly where the project can prove the opposite.
  (h) **A HYPOTHESIS EQUIVALENT TO ITS OWN CONCLUSION**, and this is the one to check FIRST because it
      costs a single `rw` attempt. `chi_eq_of_bump` proves `hbump → closed ledger`; the converse is
      three lines (`rw [hledger (pointDivisor P + E), hledger E, degK_add, degK_pointDivisor]; ring`)
      because `degK` is an `AddMonoidHom` and the bump adds exactly one point. A theorem `A → B`
      whose converse is trivial transports no information: it is a restatement, and "is `A`
      satisfiable" *is* "is `B` satisfiable". Absorbed from `I-0456`. **Before believing that
      `H → C` reduces `C` to `H`, try to prove `C → H`.** Two further notes from the same audit:
      "is `H` consistent" is nearly always answerable degenerately and nearly always worthless — the
      informative question is WHERE `H` is false; and a *conditional* refutation (one taking the
      thing it refutes as a hypothesis, as `not_bump_of_notMem_overlap` does with `hchiAdd`) is much
      weaker than an unconditional one, so do not read the first as the second. (probe §2c)

  (i) **A SORRY-BODIED INSTANCE THE `declaration uses sorry` CENSUS DOES NOT SEE, and its cure's
      own trap.** Two faces of one mechanism, absorbed from `I-0530` and `I-0526` (both archived).
      *The census undercounts:* it flags an instance only if the instance's BODY contains `sorry`.
      `instHasPicSchemeEt` has body `(fgaPicardRepresentability C).1` — an open obligation — and
      emits NO warning. Measured cost: `Pic0SchemeEt` was declared without a `[HasPicSchemeEt C]`
      binder, synthesis fired at elaboration and baked `sorryAx` into the DEFINITION, so every
      theorem about it leaked while `PicSchemeEt` one level up (which takes the binder) stayed
      clean; four "PROVED unconditionally" docstrings were wrong. Check: `#print axioms` the
      DEFINITION, not only theorems about it, and compare against the same declaration with the
      gate as an explicit binder — clean-with-binder plus dirty-without is the signature. Rule:
      every definition downstream of a gate whose only producer is sorry-bodied must take the gate
      as a BINDER; parametricity is lost silently at the first declaration that omits it. Never
      quote "zero sorry-bodied instances" as "no synthesis leak".
      *The cure is one keyword, and it can make the probe go vacuously clean:* de-instancing
      (`instance` -> `theorem` + `haveI` at the real consumers) makes `inferInstance` FAIL, so the
      dependency must be named and appears in the proof term; cost zero (AJC stayed green at 8762
      jobs, commits `df899aa50`, `519eecb15`). But `leakProbe_pullback_finiteLimits` was built on
      the IDENTITY morphism, and after de-instancing it went from `sorryAx` to CLEAN — because for
      the identity the pullback IS the identity functor (`Scheme.Modules.pullbackId`) and synthesis
      found a cheaper clean route. A probe on a DEGENERATE argument measures the intended
      declaration only until the instance graph changes. Hence the two standing defences in
      `scripts/axiom-frontier.lean`: probe over a GENERAL argument and NAME the carrier, and ship a
      CONTROL that must come out the other way. **If a control and its probe ever agree, the
      measurement is broken, not the mathematics.** Distinct from the sorried-DEFINITION trap
      (`abelJacobi`, `ajc-albanese`, same day), where no synthesis is involved and the leak is
      visible in the term.
  (j) **A GATE CLASS THAT ONLY ASSERTS INHABITATION** — the exact dual of (d), and it reads
      identically in the axiom line. Absorbed from `I-0536` (archived). (d) is a binder NOTHING can
      instantiate; this is a binder ANYTHING can. `PicScheme.ClassDegree` is literally
      `Nonempty (relPicClasses ->+ Z)`; that type contains `0`, so `<<0>>` proves it with no
      hypothesis, and `degreeOfSection` built on it is not pinned to the degree — the "one remaining
      input" demanded nothing. Fine: `HasPicScheme` asserts a PROPERTY of the object
      (`exists X, RepresentableBy X and LocallyOfFiniteType and IsSeparated`). Vacuous:
      `Nonempty (A ->+ B)`, `Nonempty (A -> Z)`, `Nonempty (A ~= B)` whenever `B` has a point.
      Probe: restate the class as a `theorem` with no gate and try `<<0>>` / `<default>` /
      `<fun _ => 0>`. Live instance: issue `I-0534`.

HOW TO CHECK, and it is the only way that works: **ELABORATE A CONSUMER**, do not read the
signature. Write an `example` with only the hypotheses you claim to need, apply the theorem, and
see whether it compiles. Reading binders tells you what is asked for; only elaboration tells you
what can be supplied.

WORKED PAIR, which is why (d) is worth stating rather than just avoiding:
`hasRationalResidues_of_isAlgClosed` and `hasRationalResidues_of_isAlgClosed_curve` have the SAME
axiom line. One is a relocation of the obligation, the other a genuine discharge. Both are
probed side by side in §6d/§6e. The axiom line was never what distinguished them.

CITATION HYGIENE, which recurred in the (h) audit: prose citations across module boundaries should
be `#check`-ed, not remembered. `primeDivisorOfNotGeneric` was cited as "producing a real prime
divisor on a curve"; the cited path does not resolve (it is `AlgebraicGeometry.Adelic.…`), and the
declaration *consumes* a non-generic point rather than producing one. A producer that consumes its
own precondition is not a non-vacuity witness.

COROLLARY FOR COUNTING: count probe output by ENTRY, not by LINE. Lean wraps a long axiom list
across several lines, so a per-line filter misclassifies exactly the declarations whose lists are
longest. A published count of "41 clean, 35 leaking of 66" survived a session in this project
without anyone noticing it does not add up.

ABSORBED THE DIAGNOSTIC HALF OF MEMORY `I-0465`, which I archived in the same pass (janitor hygiene pass, run 0055). Its mathematical half — the two-set-cover $\chi$ formula — is already the module docstring of `AlgebraicJacobian/RiemannRoch/Adelic/ChiUnconditional.lean:19-35`, so only this half needed a home, and it belongs with modes (g) and (h).

**HOW TO ATTRIBUTE A REFUTATION, i.e. what "$H$ contradicts $T$s conclusion" actually licenses.** Three sessions plus an independent audit concluded "`hbump` is refutable off the cover overlap". The derivation was valid; the ATTRIBUTION was not, because it ran through `ChiLedger.chi_add`. When a hypothesis $H$ and a theorem $T$s conclusion are incompatible on some region, what you have learned is that **$H$ and $T$s hypotheses cannot both hold there** — deciding which one gives way needs an INDEPENDENT computation of the same quantity.

Here the ungated formula supplied exactly that independent computation, and the outcome is worth recording because it went the *other* way from what the intermediate correction predicted: `chi_le_finrank_chart_along_tower` / `not_bump_of_notMem_left` (`ChiUnconditional.lean` §5) show that along the tower $n\cdot P$ both $\Gamma(U_0,-)$ and $\mathcal{A}$ freeze while $\Gamma(U_1,-) \subseteq \mathcal{A}$ stays trapped, so $\chi$ is BOUNDED against `hbump`s linear growth $n\cdot[\kappa(P):k]$. So `hbump` is unconditionally false off a chart, and the file states this as *strengthening* the `I-0449` audit from conditional to unconditional rather than overturning it.

Reading rule: **do not read "$H$ contradicts $T$s conclusion" as "$H$ is false"** — and equally, do not read an intermediate re-attribution as a rehabilitation of $H$. Only an independent computation settles it. This is the diagnostic companion to mode (g) (a refutable hypothesis) and mode (h) (a hypothesis equivalent to its conclusion); note the interaction between `I-0466` and the `I-0467`/`I-0468` audit threads, which is this rule being applied twice in opposite directions on the same hypothesis.

Also preserved from `I-0465`, the FORMALIZATION heuristic that produced the independent computation: a long exact sequence is how one proves an Euler-characteristic identity in general, but for a length-1 Čech complex the identity is inclusion-exclusion on two subspaces, i.e. a lattice fact (`Submodule.finrank_sup_add_finrank_inf_eq`). When stuck constructing a connecting homomorphism, check whether the INDEX SET is small enough that the alternating sum is a modular-law computation instead.

From `I-0530` (`ajc-etale-pic`, run 0066), measured on `Picard/Pic0Et.lean`.

The project's standing census — grep the build log for `declaration uses sorry`, then check which carriers are declared `instance` — counts an instance only if its **body** contains `sorry` directly. `instHasPicSchemeEt` (`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`) has body `(fgaPicardRepresentability C).1`, citing the project's one open obligation: **no warning is emitted**, so the census reports zero while a live leak sits in the tree.

What it cost: `Pic0SchemeEt` was declared *without* a `[HasPicSchemeEt C]` binder, the instance fired at elaboration and baked `sorryAx` into the **definition**, so every theorem about the object reported `sorryAx` however clean its own argument was — while `PicSchemeEt` one level up, which does take the binder, stayed clean. Four docstrings claiming "PROVED unconditionally" were wrong; a Ground review caught it.

**The check:** run `#print axioms` on the **definition**, not only on theorems about it, and compare against the same declaration with the gate as an explicit binder. *Clean-with-binder plus dirty-without* is this leak's signature. After adding the binder, `Pic0SchemeEt` and its four theorems all report `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`.

## MODE (j) — de-instancing a leak can make the PROBE that measured it go vacuously clean, which reads as progress

From `I-0526` (`ajc-fbc`, run 0068, commits `df899aa50` and `519eecb15`).

- **The fix half, which is right and cheap.** A sorry-bodied *instance* is qualitatively worse than a sorry-bodied theorem, and the repair is one keyword. As an instance, `pullback_preservesFiniteLimits` was found by synthesis anywhere in scope, so a declaration that merely *quantified* over it reported clean axioms while every synthesis site silently acquired `sorryAx` — contamination with no textual trace. Change `instance` to `theorem` and cite it with `haveI` at its real consumers: `inferInstance` then **fails** to synthesise and the dependency appears in the proof term. Cost was zero (root build stayed green at 8762 jobs). Do it the moment a sorried instance is introduced.
- **The trap half.** `scripts/axiom-frontier.lean` measured that leak with `leakProbe_pullback_finiteLimits (S) : PreservesFiniteLimits (Scheme.Modules.pullback (𝟙 S)) := inferInstance`, using the **identity** morphism because `Flat (𝟙 S)` synthesises for free. After de-instancing, the probe went from `sorryAx` to **clean** — not because anything was proved, but because for the identity the pullback *is* the identity functor (`Scheme.Modules.pullbackId`) and synthesis found a different, clean route. A session reading the diff would have seen a leaking line go clean and reported a closure that never happened.
- **The general trap:** a probe built on a **degenerate argument** (identity, terminal object, trivial ring) measures the intended declaration only as long as no cheaper instance path exists. Change the instance graph and the probe silently starts measuring something else.
- **Two defences:** measure the non-instance at a real (non-degenerate) argument; and always ship a **control that must come out the other way** (`leakControl_pullback_finiteLimits_given_monos`, `leakControl_pullback_monos_openImmersion`). If a control and its probe ever agree, the measurement is broken, not the mathematics.

## One distinction both items make, worth keeping

Sorried **instance** = invisible contamination at use sites. Sorried **definition** (the `abelJacobi` case `ajc-albanese` reported the same day) = no synthesis involved, the leak is in the term, but the statement does not say what it appears to say. A `sorry` count misses both; `#print axioms` at a **use site** catches both.

[persistent] MATHLIB DOES CARRY A RELATIVE-DIMENSION BRIDGE, via the rank of Omega rather than a tangent space -- and 'mathlib has no API for this' was asserted about it twice

Found by ajc-truth (run 0054 s0008) while writing a docstring that claimed the opposite, and
worth recording because the shape of the error recurs in this workspace.

THE FACT. AJC's leaf B needs SmoothOfRelativeDimension (genus C) (Pic0Scheme C).hom, and the
natural evidence available is a TANGENT SPACE dimension: dim_{kappa(e)} T_e Pic0 = genus C
(now proved at the headline, finrank_tangentSpace_pic0_eq_genus). It is easy to conclude that
mathlib offers nothing, because SmoothOfRelativeDimension is DEFINED by local standard-smooth
presentations and mentions no tangent space anywhere. I wrote 'it carries no bridge in either
direction, so this step is missing mathematics' and that is false.

The bridge is at the ALGEBRA level and through a DIFFERENT INVARIANT:

  Algebra.IsStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension.rank_kaehlerDifferential
    [Nontrivial S] [IsStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension n R S] : Module.rank S Omega[S/R] = n
  Algebra.IsStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension.iff_of_isStandardSmooth
    [Nontrivial S] [IsStandardSmooth R S] (n) :
      IsStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension n R S <-> Module.rank S Omega[S/R] = n

(RingTheory/Smooth/StandardSmoothCotangent.lean, mathlib v4.31.) The second is an IFF, so it
converts relative dimension into a rank computation in both directions.

WHY THE SEARCH MISSES IT, which is the transferable part. Grepping SmoothOfRelativeDimension
for 'tangent' or 'finrank' returns nothing, and that is a true fact about the name. The bridge
does not mention tangent spaces because it is stated in the invariant mathlib actually uses for
smoothness -- the module of Kaehler differentials. So the real obligation is not 'construct a
bridge' but 'translate between two invariants': rank Omega versus dim of the tangent space,
dual to each other over a field, plus the affine-local-to-scheme-level passage.

THE GENERAL LESSON. When a needed statement seems absent, check whether the library states the
same mathematics in a DIFFERENT INVARIANT before recording it as missing. Tangent space vs
Omega, dimension vs rank, cotangent vs derivations -- these are the same content under names
that share no substring. 'No lemma mentions X and Y together' is evidence about vocabulary, not
about mathematics. Related: [[I-0439]] (prose asserting a gate is open after it closed) and
[[I-0445]] (published counts nobody can re-derive) are the same defect class -- a checkable
claim recorded in a form that cannot be checked.

local_inbox.body:
A GAP CAN LIVE IN A HYPOTHESIS'S QUANTIFIER, NOT IN MISSING MACHINERY -- and a CORRECT obstruction argument can point at the wrong thing

AJC cluster P carried 'the closed chi-ledger reaches only the effective cone; the negative part
needs an input the lane does not have' across THREE sessions -- a module docstring, four sibling
docstrings, a roadmap summary, an inbox item. It was false. chi_eq_of_bump (run 0055 s0008)
proves the ledger at EVERY Weil divisor from the same one-point bump that gave the effective cone.

WHY IT SURVIVED. The gap shipped with a proof sketch that is entirely CORRECT:
  - write D = D+ - (-D)+ as a difference of effective divisors;
  - the effective case handles each piece;
  - but chi is NOT additive in the divisor, and D is NOT linearly equivalent to D+, so neither
    of the lane's two transport mechanisms moves chi across the decomposition.
Every clause true. It even names the two candidate tools and correctly rules both out. Each
session re-derived it, found it sound, moved on.

What nobody questioned was the SHAPE of the hypothesis already in hand. hbump reads
  forall (P : PrimeDivisor) (E : WeilDivisor), chi (pointDivisor P + E) = chi E + residueDeg P
quantified over EVERY base divisor E, not just effective ones. So the telescope never had to
start at 0. Read the same identity as D+ = (-D)+ + D: the effective divisor (-D)+ telescoped
ONTO the base D. One induction (chi_telescope_list_add), compare with the effective-cone value
of chi(D+), done. No transport of chi across anything, and no new machinery.

THE MOVE TO REMEMBER: when a gap says 'we lack machinery M to get from A to B', before hunting
for M, re-read the QUANTIFIERS of the hypotheses you already have. Ask: at which arguments have
I been instantiating this, and at which am I ENTITLED to? A hypothesis quantified more

nothing about whether it addresses the real question. When you inherit a gap with a good
argument attached, check what the argument is ABOUT before trusting its conclusion.

NON-VACUITY IS THE WRONG QUESTION FOR A HYPOTHESIS THAT IS EQUIVALENT TO ITS CONCLUSION

Durable lesson from auditing AlgebraicGeometry.Adelic.chi_eq_of_bump (AJC, LedgerClosure.lean).

The pattern. A session proves `hbump -> closed ledger`, presents it as closing an open item, then worries (correctly, and to its credit) whether hbump might be vacuous. Both the claim and the worry miss the real defect: hbump and the closed ledger are EQUIVALENT. The converse is three lines
  rw [hledger (D+P), hledger D, degK_add, degK_pointDivisor]; ring
because degK is an AddMonoidHom and the bump adds exactly one point. A theorem `A -> B` where `B -> A` is trivial transports no information; it is a restatement. No axiom check, no elaboration probe, and no vacuity check detects this, because the theorem is true, clean and instantiable. It is the re-indexing failure mode of I-0399 at one level of remove: not `Iff.rfl` dressed as content, but a genuine one-directional proof of something whose other direction is free.

The check to run before claiming a hypothesis-elimination is progress: TRY TO PROVE THE CONVERSE. If it takes three lines, you reformulated, you did not reduce. Cheap, decisive, and applies to every `..._of_bump`-shaped restatement.

Second lesson, on how to answer a vacuity question properly. "Is H consistent" is nearly always answerable degenerately (empty index type, trivial object) and is nearly always worthless. The informative questions are:
  - is H equivalent to its own conclusion (above);
  - WHERE is H false? Deriving explicit refutations bounds the region where H could hold and so measures what is actually left open. For hbump: an unconditional proof that h1 must grow linearly on the anti-effective cone, hence hbump fails on every bounded-h1 cover and outright at the degenerate cover U0=U1=top once a single prime divisor exists. That is a far sharper description of the residual leaf than "consistent, vacuously".
A conditional refutation (one taking the thing it refutes as a hypothesis, as not_bump_of_notMem_overlap does with hchiAdd) is much weaker than an unconditional one; do not read the first as the second.

Third, a citation hygiene point that recurred here. Docstrings cited `ResidueField.primeDivisorOfNotGeneric` as "producing a real prime divisor on a curve". The name does not resolve (no such namespace; it is AlgebraicGeometry.Adelic.primeDivisorOfNotGeneric), and the declaration takes a non-generic POINT as input rather than producing one — the existence proof is real but sits in a `private lemma` (exists_pole, NonconstantToP1.lean) and is unexported. Prose citations across module boundaries should be #check-ed, not remembered; a producer that consumes its own precondition is not a non-vacuity witness.

AJCR IS NOT PORTABLE INTO AJC'S ADELIC LANE, AND ITS EXTENSION UNIFORMITY IS D=0 ONLY

Surveyed this run (0055 s0014) for task ajc-rr, so no future session needs to re-open the question.
Two separate lake packages; AJC does not depend on AJCR. Nothing is a drop-in import.

ABSTRACTIONS DO NOT MATCH. AJCR has no PrimeDivisor/WeilDivisor and NO Adelic/ folder at all. Its
divisor type is Scheme.CurveDivisor := {x // x != genericPoint X} ->0 Z (RiemannRoch/Divisor.lean)
and its RR machinery is sheaf-cohomology based (Sheaf.HModule, Sheaf.chi, divisorSheaf, CechPic).
AJC's Adelic layer carries sections as Submodule k X.functionField (sectionSub) with chi k U0 U1 D.
AJCR is architecturally closer to AJC's OLDER WeilDivisor.lean layer than to the Adelic layer.

THE THREE CLUSTER-P ITEMS, honestly:
1. Field-extension uniformity. AJCR PROVES IT ONLY FOR THE STRUCTURE SHEAF (D=0):
   finrank_h1_baseField / finrank_h0_baseField / genus_baseField
   (Cohomology/H1BaseFieldInvariance.lean:328-373), sorry-free. There is NO
   'dim_k L(D) = dim_K L(D_K)' for general D anywhere in AJCR -- CarveDegree.lean:96-99
   finrank_tensor_divisorSections is just Module.finrank_baseChange on K tensor L(D), NOT an iso
   K tensor L(D) ~= L(D_K) on the base-changed curve. So the task statement's framing is right:
   AJCR does not supply extension uniformity. Nobody should go looking for it there again.
2. UniformVanishing.lean's core is exists_bound_subsingleton_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1
   (line 71): needs an explicit finite dominant pi : Y -> P1 K supplied as a hypothesis, plus
   Module.Finite of H0/H1 of the structure sheaf. Same SHAPE as AJC's
   exists_bound_subsingleton_h1Mod but incompatible primitives: AJCR derives the bound
   geometrically from fiber-divisor positivity, AJC combinatorially from a ledger identity + Peel.
   Neither can import the other's proof text.
3. Principal degree zero. AJCR's deg_divOf (RiemannRoch/ChiLedger.lean) is sorry-free but does
   NOT go through finite-map-to-P1 pullback -- it telescopes its own chi-ledger by devissage over
   closed points. AJCR's pullback-degree lemma classDeg_cechPicMap_eq_finrank_mul
   (DegreePullback.lean:267-303, sorry-free) is the right SHAPE for AJC's open leaf but is stated
   over CechPic/CurveDivisor. Transferable as a proof STRATEGY only.

BOTTOM LINE for a future session: the only two genuinely transferable ideas are (a) the
two-cover-Cech-termwise-base-change technique for uniformity -- and note AJCR only ever ran it at
D=0, so even the idea is unproven for general D -- and (b) the finite-pullback degree
multiplicativity strategy for the principal-divisor leaf. Do not promise a mechanical port.

ABSORBED `I-0384` (janitor hygiene pass, run 0055 s0014), which I archived as a near-duplicate of this item. Both answered the same question — "can AJCR's Riemann-Roch lane be ported into AJC?" — and this item is the more complete of the two (it covers all three cluster-P items and pins the extension uniformity at $D=0$ only). Two findings of `I-0384` are **not** restated above, so they are preserved here:

- **The adelic form is sometimes CHEAPER, not merely different.** $\chi$ class-invariance is elementary subspace linear algebra in AJC (multiplication by $g$ maps sections onto shifted sections) and needs neither finiteness nor additivity of $\chi$, whereas AJCR's sheaf form needs the $\chi$ machinery even to *state* the transport. - **Extension uniformity in AJC is not merely unproved — it is not currently STATABLE.** Every adelic invariant is pinned on a chosen 2-affine cover (deliberately, to dodge the `HasCechToHModuleIso` gate), and `RiemannRoch/CurveBaseChange.lean` produces $C_\kappa$ as an AJC curve but does **not** transport the cover data. Anyone quantifying a bound over field extensions must first build the base-changed cover.

Cost/benefit measured by `I-0384`'s session, also kept: three modules (~1060 lines) rederived the $\chi$ class-invariance, the weighted degree, the drop bounds and the bounded-vanishing assembly. The parts that did **not** come across are exactly those with machinery behind them (AJCR's base $H^1$ vanishing from the FLV machine, its peel from `peel_effective` on `divisorSheaf`); those became named hypotheses in AJC. So AJC's vanishing lane is assembled but conditional, while its degree and drop lanes are unconditional.

THE CECH EULER CHARACTERISTIC OF A TWO-SET COVER NEEDS NO EXACT SEQUENCE -- and this lane spent four sessions gated on one

Durable lesson from AJC run 0055 s0014 (task ajc-rr).

THE FACT. AJC's Adelic lane built its chi-additivity (ChiLedger.chi_add) on a four-term exact
sequence 0 -> L(D')/L(D) -> A(D')/A(D) -> H1(D) -> H1(D') -> 0, carried as FOUR hypotheses
(window, connect, twist, right-exactness) because the lane never constructs the connecting
homomorphism. Every downstream chi statement inherited those binders, and the residual leaf
hbump was then a hypothesis nobody could discharge. All of it was avoidable. For a TWO-SET
cover:

  chi(D) = dim Gamma(U0,O(D)) + dim Gamma(U1,O(D)) - dim A(D)

because ell(D) = dim(S0 inf S1) (the cover identity) and h1(D) = dim A(D) - dim(S0 sup S1)
(rank-nullity on the SAME quotient), so chi = dim(S0 inf S1) + dim(S0 sup S1) - dim A, and the
MODULAR LAW (mathlib Submodule.finrank_sup_add_finrank_inf_eq) collapses the first two terms.
One mathlib lemma, no connecting map, no approximation input.

THE GENERALISABLE LESSON. A long exact sequence is how one PROVES an Euler-characteristic
identity in general, but for a length-1 Cech complex the identity is inclusion-exclusion on two
subspaces, and inclusion-exclusion is a lattice fact. When a formalization is stuck on
constructing a connecting homomorphism, check whether the INDEX SET is small enough that the
alternating sum is a modular-law computation instead. Nobody in four sessions asked that, because
the sheaf-cohomology framing makes the exact sequence look like the only route.

SECOND LESSON, ON DIAGNOSING A REFUTATION. Three sessions plus an independent audit concluded
'hbump is refutable off the cover overlap'. The derivation was valid and the attribution was
wrong: it ran through chi_add, so what it showed is that CHI_ADD'S HYPOTHESES are unsatisfiable
off the overlap. When a hypothesis H and a theorem T's conclusion are incompatible on some
region, you have learned that H and T's HYPOTHESES cannot both hold there -- deciding which one
gives way needs an independent computation of the same quantity. Here the ungated formula
supplied it: off the overlap the chi-jump is the surviving one-chart step, and hbump is
EQUIVALENT there to that step being full. Do not read 'H contradicts T's conclusion' as
'H is false'.

WHEN YOU OVERTURN AN AUDIT, RE-DERIVE THE AUDIT'S CONCLUSION IN YOUR NEW FRAMEWORK BEFORE DECLARING IT WRONG

From auditing AJC ChiUnconditional.lean, which correctly proved an ungated chi formula and then used it to declare I-0449's refutation of hbump a 'measurement of chi_add, not of hbump'. The formula was right; the reversal was wrong. Under the SAME hypotheses, the new formula reproves I-0449's conclusion and strengthens it from conditional to unconditional.

The mechanism of the error is worth naming, because it is a general one. The session derived a LOCAL identity -- 'off U0 the chi-jump is exactly the surviving U1-chart step' -- observed that this quantity is >= 0 rather than provably 0, and concluded 'so no contradiction, hbump survives here'. But a one-step identity constrains nothing on its own. The refutation lives in the TOWER: iterate the same bump n times. There S0 and A are frozen and S1 <= A, so chi is BOUNDED while hbump demands linear growth n.[k(P):k]. The one-step view cannot see this; the tower view closes it in twenty lines.

Rules that follow:
1. Before writing 'this overturns inbox I-xxxx', formalize I-xxxx's conclusion as a theorem in the NEW abstractions and try to prove it. If it compiles, you did not overturn it -- you strengthened it, and the docstring should say so. Cheap and decisive, the dual of I-0456's 'try to prove the converse'.
2. A local/one-step non-contradiction is not evidence of consistency for a hypothesis quantified over all divisors. Iterate it. Any hypothesis asserting a fixed positive jump per step is refuted by ANY uniform bound on the quantity being jumped -- look for the bound before believing the hypothesis.
3. Finiteness binders are not innocent bookkeeping in this lane. Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U D) at a NON-total open U is a strong assumption: for P.point notin U it forces ell(n.P + E) bounded in n (machine-checked), i.e. it forbids Riemann growth. Instance binders assumed 'for convenience' silently chose the geometry.
4. If a new Prop def is Iff.rfl to an existing hypothesis AND the existing theorem accepts it verbatim, the new theorem is a duplicate, not a reduction -- even if its docstring honestly admits it is a restatement. Admitting the failure mode in prose does not repair it; delete or fold into the original.

CHART-LEVEL Module.Finite AT A NON-TOTAL OPEN FORBIDS RIEMANN GROWTH -- and the bounded/unbounded distinction is what separates a live vanishing hypothesis from a dead ledger

AJC run 0055 s0014, task ajc-rr. Supersedes the chi-level framing in my earlier memory this
session: the root cause is one level lower and much simpler.

THE FACT (ell_le_finrank_chart_along_tower, Adelic/ChiUnconditional.lean, axiom-clean):

  ell(n.P + E) <= dim Gamma(U0, O(E))  for ALL n,  when P.point notin U0
                                                   and [forall D, Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U0 D)]

No cover hypothesis, no chi, no exactness datum. Proof is two steps: sectionSub k top D <=
sectionSub k U0 D (antitonicity in the open, since U0 <= top), and sectionSub k U0 is FROZEN along
the tower n.P because the point is off U0.

WHY IT MATTERS. Riemann-Roch says ell(D) grows like deg D. This says it CANNOT, along any tower at
a point missing a chart whose section spaces are finite-dimensional. So the innocuous-looking
binder [forall D, Module.Finite k (sectionSub k U D)] at a NON-TOTAL U is not bookkeeping -- it has
already excluded the curves Riemann-Roch is about. Prefer stating results at top, where
Module.Finite is the honest finiteness of L(D).

THE DISTINCTION THAT TOOK ME TWO WRONG TURNS TO FIND, and which is the generalisable payoff:

  a hypothesis equating chi (or ell) with an UNBOUNDED quantity -- e.g. hledger: chi(D) =
  chi(0) + degK D -- is REFUTED by any uniform bound on the left side;

  a hypothesis equating bounded with bounded -- a chart count = ell(D), or a subspace inclusion
  A(D) subseteq B(D) -- is untouched by the same argument.

So VANISHING content survives a boundedness argument and GROWTH content dies. I initially applied
the refutation too narrowly (only off the overlap, via chi_add), then too broadly (warning that my
own vanishing criteria were vacuous too). Both errors came from not asking 'is the right-hand side
bounded?'. Ask that first.

PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE FOR AJC, unchanged: hbump and hledger are false on a genuine two-chart cover
with finite-dimensional chart sections having a prime off a chart, so the hledger-conditional
results in SectionBounds section 3, BoundedVanishing and GlobalGeneration are vacuous there. Note
those consumers assume NEITHER a cover NOR chart-level finiteness -- they take arbitrary U0 U1 and
finiteness only at top -- so the refutation constrains which covers are usable rather than
refuting their hypotheses outright. Do not overstate it in either direction.

Cross-refs: [[one-step-non-contradiction-is-not-consistency]], [[ajc-adelic-ledger-refuted]].

## The rule, and it is audience/scope filtering rather than corruption

Sorting the open set by `(audience, scope.projects)` makes the boundary exact. An item is hidden from a team on project **P** iff any of:

1. `audience: human` — every one of `I-0372`, `I-0387`, `I-0481`, `I-0489`, `I-0502`, `I-0505` is hidden (6 of 18). These are the human-addressed reports, including this workspace's top open decision.

4. `audience: project:<other>` — `I-0319`.

So per-item this is *documented* behaviour (per-team ownership, project addressing). The defect is that the **advisory warning counts the whole store** while the list applies the filters, so the number an agent is told to act on includes items it cannot see, cannot open (`inbox show I-0408` fails with `I-0408 is not addressed to this team`), and cannot archive.

## The consequence that bit this pass, and the workaround

Two of the hidden items are `[persistent]` memories addressed to `horizon` — `I-0408` and `I-0430`. **A `[persistent]` memory nobody can open is not a memory.** I nearly made it worse by folding a visible item (`I-0520`) into the invisible `I-0408`, which would have buried both.

**Workaround for a janitor consolidating memory: check the merge TARGET is CLI-visible before folding anything into it.** One command:

```
horizon inbox list --status open --kind memory --limit 100 --json | jq -r .items[].id
```

A MECHANICAL AUDIT IS ONLY AS GOOD AS ITS DOMAIN: five domain-shrinking bugs in one 20-line check, each printing a clean-looking result -- and the check had "found" three defects where a human reader had already been right

AJC run 0054 s0014, task ajc-truth. This is the generalisable form of a lesson this project has now
paid for three times in three different tools.

THE CASE. Session 0012 published a \leanok-honesty check in scripts/axiom-frontier.lean: join every
proof-level \leanok in the blueprint against #print axioms, because the mark is local while the
defect (routing through a sorry) is transitive. Sound design. It reported THREE dishonest marks and
filed I-0473, with the method point "reading cannot audit this -- the audit by eye reported zero one
session before the join found three".

ALL THREE WERE ARTIFACTS. True count: ZERO, over 998 proof-level marks / 1073 pins. And the reading
it was contrasted against had been CORRECT: commit b61d416e9 states in as many words that
thm:pic0_smooth and thm:pic0_proper carry no \leanok in either position, having reverted exactly
that class of withdrawal one run earlier for the right reason.

THE FIVE BUGS, all in ~20 lines, every one of which printed a plausible "0 dishonest" or a
plausible defect list while examining a STRICT SUBSET of its domain:

  1. Required statement and proof to be TEXTUALLY ADJACENT (\end{theorem}\s*\n\s*\begin{proof}).
     Nodes routinely carry a % SOURCE comment block between them -> 452 of 1311 pinned pairs never
     examined.
  2. Given (1), the non-greedy (.*?) then reaches PAST the true \end{theorem} to find an adjacent
     pair, attributing a LATER node proof to an EARLIER node statement. This is what manufactured
     all three findings: the thm:pic0_smooth "statement" spanned NINE \labels and the \leanok found
     belonged to thm:pic0_geom_irred, which is proved and clean. 48 nodes mis-attributed.
  3. #print axioms on an absent name is an ERROR and lean halts at 100 -> silent truncation that
     reads as a complete run ("537 probed, 0 leaking").
  4. #print axioms prints a DIFFERENT SENTENCE for an axiom-free declaration -- "does not depend on
     any axioms", not "depends on axioms: [...]".
  5. split numbers past z: 1073 pins at 40/batch gives lk_aa..lk_az AND lk_ba, so a lk_a* glob
     skips the last 33. Plus the output log named /tmp/lk_all.txt was itself matched by that glob
     and re-ingested as a 1617-line "batch".

THE ACTIONABLE RULE. Give every mechanical audit an ARITHMETIC IDENTITY it must satisfy, asserted
IN CODE, relating what it examined to the size of its domain. Here: probed + unprobeable == pins.
Bugs 1-3 I found by looking at the code. Bugs 4 and 5 were found ONLY because that assertion
failed -- after I had read the code closely enough to publish it twice, and while I was in the act
of writing a correction to a finding about a parser losing pins. "It printed 0 defects" is not a
measurement; it is a statement that it printed.

SECOND-ORDER: I published the coverage figure wrong FIVE times (891, then "corrected" to 950/123,
finally 930/143 -- the original 143 was right and I corrected a right number to a wrong one). The
conclusion (zero) never moved and was reproduced four independent ways. What kept moving was the
claim about how much of the domain had been measured -- which is exactly the quantity the false
finding hinged on. When retracting a measurement error, the retraction is a measurement too.

AND THE ONE THAT STINGS: the check found "defects" precisely where a careful predecessor had
already looked and been right, and the finding was published with a moral about machines beating
reading. Before trusting a machine audit over a human audit trail, read the human trail -- it may
already contain the answer, with reasoning.

METHOD BOUND worth carrying: 143 of the 1073 pins name PRIVATE declarations, unaddressable by
#print axioms from outside their defining file. No single-file probe can audit those. State bounds
like that as bounds, not as clean results.

Cross-refs: [[leanok-honesty-needs-print-axioms]], I-0473, I-0474, commits 83de22eb3 745c121d3
443d9ee60 6a171e149.
