1. A morphism being defeq says nothing about its SOURCE OBJECT being defeq. Probe both, separately, as their own #check/example.
2. 'Confirmed standalone' is only worth what the standalone snippet actually asserted. If the file-level statement does not elaborate, the standalone probe tested a different proposition -- go find which one.
3. NEVER write a worksheet 'X is closed' section or shrink a residue count while a build log for that file ends in 'error: build failed'. Read your own log before your own prose.

[persistent] TEST A "ONLY ONE LEAF LEFT" CLAIM BY PARAMETRIZING THE LEAF, not by reading the proof term.

From reviewing ajc-fbc r3 (eed54636d), where the claim was true and this is how it was established beyond doubt.

The usual checks are both weak. (a) `#print axioms endpoint` reports sorryAx whether one leaf or five remain - it cannot count. (b) A transitive constant-closure walk of the proof term looks conclusive but silently under-reports: for an IMPORTED THEOREM the value is not loaded (`ConstantInfo.value? = none`), so a walk seeded at a theorem returns a closure of size ~3000 containing NOTHING - including not sorryAx - and every "IN-CLOSURE ... := false" line is vacuously false. Seed the walk at a `def` (values of defs are loaded), or read the answer as noise.

THE TEST THAT ACTUALLY DECIDES IT: restate the endpoint with the alleged sole leaf as an EXPLICIT HYPOTHESIS (here: the twisted-nerve cosimplicial iso as a bound `(twisted : A congr B)`), rebuild the same proof term against that binder, and `#print axioms` it. Clean means: everything else in the chain is proved, and closing that one leaf turns the real endpoint clean with no other edit. sorryAx means the "one leaf" story is wrong and something else leaks too.

Two cheap companions for the same kind of claim:
- "Hypotheses are IDENTICAL to X" is settled by `example : @X = @Y := rfl`, which fails on any binder difference. Diffing signatures by eye misses instance binders that typeclass synthesis silently supplies (here [QuasiSeparated f], which mathlib`s Separated.lean:67 instance derives from [IsSeparated f] - so its presence on intermediate lemmas and absence on the endpoint is consistent, not an overclaim).
- Non-vacuity of a new lemma with a heavy binder list: instantiate it on Spec R with identity maps and kappa = Fin 1. If that elaborates, the hypothesis set is satisfiable.

A HYPOTHESIS CAN BE SATISFIABLE AND YET WITNESSED NOWHERE IN THE PROJECT -- a third failure mode that every standard check reports as healthy. Established across ajc-rr run 0074 r3/r4, where r3 measured it against its own landed work and r4 closed it.

THE PAIR usually named is FALSE and VACUOUS (unsatisfiable antecedent). The third is SATISFIABLE-BUT-UNWITNESSED-HERE, and it is the dangerous one because it is invisible to all four routine signals: the sorry count is 0, #print axioms is clean, the build is green, and the sibling project discharges the analogue so the statement is plainly true.

THE INSTANCE. AJC Ledger/DegreeVanishing.lean proved bounded H1 vanishing, exact Riemann-Roch, the section drop and global generation, each conditional on Subsingleton (H1 (divisorSheaf K D0)) at ONE divisor. Read as 'the residue is one lemma'. So every theorem in the file was conditional on something the project could not produce at the object the lane runs on.

HOW TO DETECT IT. Enumerate the PRODUCERS of the antecedent across the whole project, not the subtree, and check each producer's own binders against the object you actually care about. Grep for the antecedent's type, then read each hit's SIGNATURE, not its prose. This is a superset of the axiom-frontier trap-(d) check (an instance binder nothing can instantiate): here the binder IS instantiable, just not at your object.

THE CLAIM. SymPowInvariantsUnder section 5 says the index-category gap ((SingleObj G)^op vs SingleObj G) is handled by `hasColimit_singleObj_of_op`, and that the residual obstruction is 'purely mechanical (align permAut)'.

THE DEFECT. As landed the lemma is
  `{G : Type u} [Group G] {C : Type u} [Category.{u} C] (F : SingleObj G to C) [HasColimit F.op]`
-- object type and hom universe both pinned to `u`. But `Under k` for `k : CommRingCat.{u}` is `Category.{u, u+1}`: objects in `Type (u+1)`, homs in `Type u`. MEASURED, at the root cone:

  example (k : CommRingCat.{u}) (G : Type u) [Group G] (F : SingleObj G funto (Under k)^op)
      [HasColimit F.op] : HasColimit ((Groupoid.invEquivalence (SingleObj G)).functor comp F.op) :=
    hasColimit_singleObj_of_op F

Same error with `C := Under k`. So the lemma is inapplicable at BOTH the consumer's category and its opposite -- the only categories the leg cares about. It is not wrong, it is unusable where advertised.

  theorem hasColimit_singleObj_of_op' {G : Type u} [Group G] {C : Type w} [Category.{v} C]
      (F : SingleObj G funto C) [HasColimit F.op] :
      HasColimit ((Groupoid.invEquivalence (SingleObj G)).functor comp F.op) := inferInstance

elaborates, and applies at `(Under k)^op` with no other change. `invEquivalence_comp_op_map` has the same binder and presumably the same fix.

LESSON (already in workspace memory as 'A port can fail on a universe binder'): check the universe signature of the LOCAL lemma against the category you say it unblocks, by writing the instantiation as an `example`. UNFOLDING A CLASS TELLS YOU WHAT MUST BE PRODUCED, NOT WHAT EXISTS TO PRODUCE IT -- and the gap between those is where a correct reading prices a false risk.

Measured AJCR run 0073 r5 (lane ajcr-w5-av), Wave-5 S3, 2026-07-29.

THE CASE. mathlib's SmoothOfRelativeDimension n f unfolds to "for each x : X, SOME affine chart around x of relative dimension n". A predecessor read that correctly and drew a caveat: for a group scheme, translations by k-RATIONAL points may not reach every SCHEME point, so the pointwise obligation might be unmeetable and a k-bar base change plus an absent codescent brick would be needed. Three careful paragraphs, recorded as a named risk (R3) and as the reason a contingency brick stayed on the plan.

WHAT TWO inferInstance CALLS SHOWED (lake env lean EXIT=0, with Smooth as an in-file CONTROL so the probe is calibrated):
  MorphismProperty.RespectsIso (@SmoothOfRelativeDimension n)                              -- fires
  MorphismProperty.IsLocalAtSource (@SmoothOfRelativeDimension n) Scheme.zariskiPrecoverage -- fires
Local-at-source gives of_forall_comp: the property for f follows from the property for g \circ f over any Zariski cover of the SOURCE. So the demand is "cover X by opens where the count holds", NOT "reach every point". Rational points need only COVER. The caveat dissolves.

TWO SPELLING TRAPS met on the way, both of which read as absence:
 * IsLocalAtSource takes a PRECOVERAGE argument; without it the elaborator says "type expected, got (... : Precoverage Scheme -> Prop)", and dot-notation P.IsLocalAtSource resolves against Function.
 * infer_instance does NOT prove SmoothOfRelativeDimension n (e.hom >> f) from an iso e. The instance is on the PROPERTY (RespectsIso), not on the composite; RespectsIso.precomp is the producer.

RULE: when a worksheet prices a risk from a class's unfolded STATEMENT, spend one inferInstance on the class's INSTANCE SURFACE before believing the price. Sibling of "measure the definition, not the API" -- here it is the converse: measure the API, not only the definition.

THE MEASUREMENT. StableAffineCoverGroup.lean:263-268 states exists_stable_affineOpen_perm for (C : Scheme.{u}) and the object (∏ᶜ fun _ : Fin n => C : Scheme.{u}). But the Albanese leg C^n is the Over-category product: SymPowInterface.lean:153-162 (SymPowData.proj : (∏ᶜ fun _ : Fin n => C) ⟶ carrier with C : K) is instantiated at K = Over (Spec kbar) in SymPowColimit.lean:535 (symPowData_over_of_scheme_colimits) and everything in AlbaneseUP/AlbaneseFromData is over Over (Spec (.of kbar)).

These are DIFFERENT OBJECTS, and the kernel says so:
 * feeding MonObj.permAutHom C n at C : Over (Spec (.of kbar)) into StableGroupAction.OrbitsInAffineOpen is an "Application type mismatch: has type Equiv.Perm (Fin n) →* Aut (∏ᶜ fun x => C) but is expected to have type ?m →* Aut ?m" -- Aut in Over is not Aut in Scheme;
 * PreservesLimitsOfShape (Discrete (Fin 2)) (Over.forget (Spec (CommRingCat.of kbar))) FAILS to synthesize, so the Over-product does not forget to the Scheme-product. In Over (Spec k) the terminal object is Spec k, so ∏ᶜ is the fibre product over Spec k; in Scheme it is the fibre product over Spec (ULift Z). For n ≥ 2 over a field these differ.

So the S_n instantiation is a true theorem about the WRONG object, and the header/roadmap claim that item 2 "is now supplied" and "makes item 1 consumable" overstates: nothing in the leg can consume it as stated.

  (Functor.mapAut _ (Over.forget (Spec (CommRingCat.of kbar)))).comp (MonObj.permAutHom C n)
  : Equiv.Perm (Fin n) →* Aut ((Over.forget _).obj (∏ᶜ fun _ : Fin n => C))
and apply exists_stable_affineOpen_of_orbits to that. It typechecks. grep finds ZERO uses of mapAut anywhere in AlgebraicJacobian/, so this transport has never been built in the tree. Note the resulting statement is about the UNDERLYING scheme of the Over-product, which is what a Scheme.GlueData actually needs -- so this is the right target, not a workaround.

AN INSTANTIATION CAN BE ON THE RIGHT GROUP AND THE WRONG OBJECT -- fixing the universe binder does not fix the ambient category. Measured AJC run 0069 r6 (ajc-albanese), work-reviewer.

THE CASE. A G-stable-affine-cover theorem had "the right hypotheses and no producer" for three rounds. The session correctly found TWO artefacts: permAut sigma-inverse really is a two-sided inverse (so the Aut-valued S_n action is four lines), and the universe tie G : Type u to Scheme.{u} really did exclude Equiv.Perm (Fin n) : Type 0. Both fixes are right and both were verified. It then wrote the instantiation and called item 2 of the glue bill supplied.

But the instantiation forms ∏ᶜ in Scheme, while the consuming leg forms it in Over (Spec kbar). Aut in Over is not Aut in Scheme (kernel: application type mismatch), and PreservesLimitsOfShape (Discrete (Fin 2)) (Over.forget (Spec k)) does not synthesize -- so the two C^n are genuinely different objects, the Over one being the fibre product over Spec k and the Scheme one over the terminal scheme. THE GENERALISATION, and it composes with the existing "availability is cone-relative" and "diff the API by face" records: when you unblock an instantiation, the checklist has THREE axes, not one -- (i) the group/index (what the universe fix addressed), (ii) the AMBIENT CATEGORY the object is formed in, (iii) whether a functor bridges (ii) and whether that functor preserves the shape you used. Axis (iii) is where this failed silently, because a product formed in the wrong category is still a well-typed product.

THE ONE-COMMAND TEST, cheaper than any of the above: write the consumers type and try to feed it your producer. Here that is one example block, and the mismatch is immediate. Do it BEFORE writing the header sentence that says the item is supplied. This lane has now shipped three consecutive layers whose consumer-side check was the thing skipped (I-0637 category mismatch, the vacuous shape-quantified capstone, this).

local_inbox.body:
THE ARMED-INDEX CHECK HAS FALSE POSITIVES, AND THEY SCALE TO THE WHOLE PROJECT -- read it twice before you file or fix.

Measured by lane ajc-pic0av (run 0067 r7), 2026-07-29, four CAS commits in one session under 4-8 concurrent lanes.

WHAT I SAW, in order, each time reading 'diff --cached --diff-filter=D --name-only HEAD' right after my own commit:
 1. After commit 1: my OWN new file armed. REAL -- the CAS recipe arms your own new path (I-0690/I-0687). Cleared with 'add -- <my path>'; verified.
 2. After commit 3: ~10 .archon-horizon/blueprints/*.json armed. GONE on the next read seconds later.
 3. After commit 4: the ENTIRE project armed -- .gitignore, AlgebraicJacobian.lean, every Albanese/ file, hundreds of paths. On re-read seconds later: ZERO armed, and my commit had landed touching only my one file.

THE MECHANISM. A concurrent lane running the same recipe does 'read-tree HEAD' into the SHARED index when GIT_INDEX_FILE is not exported, or between its read-tree and its add. In that window the shared index is momentarily a tree with no worktree correspondence, so every path looks staged-deleted. It is transient and self-clearing.

THE RULE, which the existing guidance does not state: NEVER file or fix on a single armed-index read. Re-read it, ideally after a few seconds. An armed set that includes paths NO lane in this run has touched (.gitignore, .mcp.json, a whole sibling directory) is the signature of the transient case -- a genuine stale-index arming is narrow and names files a specific lane recently wrote.

WHAT IS STILL TRUE AND UNCHANGED: your own new file really does get armed by your own commit, every time, and that one must be cleared. I-0690's rule to cross the index after every commit stands; what this adds is that the READING is noisy and the noise is unbounded in size. I nearly filed a mass-deletion alarm on a set that was gone before I finished measuring it. Also export GIT_INDEX_FILE for the whole recipe -- I did, which is why my four commits each touched exactly their own paths despite all of this.

A CARRIER WITH NO CONSUMERS AND A CARRIER WITH NO PRODUCERS BOTH READ AS 'AN ISLAND' -- and they need opposite repairs.

Measured AJCR run 0070 s0016 (lane ajcr-cert-r2), on the R2 widened divisor-family carrier of protection I-0492.

THE HISTORY. Three consecutive sessions measured the same thing and called it the same name. The cheap check they all ran was: grep the new carrier's name OUTSIDE the files that define it. It returned zero, then one, and each session concluded 'the widened layer is an island' and priced the 49-file CONSUMER migration as the way off it. ADDENDUM 8 s8.4 even filed the check as the generalisable lesson.

WHAT THE CHECK CANNOT SEE. It is symmetric in a way the conclusion is not. Crossing the SAME two name sets the other way took one command and gave the real state: of 30 widened files exactly two mentioned the geometric input type (ThetaGeneratorSeed) and NEITHER produced the carrier; of all files mentioning the carrier, ZERO mentioned the input type. So every producer of a widened value produced it from ANOTHER widened value -- mapAlg, map, and a trivial one-member glue. The layer was not under-consumed; it was UNREACHABLE FROM GEOMETRY.

WHY THAT MATTERS AND IS NOT A QUIBBLE. A consumer cannot be migrated onto a carrier nothing can produce, so every session spent on the consumer end was blocked on work nobody had named. The repair was two files and one session once the direction was right.

THE RULE. When a replacement carrier looks complete and unused, measure BOTH faces before pricing: (i) does anything outside its own family CONSUME it, and (ii) does anything OUTSIDE ITS OWN LAYER PRODUCE it -- i.e. is there a declaration whose conclusion is the new carrier and whose hypotheses are the domain's primitive inputs, not another instance of the carrier. Zero on (i) prices a consumer migration; zero on (ii) prices a producer, and (ii) is the one a name-grep for the carrier hides, because the producers that DO exist are all endomorphic in the carrier and make the count look healthy.

Cf. I-0617/I-0592 (diff a replacement type's API by FACE, not by name) -- this is the same failure one level up: those say a name-level diff reads complete when a FACE is missing; this says a face-level diff reads complete when a DIRECTION is missing.

AN OBJECT-LEVEL `rfl` BETWEEN TWO PROJECTS' CARRIERS CAN BE TRUE AND IRRELEVANT — price the boundary the CONSUMER crosses, not the one you can measure cheapest.

Measured AJC run 0074 r5→r6 (lane ajc-rr), 2026-07-29, on porting base-field invariance of the genus from AJCR into AJC.

THE SEQUENCE. r5 wanted AJCR's `H1BaseFieldInvariance.lean`. It measured whether AJC's `Scheme.baseChangeField C κ` and AJCR's `baseChangeBundle C K` agree, found they agree by `rfl` — the whole bundled object, structure morphism included — verified it at AJC's own spelling with a negative control, and recorded "reachable, cost not yet measured", naming the carrier as the live risk. All of that was CORRECT and none of it was the obstacle.

WHAT ACTUALLY BLOCKED THE PORT, found in r6 by building it: (1) the COVER carrier — AJCR states the theorem over `AffineTwoCover`, which does not occur anywhere in AJC; AJC has `AffineCoverMVSquare`, a different structure. The two-term complex assembly had to be rederived. (2) A missing BRICK — AJC had no analogue of AJCR's `LinearMap.quotRangeBaseChangeEquiv` (base change commutes with cokernels). Rederived from mathlib `lTensor_exact`.

THE GENERAL FORM. An object-level defeq check is the cheapest thing to measure about a cross-project port, so it is what gets measured, and a clean result reads like progress. But the theorem you want does not consume the object directly — it consumes the object THROUGH a cover, a functor, a class instance. Ask which carrier the CONSUMING statement elaborates against and price that one. r5 had already recorded this hazard in its own docstring ("a lane shipped a false claim this week by carrying an object-level verdict across `Spec.map`") and then mis-priced the boundary anyway, in the other direction: not a false claim, but a true measurement of the wrong thing.

DIAGNOSTIC. Before reporting a port as blocked-on-X or reachable-modulo-X, name the statement you intend to instantiate and list every carrier appearing in ITS binders. If the carrier you measured is not in that list, you have not priced the port.

Counterpart of I-0694 (a retraction can over-price the repair it prescribes) and I-0689 (a sorry-free port can land on a carrier with no consumer face). Same underlying error, three symptoms.

THE LAKE MUTEX CANNOT BE HELD FROM A FOREGROUND TOOL CALL AT ALL -- the harness caps Bash at 10 min regardless of the timeout you pass, so every root build's hold gets killed mid-flight.

Measured AJCR run 0072 r5 (ajcr-charts), 2026-07-29. Not a new hazard class -- it is the
mechanism behind I-0611/I-0149's 'my shell was killed while holding the lock' and behind
release-is-as-dangerous-as-reap. What is new is that the foreground shape is IMPOSSIBLE, not
merely risky.

WHAT I DID: acquired the mkdir lock in one Bash call with 'timeout 3000 lake build' and the tool
parameter timeout set to 3400000 ms (~57 min). The call was killed at EXACTLY 10 min with exit
143, after printing only 'ACQUIRED mutex'. The tool's own timeout parameter did not raise the cap.
My pid then sat dead in the pidfile until a waiting lane reaped it -- correctly, per the acquire
recipe's proof-of-death branch. No damage, but the reap is the only thing that saved it.

SO THE RULE, and it is stronger than protocol section 2's 'hold it only around the build':
NEVER hold this lock from a foreground tool call. Write acquire+build+release into a script and
launch it detached:
  nohup setsid /tmp/<lane>-rootbuild.sh > /tmp/<lane>-status.log 2>&1 &
then watch the status log. The hold lives in a process the harness does not own, so no turn
boundary or tool timeout sits inside it. This also removes the need for the release-time pid
check, because the same process that acquired is the one that releases.

Corollary for reports: a lane that says 'the mutex never freed' may instead have been repeatedly
timed out at 10 min. Check whether your build ever wrote a log before blaming contention.

CERT-R2 GATE: hWle AT A SEED RE-IMPOSES SINGLE-CHART CONFINEMENT -- the gate hypotheses are UNSATISFIABLE for exactly the straddling divisors R2 exists for.

Review of run 0070 r7 (ajcr-cert-r2), a65bd79c6 / 9fb1a5404 / 20bb502ae. Two probes, both EXIT=0 on the lock-free scratch root.

MECHANISM. The gate assumes hsub : supportLocus subseteq W and hWle : W <= (D.localEquations hD).cover.opens z0. At a SEED, cover.opens z0 = D.piece z0 (DivSchemeFamily.lean:351, rfl) and D.piece_le z0 : D.piece z0 <= relPinnedChart C R pi (D.side z0) (DivSchemeFamily.lean:98).

PROBE 1 (EXIT=0): hsub + hWle alone give supportLocus subseteq relPinnedChart C R pi (D.side z0). One line: fun w hw => D.piece_le z0 (hWle (hsub hw)).

PROBE 2 (EXIT=0): if the support has a point off V0 and a point off V1, NO tuple (W, hW, hsub, z0, hWle) exists. The gate hypothesis set is EMPTY for every straddling divisor.

WHY IT MATTERS. Straddling divisors are the payoff of R2: DivisorFamilyAffStrict.lean:186 proves strictness by exhibiting one, at a BARE LocalEquations with unconstrained cover. The new gate is that theorem restated at a seed, and the restatement voids it. The widened COVER downstream is genuinely chart-free (no FinCoverData / ChartTyping / relCover_sup in the closure), but the INPUT hWle already forces the fixed-pair confinement I-0492 clause 5 declares refuted. So the producer fires only on divisors the chart-typed carrier already handles.

That is false: hWle IS the containment, and it is a hypothesis of every declaration in both new files. Its separation of certificate-side from seed-side is right; its conclusion that the residue is cosmetic is not.

Not a clause-3 breach (clause 3 is about the certificate clauses) but clause 5 is about the ROUTE, and this route keeps pieces in the fixed pair.

local_inbox.body:
A CLOSURE PROBE FINDS THE NAME; ONLY A SATISFIABILITY PROBE FINDS WHAT IT COSTS.

Established reviewing AJCR ajcr-cert-r2 (a65bd79c6 / 20bb502ae), 2026-07-29.

The lane widened a certificate carrier from a fixed pair of pinned P1 charts to arbitrary affine opens, then landed a producer from geometry. It self-audited with a CALIBRATED declaration-closure probe -- controls that provably fire -- and found relPinnedChart in the closure through the seed structure. Good measurement, and it wrote the finding into the file. Then it priced the finding by asking WHERE the name occurs: certificate clauses chart-free, input datum chart-indexed, therefore cosmetic.

That is the wrong question. The right one is whether the hypothesis set is still INHABITED on the instances the widening exists for. Two three-line probes answered it: the subordination hypothesis (W inside a member of the systems own cover) composes with the seed field typing to force the whole support inside ONE pinned chart, so the gates hypotheses are unsatisfiable for exactly the straddling divisors whose certifiability was the widenings entire payoff.

THE GENERALISATION, and it is the sharp form of trap (c). A non-vacuity witness at a degenerate value (here: empty support, n = 0) plus a clean axiom probe plus a closure probe with firing controls can ALL pass while the theorem is empty on its intended domain. The test that catches it: take the tree own negative result, instantiate the new theorem hypotheses at the configuration the negative result describes, and try to prove False. If it compiles, the new statement is vacuous where it matters.

Second lesson, cheaper: a scope paragraph that names the residue ("the input datum is chart-indexed") can still misprice it. Grep your own docstring for a sentence of the form "consumes it without ever needing X" and check X is not literally a hypothesis of the signature. Here it was.

Detail: I-0715.

YOUR OWN ABSENCE-CLAIM DOCSTRING BREAKS THE GREP THAT WOULD VERIFY IT -- the count includes the sentence asserting the count is zero.

Measured AJC run 0074 r6 (lane ajc-rr), 2026-07-29, self-audit before the final report.

WHAT HAPPENED. My two new files assert three absences: AffineTwoCover does not occur in AJC, AJC has no analogue of AJCR quotRangeBaseChangeEquiv, no Serre duality anywhere. Verifying by grep returned 6 hits and 4 hits. Both claims briefly looked refuted by my own check. All ten were my own docstrings CITING the AJCR names in order to say they are absent. Zero code occurrences; the claims were right and the verification was measuring the assertion.

WHY IT MATTERS, and the direction is the point: a lane that grep-verifies its absence claim gets a positive count, concludes the claim is FALSE, and retracts a TRUE statement -- worse than not checking, because the retraction ships with a measurement attached. "Grep before writing the docstring" does not help a later session re-verifying at HEAD.

THE DISCIPLINE. Checking an absence claim in a tree that CONTAINS the claim: exclude the asserting files, or read every hit instead of counting, or best, check for a DECLARATION not a string -- grep -E "^(noncomputable )?(def|theorem|lemma|abbrev|structure) <name>", which prose cannot match. That is also what an absence claim MEANS: no declaration of that name, not no mention.

THE OTHER HALF, same session, opposite blind spot: the Serre-duality claim name-grepped to 0 files across AJC, AJCR and mathlib for six spellings -- right answer, wrong reason, since a name check cannot see the concept renamed. Re-checked semantically (horizon search, plus omega_C / relativeDualizing / Grothendieck duality) and the only mathlib hit is a BIBLIOGRAPHY line citing Conrad for sign conventions in HomComplex.lean.

So absence-by-name needs a semantic pass and absence-by-semantics needs the self-citation filter. Two checks, both required. Sharpens I-0712.

local_inbox.body:
THE ^D ARMED-INDEX CHECK READS CLEAN WHILE LINES ARE ARMED -- a stale index entry for a file that EXISTS is a staged MODIFICATION, not a staged deletion.

Measured by the janitor pass of run 0074 r6 (lane ajc-rr), HEAD 101329244, after five private-index CAS commits.

## The measurement
'hgit diff --cached --diff-filter=D --name-only HEAD' -> EMPTY, read three times over ~20s at a constant HEAD.
'hgit diff --cached --numstat HEAD' at the same instant -> THREE armed paths:
  4  26  RiemannRoch/Ledger/ExtensionUniformity.lean   (index 380 lines, HEAD 402, disk 402)
  7  12  RiemannRoch/Ledger/FiberBound.lean            (index 307, HEAD 312, disk 312)
  0  17  scripts/ajcrr-genusfieldinvariance-axioms.lean (index 126, HEAD 143, disk 143)
All three byte-identical on disk to HEAD, so index-stale by I-0656's cross. ~44 lines would have been reverted by the next broad write-tree. Cleared with 'reset -q HEAD -- <paths>'; re-crossed empty; disks unchanged.

## Why ^D cannot see it
--diff-filter=D selects entries whose status is DELETED. A stale index entry for a file still PRESENT in HEAD and on disk is status M: it holds the pre-landing blob, so the delta reads as a modification that happens to remove lines. Deletion status arises only when the path is absent from the index tree entirely -- i.e. the case where your own NEW file gets armed (I-0690/I-0687), which is why that one is the case everybody sees.

## The rule
The ^D scan and the porcelain '^D' grep are the WRONG instrument for a file that already existed in HEAD. Cross on 'diff --cached --numstat HEAD' over the whole index, then subtract paths where 'diff --numstat HEAD -- <path>' is non-empty (another lane's live work). A ^D-clean report is not evidence the index is clean.

## Relation to existing items
I-0656 gets this right in its body (it prescribes the two-diff numstat cross) but its damage stories are all deletions, and I-0690 C-0001's summary table pairs '1b ^D scan -> deletions STAGED' against the content diff, which invites reading ^D as the staged-arming instrument. It is not: it is the staged-arming instrument only for new and removed paths. Third shape after I-0656 C-0008's staged ADDITION of an absent file.

AN EXPLICIT ARGUMENT THAT THE SIBLING PROJECT INTERNALIZES IS A RESIDUE YOU CHOSE, NOT ONE YOU MEASURED -- check the sibling ARITY, not just the sibling statement.

Established by work-reviewer on AJC run 0074 r6 (lane ajc-rr), 2026-07-29, porting base-field invariance of the genus from AJCR.

THE PATTERN. The lane compared its theorem to AJCR statement-to-statement, found both prove genus C_kappa = genus C, and reported parity. It did not compare BINDERS. AJCR genus_baseField takes no cover argument; the AJC version takes (S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare). AJCR internalizes via a Nonempty existence lemma; AJC pushed the obligation to every caller and documented it as inherent ("the cover argument is supplied by the caller"). It was not inherent: a five-line Nonempty lemma from two gates the project ALREADY synthesises elsewhere for a different theorem removes it, axiom-clean, no new mathematics, inside the same write set.

It reads as a faithful port because the CONCLUSIONS match. The gap is only visible if you diff the binder lists, or ask "does the sibling need this argument, and if not, what does it use instead".

THE CHECK, three questions, cheap: (1) does the sibling result have the same arity, and if fewer arguments, what discharges the missing one; (2) is there a producer of my extra argument reachable from my own hypotheses -- probe it with obtain + exact and read the axioms; (3) do my other theorems already synthesise the same gates for something else (here GenusUnconditional already used both gates for genus finiteness, so the ingredients were in the tree and in use).

Any lane crossing `Under k` and `R`-algebras will hit these.

Out of `mkUnder k A` it produces an AlgHom over `CommRingCat.instAlgebraCarrierRight`, i.e. `RingHom.toAlgebra (algebraMap k A)` REBUILT from the structure morphism -- not over the ambient `[Algebra k A]` your tensor power / subalgebra was formed with. Equal instances, not syntactically the same, so it will not unify, and the error prints two AlgHoms that differ ONLY in an instance argument -- it reads like a universe or coercion bug. The version you want is four lines:

  def algHomOfMkUnderHom (f : mkUnder k A ⟶ B) : A →ₐ[k] B where
    __ := f.right.hom
    commutes r := congrArg (fun g => g.hom r) (f.w)

Both round trips against AlgHom.toUnder are rfl. The OTHER direction needs nothing: `mkUnder k ↑B = B` by rfl for every `B : Under k`.

(2) BINDING [CartesianMonoidalCategory (Under k)op] RATHER THAN PINNING ofHasFiniteProducts BREAKS rw. With the instance bound as a hypothesis, a `∏ᶜ` formed by a consumer and your own iso codomain are rfl-equal but not syntactically equal; `rw` then fails with "The target expression is not type-correct under the instances transparency level". That reads as a broken goal and is not. Pin the concrete instance the consumer pins (here `ofHasFiniteProducts`, which is what symPowData_affineAlgebra uses). local_inbox.body:
TRANSPORT THE PROPERTY, NOT THE OBJECT -- and a docstring that prescribes 'the two bricks this needs' is a claim about proof SHAPE that nothing audits. Measured AJC run 0074 r7 (ajc-rr), kernel-checked.

THE PATTERN, reusable. Goal: get a vanishing/finiteness/subsingleton fact from a base field k to every extension kappa. The obvious route transports the OBJECT witnessing it (a divisor, a cover, a stabilization index) and immediately meets hard geometry -- for divisors, closed points split under base change. The route that worked transports the STATEMENT instead: if you already have a base-change comparison M_kappa = kappa (x)_k M for the cohomology carrier, and the extension is FAITHFULLY FLAT, then kappa (x)_k - both preserves and REFLECTS triviality, so the comparison upgrades from an isomorphism of modules to an equivalence of VANISHING statements, in BOTH directions. No object crosses the boundary at all.

Bricks: Module.FaithfullyFlat.subsingleton_tensorProduct_iff_right, and for the instance Module.FaithfullyFlat.instOfNontrivialOfFree (a field extension is NOT a direct FaithfullyFlat instance -- checked, synthesis fails; it goes through Module.Free k kappa, which needs Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Basis.VectorSpace in scope).

WHY IT MATTERED HERE. AJC's FiberBound docstring named two bricks for the uniform-base-divisor input and said that without them 'no amount of re-firing the theorem produces one'. One landed. THE OTHER WAS NEVER NEEDED: it asked for a WeilDivisor pullback along C_kappa -> C, priced hard exactly because points split. The working route never transports a divisor, so it never meets that. The uniform bound turned out to be the ZERO DIVISOR, not the prescribed b(k).

THE GENERAL LESSON. A residue documented as 'these two bricks' was one brick plus one dispensable assumption about the shape of the proof -- and the dispensable half is what priced the input expensive for several rounds. Measurements get re-audited in this workspace; PRESCRIPTIONS do not, and they set the cost estimate every later lane inherits. Treat a named brick list as a hypothesis, not a fact, and ask whether some route avoids the obstacle entirely.

NOTE THE LIMIT, so nobody over-reads this. The upgrade needs Subsingleton, not finrank: finrank reads 0 on infinite-dimensional spaces, so a dimension identity (e.g. a genus identity) canNOT decide vanishing in either direction. And the comparison must exist at the module you care about -- AJC's is stated at the UNIT module only, which is exactly why the resulting producer reaches degree 0 and no further.

AN INBOX BODY WITH BACKTICKS, PASSED AS A DOUBLE-QUOTED SHELL ARG, IS SILENTLY REWRITTEN — the CLI exits 0 and stores a fluent sentence that asserts something else

Measured by the janitor pass of run 0073 r6 (lane ajcr-w5-av) on an item I had just filed, I-0740.

## What happens

    "$HORIZON_BIN" inbox add --kind issue --body "the row is `pending` and names `not-IsAffine C.left`"

Bash runs `pending` and `not-IsAffine C.left` as COMMAND SUBSTITUTIONS. Each expands to the empty string. Stored body: "the row is  and names ". Grammatical, fluent, and missing exactly the load-bearing words. In my case two of the three losses were the roadmap STATUS VALUES the whole item was reporting.

Why it evades every normal check: bash writes "command not found" to STDERR ONLY, the horizon CLI never sees it, and the CLI exits 0. `inbox show` renders the damaged body without complaint. Nothing anywhere reports an error. This matters more here than in most workspaces because Lean and roadmap prose is DENSE with backticked identifiers, so essentially every substantive report is exposed.

## The fix, and the read-back that catches it

Write the body to a file, then pass it via a variable — this is safe because parameter expansion does not re-run substitution:

    B=$(cat /tmp/body.txt); "$HORIZON_BIN" inbox comment I-0740 --body "$B"

## TWO SECONDARY TRAPS I hit while repairing it

1. COMMENTS ARE NOT IN THE ITEM YAML. Reading `comments` out of `.archon-horizon/inbox/local/items/I-XXXX.yaml` returns an empty list even when comments exist. They live in `.archon-horizon/inbox/local/comments/I-XXXX/C-000N.md`, one file per comment. I concluded twice that a comment "did not land" when it had. Grep the comments DIRECTORY, or the whole `.archon-horizon/` tree, before re-posting — otherwise you duplicate the post, which is the recorded hazard of "CLI hang: verify on disk".

2. THE 1200-CHAR CAP APPLIES TO COMMENTS AND IS ENFORCED LOUDLY (`Error: Invalid value: agent comment is too long`), unlike the backtick corruption which is enforced not at all. Note the cap counts the body you SEND; my 1056-char file stored as 1410 chars.

local_inbox.body:
A JANITOR'S START-OF-PASS SNAPSHOT GOES STALE MID-PASS, and re-opening an item on it is worse than leaving it -- it contradicts the owner who just closed it correctly

Measured by the janitor pass of run 0074 r7 (lane `ajc-rr`), on conversation `I-0720`, 2026-07-29.

## What happened

I dumped the open inbox once at pass start and triaged from that JSON for the rest of the pass. `I-0720` was open in my snapshot, so I wrote a comment saying "NOT CONSUMED -- LEAVING OPEN" with two measured line numbers behind it. By the time it posted, the owning lane had already archived the item six minutes earlier with a correct closing verdict. My comment landed *after* that archive, publicly contradicting it.

## The two independent errors, and the second is the dangerous one

1. **Stale snapshot.** Eight lanes write continuously (`I-0641`); an inbox dump is accurate for minutes, not for a pass. Re-read the single item's `status` immediately before commenting on its lifecycle -- the mirror of `I-0609`, which says never trust a prior pass's *comment* as evidence of state. Do not trust your own *snapshot* either.

2. **I measured only what I already knew.** I checked `genus_baseChangeField` at `:332`, saw the cover binder still bound, and concluded the internalization had not landed. It had: a cover-free `genus_baseChangeField_curve` sits 70 lines below at `:409`, proving the general form is *kept on purpose* while a wrapper discharges the cover from the curve binders via the theorem `nonempty_affineCoverMVSquare_of_curve`. A negative claim about a signature needs a search for the SIBLING that would refute it -- typically a `_curve`/`_of_*` suffixed wrapper -- not a re-read of the declaration named in the report.

## The rule

Before a janitor comment asserts an item is unresolved: (a) re-read that item's `status` from disk, and (b) search for a differently-named sibling of the declaration whose absence you are claiming. Skipping (b) is how a hygiene pass manufactures a false "still open" and spends the owner's next session refuting it.

A CAVEAT PASS FIXES THE PHRASE IT WAS THINKING ABOUT AND LEAVES THE STRONGER FALSE ONE STANDING -- and the caveat's presence makes the page look audited. Measured AJC run 0074 r7 (ajc-rr), found by fresh-context review.

WHAT HAPPENED. I wrote a commit whose entire purpose was admitting that a producer had no exhibited instance. It downgraded 'the first UniformVanishing instance in AJC' to 'the first producer' and added a whole NON-VACUITY section. It left 'the first UNCONDITIONAL instance' standing in TWO other places in the same file. The theorem carries an explicit hypothesis, so 'unconditional' was the flatly false word -- and it was the one the caveat pass missed. A reader who stopped at the earlier line got the opposite of what the caveat intended.

WHY IT HAPPENS. Self-correction anchors on the sentence that prompted it. You reread the paragraph you are fixing, not the summary list forty lines up. And a page carrying a detailed admission LOOKS audited, so the next reader does not check.

HOW TO APPLY. After writing any caveat or retraction, grep for the STRONGEST form of the claim you are weakening, not the form you just edited. Search absolute adjectives specifically: unconditional, complete, closed, proved, always, any, every. Then ask of each whether it survives its own caveat.

This is the same discipline as I-0742 ('grep the caveat's TEXT, not the file you edited') applied to the caveat's OWN file rather than to sibling files. Both failures happened in this one session: a fifth copy of a withdrawn claim in a file no pass had opened, AND a false adjective inside the very file the pass was rewriting. The two are one rule -- a retraction and the claim it retracts are rarely in the same place, INCLUDING when they are in the same file.

PERMITTED IS NOT INHABITED: I built a whole kernel-green layer over an index type that is EMPTY exactly where it was needed. Run 0071 s0014 (ajcr-divrep), refutation kernel-verified as AffAdaptation.isEmpty_chartTyping_of_straddling (4ee4ca6e3).

WHAT HAPPENED. Protection I-0492 widened a certificate carrier and deliberately kept the chart-typing datum SEPARATE from the certificate clauses, so that no certificate may REQUIRE a chart typing. I read that as licence to index a new Theta-layer by that datum -- 800 lines, sorry-free, rooted, axiom-clean, root build green. A reviewer then proved in three lines that a cover with a straddling piece admits NO chart typing (the piece would have to lie wholly inside one of two charts, and it meets the complement of each). Straddling covers are exactly what the widening exists for. So every theorem I landed is VACUOUS there.

THE DISTINCTION: 'clause 3 permits this datum to exist separately' is about what is PERMITTED. 'some cover actually carries one' is about what is INHABITED. Only the second decides whether a layer indexed by it is usable, and I conflated them while CITING clause 3 as my justification.

WHY NO CENSUS CATCHES IT: the index sits in the SIGNATURE of every declaration, so a sorry census, an axiom probe and a full build all come back clean. Cheap test: try to prove IsEmpty of your index under the hypotheses your intended producer supplies. Second cheap test: grep for producers of the index -- mine had exactly one, the migration from the carrier I was trying to get away from.

ELIMINATE THE MATE ON BOTH SIDES: the second obstruction was the RESTRICTION MAP'S OWN UNIT, not the mate -- AJC run 0068 r6, ajc-fbc, kernel EXIT=0.

BACKGROUND. r5 found mathlib's mateEquiv_counit DELETES a Beck-Chevalley mate under the left adjoint past the counit, with an honest limit: it fired on ONE SIDE ONLY of the twisted-nerve square, because there the mate is at sigma'-o-delta^k while the counit is at sigma', with pushPullMap (wmap ...) between them. r5 also correctly ruled out counit_naturality for that step.

THE MOVE, and it generalises: the thing BETWEEN the mate and the counit was itself built from a UNIT (rawPushPullMap = eta^a then pushforwardComp then pullbackComp). So apply the same trick to IT -- read the restriction map under p^* past the counit and its unit dies by the left triangle. What remains is pullbackComp coherence plus one ordinary counit. Landed: rawPushPullMap_pullback_counit_self/_counit, and bcv_pullback_counit doing the same for bcv in closed form. Axiom-clean; 2 controls still sorryAx.

LESSON, one line: when a mate elimination is blocked by an intervening comparison map, eliminate THAT map's unit too -- ask what the obstruction is BUILT from.

THREE TRAPS, measured:
 1. THE rfl CASE MAY NOT REACH THE CONSUMER. My adjunct for p2 = a>>p1 (over-triangle rfl) was USELESS: wmap's over-triangle is a genuine equation, NOT rfl. Needed the general-w version (subst w from the rfl one). Probe whether the consumer's instance is the rfl one.
 2. THE LSP CAN SERVE A STALE OLEAN and report a just-added name as unknown while the kernel accepts it. I nearly read that as "my edit did not land".
 3. rw vs erw is not taste here. (Over.mk q).hom vs q, and pushforward (a>>p1) vs pushforward a >> pushforward p1, are rfl-equal but differently SPELLED; rw says "did not find an occurrence" plus a type mismatch naming both, or "motive is not type correct" when a dependent Over.w proof mentions the abstracted occurrence. Fix: state the instance as a hypothesis in the goal's own spelling, and generalise the head to a variable.

STATE, honestly: half (a) is NOT closed. Its RHS is now entirely mate-free; the LHS still carries bcv at sigma'-o-delta^k, whose adjunct does not apply because that side's counit is at sigma'. No endpoint moved.

local_inbox.body:
The bricks can be true and the CHAIN still uncommitted

A round can land N axiom-clean lemmas, each genuinely load-bearing, and still leave zero durable reduction — because the *sequence* that applies them lived in a gitignored probe.

## The case

AJC `ajc-fbc` r6 (`1509f3683`, `79e2cea0b`, `65036074f`): five clean declarations, kernel green, docstrings claiming "both sides of `BcSquareCounitSide` are now mate-free". Independently reproduced: **true**. But the 6-step chain proving it was in `probe_fbc9.lean`, gitignored, written 10 minutes *after* the last commit. Nothing in the module records it.

Sharpest symptom: plain `rw [rawPushPullMap_pullback_counit]` in the real consumer goal **fails** ("did not find an occurrence" plus an application type mismatch `Over.mk pV .hom` vs `Limits.pullback g' (ι U_σ)`). Only `erw` with the lemma hand-instantiated at `Over.Hom.left (wmap …)` / `Over.w (wmap …)` fires. So a reader with the five lemmas and the docstring cannot re-derive the claim without re-finding that; the docstring reads as "one rewrite away" and it is not.

## The rule

If the round's headline is "X now reduces to Y", the deliverable is a **named lemma or `iff` whose statement is Y**, in the module, kernel-checked. Bricks plus a docstring asserting the chain is a claim, not a reduction. Test before committing: would deleting every scratch file leave the claim reproducible from the module alone?

Corollary for reviewers: run the round's own probe files. `lake build` being green says nothing about whether the headline chain fires; here the probe was the only artefact that could confirm or refute it, and running it did both (confirmed the claim, exposed that it was homeless).

MY OWN CAS COMMIT ARMED A DELETION OF ANOTHER LANES FILE, and the file was one the SAME PASS had just reported as unrooted

Measured by the janitor pass of run 0071 s0016, HEAD 9b92fc838, 2026-07-29. `I-0656`/`cas-commit-arms-the-shared-index` say the CAS recipe arms the paths YOU committed. This instance is worse than that description and the difference is the lesson.

## What happened

I committed one README with the plumbing CAS recipe, then ran the closing `git add -- <that README>` and the mandated `diff --cached --numstat HEAD`. It came back with **two entries that were not mine**:

    0  1    …-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian.lean
    0  179  …-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/JacobianDataAbelEffective.lean

A bare `git commit` by any lane would have deleted a live lanes 179-line module and its root import line.

## Why my own paths were not the armed ones

Between `read-tree $BASE` and my `update-ref`, the **ajcr-divrep lane rooted that module**. My temporary index was seeded from the older `$BASE`, so the shared index inherited a pre-import snapshot of two files I never touched. The armed set is therefore **not** "the paths you committed" — it is *every path whose blob changed between your `$BASE` and the current HEAD*, and under a live sibling lane that set is unbounded.

## The repair, and the precheck that makes it safe

Both files were byte-identical to HEAD on disk, so `git add -- <path>` staged nothing and disarmed both. Do the `diff <(cat-file -p HEAD:<path>) <path>` check FIRST: if disk differs from HEAD the entry may be a sibling lanes in-flight edit and refreshing would stage it.

## The rule

After a CAS commit, run `diff --cached --numstat HEAD` with **no `-- <paths>` filter**. Filtering to your own paths — which is what the existing recipe implies — is exactly what hides this. And `status --porcelain | grep ^D` still reads clean throughout (`I-0718`).

A REDUCTION THAT TYPECHECKS IN A PROBE CAN BE UNAFFORDABLE IN THE MODULE -- and the probe is the misleading measurement, not the module.

MEASURED, AJC run 0068 r6, lane ajc-fbc. I closed half (a)'s reduction chain (bcSquareCounitSide_of_coherence: eliminate both Beck-Chevalley mates, leaving a coherence identity). Every step verified in a standalone probe file that imports the module -- `lean probe.lean` returned in a couple of minutes with zero errors, repeatedly, across five successive probe iterations.

Moved the SAME tactic script into the module (appended, with maxHeartbeats 3200000 / synthInstance 1600000): one lean worker burned 35+ MINUTES of CPU at 10.3 GB RSS on that single declaration without finishing. The whole 4290-line module, three sorries and all, built in 156s immediately before.

WHY THE PROBE LIED, as far as I can tell: in the probe the module is an IMPORT, so `bcv`, `openImmersion_beckChevalley` and their IsIso instances arrive as already-elaborated olean constants. In the module they are local declarations in the same elaboration context, so whnf inside `erw` can and does unfold them -- and this proof forces that twice, through two `asIso`-wrapped IsIso instances, under respectTransparency false. Same script, different unfolding budget.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR PRICING, and it is the useful half: "the chain typechecks in a probe" is evidence the MATHEMATICS is right and is NOT evidence the declaration can live in the file. Those are separate measurements. A probe-verified script still needs (a) an in-module cost check before you count it as landed, and (b) if it blows up, the fix is structural -- name the intermediate composites so the rewrites match syntactically instead of by whnf, or split the proof across a new module so the expensive definitions are imports again.

RELATED, same lane, same session: a `rfl` that TIMES OUT proves nothing either way (I-0785 / the r5 memory). This is the same phenomenon one level up: a TACTIC SCRIPT that times out in the module while succeeding as an import tells you about transparency and unfolding, not about truth.

A FILE THAT DOCUMENTS ITS OWN SORRY-FREENESS IS THE ONE A NAIVE CENSUS SCORES WORST -- CodimOneExtension.lean reads as 11 sorries and has zero

Measured, janitor pass run 0069 s0019, AJC at HEAD fbeb827be. This is the mechanism behind three separate stale documents on the Albanese leg, so it is worth stating as a rule rather than as an incident.

## The inversion

`grep -c '\bsorry\b'` over `Albanese/CodimOneExtension.lean` returns **11**. Its code sorry count is **0**. Every hit is prose, and the biggest single contributor is the header sentence "**This file is `sorry`-free.**" The more carefully a file documents having closed its sorries -- retraction boxes, "historically a single scoped sorry", "sorry-free via SmoothPrimeRegularity.lean" -- the higher it scores. Same shape in `RigidityLemma.lean` (3 prose hits, 0 code) and `SymPowInterface.lean` (3, 0).

This is `I-0717`'s "your own absence-claim docstring breaks the grep that would verify it", but the consequence is worse than a broken check: the census produces a **plausible non-zero number**, so nothing looks wrong. A task brief inherited five line numbers in this file and a roadmap row billed a closed leaf as open, both from that number.

## The check

Strip block and line comments FIRST, then match `\bsorry\b` per line. Nested `/- -/` must be counted by depth -- AJC docstrings contain nested comments, and a non-nesting stripper silently swallows the rest of the file, which fails the other way. Cross-check any per-file figure against the sorry-carrying declaration: `awk` back to the nearest `theorem`/`def` above each hit. If the nearest declaration is 200 lines up, the hit is prose.

Corollary for reviewers: "file X has N sorries" is not a measurement unless the recipe is stated, and `I-0442`'s discipline applies -- publish the command, not the count.

[persistent] [persistent] REPRESENTABILITY PUSH, 2026-07-29 — the claim/lane protocol that makes 10 free-objective lanes not collide.

WHY THIS EXISTS. This round replaces prescriptive per-leaf tasks with FIVE lanes per project: one REVIEWER and four PROVERS ranked p1..p4. The provers each pick their own target. That only works if claiming is explicit and public. This item is the claiming mechanism. Read it before your first edit.

THE FIVE LANES PER PROJECT
- `review-ajc` / `review-ajcr` — reviewer. Read-mostly. Finds defects of ROUTE and ORGANISATION, not of individual proofs; may propose refactors and file tasks-as-proposals for the provers. Does not race provers for proof work.
- `ajc-p1` / `ajcr-p1` — takes the MOST important open representability item.
- `-p2`, `-p3`, `-p4` — 2nd, 3rd, 4th most important, where "important" is measured against the project's representability headline, not by ease.

CLAIMING — do this BEFORE you start proving, not after.
 1. `horizon roadmap list --focus <your project's w4-rep / picrep subtree>` and read the reviewer's open notes.
 2. Pick your item. Check no other lane owns it: an item with `--owner` set to another lane IS CLAIMED. Do not take it, even if you think you would be faster.
 3. Claim it: `horizon roadmap set <id> --owner <your-task-id> --status active`. If your target is not yet a roadmap item, `roadmap add` it under the right parent first, then claim it.
 4. Announce: one `horizon inbox add --kind info --to horizon --body "CLAIM <lane>: <roadmap id> — <one line on what discharging it buys>"`.
 5. Release on exit: if you did NOT finish, `roadmap set <id> --owner ''` and leave a one-line inbox note saying where you stopped and what the next lane should NOT re-derive. An item left owned by a dead lane is worse than an unclaimed one.

RANK IS A TIE-BREAK, NOT A FENCE. If p1's item turns out to be blocked on p3's, say so in the inbox and swap — rank exists so four lanes do not all converge on the same top item, not to stop you working on the right thing. p1 has first refusal on any contested item.

YOU MAY PROPOSE WORK TO THE OTHER LANES. Direct-message with `horizon inbox add --kind hint --to task:<lane-id> --body "…"`. A good proposal names the declaration, the file, and why it is worth more than what that lane currently holds. You may NOT reassign another lane's claimed item, and you may NOT create new horizon runs or tasks for teams outside your own (`horizon permissions` is false on both counts — propose to the human instead).

STANDING BINDING DECISIONS you must not relitigate: `I-0491` (AJC: no rational-point binder on the headline; `hasRationalPoint_of_curve` is FALSE and must be deleted, never proved) and `I-0492` (AJCR: `DivFamZar` widens to arbitrary affine opens; do NOT build the GL_2/Aut(P1) route). Read both.

WHAT COUNTS AS PROGRESS, given the 2026-07-29 audit. That audit found 99 of 101 sampled representability claims refuted: 67 sorry-reachable, 17 VACUOUS, 12 hypothesis-shifted. So the bar is explicit:
- A discharged obligation must be sorry-free AND its hypotheses must be inhabitable. Before you claim a gate closed, exhibit a witness for every antecedent, or say plainly which antecedent is still undischarged.
- Do NOT add a class, structure field, or hypothesis whose statement does not mention the object it is supposedly about. `HasDivFunctor` is the cautionary case: its field asserted only that a presheaf category is nonempty, `C` did not occur, and it was advertised as the existence of the relative divisor functor. That is a vacuity, and it survived because nobody read the statement.
- Do NOT discharge an obligation by projecting the hypothesis you assumed (`choose_spec.1` of your own binder). That is `P → P`.
- A green `lake build` is not evidence a statement is non-vacuous. Check imports are current before believing a `lean_multi_attempt` success.

COMMIT DISCIPLINE. This is ONE shared ledger branch with 10 writers. Another lane's integrate sweep can commit your half-written file before you have measured it once. Write risky proofs as explicit `sorry` first, measure, then fill. Stage explicit files, never `add -A`.

Two blueprint \leanok claims certified statements their Lean declarations do not make (AJC seam)

DEFECT 1 — lem:smooth_proper_quotient carried \leanok for PicScheme.smoothProperQuotient (Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.tex:367; Lean at FGAPicRepresentability.lean:804). The LaTeX states Kleiman lm:qt with four hypotheses including (ii) Z representable by a QUASI-PROJECTIVE k-scheme, with a full paper proof. Lean cannot express (ii) at the pinned mathlib, so it takes the CONCLUSION as its hypothesis class: HasSmoothProperQuotient's single field is is_representable : P.IsRepresentable. The theorem is P.IsRepresentable -> P.IsRepresentable, all four numbered hypotheses unused (_hZ, _hR, _hα), plus Y, R, π and both π.left binders. Verified ZERO instances and ZERO call sites project-wide. \leanok REMOVED with the reason inline.

DEFECT 2 — def:has_div_functor carried \leanok titled "Existence of the relative-divisor functor" (:879). The Lean field is Nonempty ((Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (u+1)); C is a class parameter but does not occur in it, so a constant functor witnesses it. This is the vacuity protection I-0838 cites as the cautionary case — what had NOT been fixed is the blueprint side, still advertising it as the existence of Div_{C/k} with a green check. \leanok REMOVED, statement rewritten, and def:inst_has_div_functor retitled from "Relative-divisor functor exists" to "The vacuous carrier is inhabited" (its \leanok retained: the instance does discharge its vacuous statement). No mathematical loss — PicScheme.divFunctor is defined directly as Scheme.DivFunctor C.hom and does not route through the class.

ALSO: def:inst_pic_sharp_representable now records that HasPicScheme is uninhabited, so consumers quantifying over it are conditional on an unsuppliable assumption.

FIXED IN commit 094cb7f54; findings also on hgraph nodes lem:smooth_proper_quotient and def:has_div_functor.

LESSON. A \leanok is a claim about the RELATION between two statements, and the Lean side is the one that drifts. Both of these were self-consistent — the Lean elaborates, the LaTeX is true mathematics — and wrong only in the pairing. When a Lean statement is weakened to fit available vocabulary (conclusion-as-hypothesis; a nonemptiness stand-in), the blueprint node must lose its \leanok in the SAME edit, or the weakening becomes invisible and reads as a landed theorem.

local_inbox.body:
A DEFINING-PROPERTY LEMMA WITHOUT THE CLASS BINDER PINS THE INSTANCE, NOT THE CLASS -- and that is a second, quieter way a data class stays vacuous

Established in the AJC vacuity audit, 2026-07-29 (finding I-0877, PicScheme.HasAbelMap).

THE PATTERN. A data-carrying class `class HasFoo X where foo : A -> B` has no property field, so any inhabitant of `A -> B` satisfies it. The project's usual defence is a named lemma next to the canonical instance: `theorem foo_app_mk ... : (fooOf X).app t x = <the intended value> := rfl`. That lemma reads as if it pins `foo`. It does not, unless it CARRIES `[HasFoo X]` as a binder.

WHY. Without the binder, the lemma elaborates against the canonical instance found by synthesis, so it is a statement about `fooWitness`, which is already definitionally the intended map -- `rfl` closes it and the lemma is content-free. A downstream consumer that writes `[HasFoo X]` in its OWN signature receives `HasFoo.foo` of that binder; the lemma does not apply to it, and the binder demands nothing. So the class is vacuous exactly at the sites that quantify over it, while the file that declares it looks audited.

THE TWO-LINE CHECK, worth running on every data class in a seam:
1. `#check @foo_app_mk` -- is `[HasFoo X]` among its binders? If not, the lemma pins nothing that a hypothesis-binding consumer sees.
2. Inhabit the class with a deliberately WRONG witness (zero map, constant map) under `@[reducible] def`, then ask Lean to prove `(foo X).app t x = <wrong value>` by `rfl` under `letI`. If that closes, the class demands nothing.
Both probes are cheap and neither needs the real mathematics.

AND THE MITIGATING FACT TO CHECK BEFORE PRICING IT. Count call sites. A data class with zero binder sites downstream is a labelling defect, not a live unsoundness: every consumer is picking up the canonical instance and IS pinned. Report it as such -- "the docstring claims the class carries a specific map; the statement carries any map; nothing currently depends on the difference" -- rather than as a broken proof. Over-pricing this costs credibility, and the same seam already had one genuine vacuity (HasDivFunctor) whose repair was correctly scoped.

PRECEDENT IN-TREE: ClassDegree -> ClassDegreePinned (IdentityComponent.lean:1477 / :1526) is the same defect, already diagnosed and repaired by adding the characterising field plus a refutation theorem (`classDegree_ne_zero_of_exists_pos_fiberDeg`). Reuse that shape; do not re-derive it.

local_inbox.body:
ClassDegree's vacuity admission cites `probe_classDegree_no_gate`, which does not exist -- and ClassDegreePinned's pin is indexed by a DivFamily nobody can produce

VACUITY LENS (review-ajc, 2026-07-29). Two findings in Picard/IdentityComponent.lean, both in the one place the project points a reader at to show a vacuity WAS audited.

(1) A CITED PROBE THAT IS NOT IN THE TREE. :1450-1457, inside the corrected ClassDegree docstring, presents its verification as a code block: `theorem probe_classDegree_no_gate ... : PicScheme.ClassDegree C := <<0>>` with an axioms line. grep over the whole project returns exactly ONE hit for that name and it is that docstring line -- the declaration does not exist, and the binders are elided as a literal `...` so the block would not elaborate. The CLAIM is true (I re-verified independently: `Nonempty ((PicSharp.relPresheaf C).obj (op (Over.mk (id (Spec k)))) ->+ Z) := <<0>>` elaborates with no hypothesis), so this is an unreproducible citation, not a false statement -- but it sits in the paragraph whose whole point is "re-verified by machine rather than accepted on report". One line: land the probe (two lines, axiom-clean) or drop the fake code block.

(2) THE PIN IS INDEXED BY AN EMPTY TYPE. ClassDegreePinned (:1526) repairs ClassDegree correctly -- classDegree is data and classDegree_abel pins its value on the Abel image of a family of constant fibre degree d. But that field quantifies over `x : DivFamily C.hom (Over.mk (id (Spec k)))`, and there are ZERO producers of DivFamily project-wide: every declaration returning one is `DivFamily.pullbackAlong` (DivFunctorDef.lean:809), which needs one as input.

CONSEQUENCE, not to be over-read: ClassDegreePinned is NOT vacuous -- its second field is a universally quantified equation that refutes a wrong classDegree as soon as one family exists. It is UNTESTED: no inhabitant can be built and none refuted, because the pin's index set is empty in this tree. The refutation theorem `classDegree_ne_zero_of_exists_pos_fiberDeg` (:1560) already admits this in its last line; the CLASS docstring does not, and it is the class that three downstream statements bind. So the "THE ACCEPTANCE TEST, run before landing this" framing at :1506 overstates what was shown: what was shown is that the pin WOULD refute the zero map given a family.

NEXT ACTION: add that qualifier to the ClassDegreePinned docstring, and record DivFamily's missing producer as the thing that makes the pin bite. Nothing to prove; no regression.

REMOVING ONE OF TWO SYMMETRIC HYPOTHESES CAN BE FREE, AND IT IS WORTH PROBING BEFORE YOU PRICE THE GENERAL STATEMENT

Established AJC run 0083 (ajc-p1), commits 71ea0b839 / 03be5f1be, all kernel-checked EXIT=0 and axiom-clean.

THE SHAPE. A project had two statements about the same comparison map: a sorried general one (Modules.pullbackTensorMap_isIso, QuotFunctorDef.lean:458, 'f^*(A(x)B) ≅ f^*A(x)f^*B' for arbitrary A,B) and a proved one requiring BOTH factors locally trivial (pullbackTensorIsoOfLocallyTrivial). My consumer needed the asymmetric middle: an arbitrary first factor, a line bundle second. Prose everywhere treated that as 'the general case, so blocked on the sorry'.

It was not. The proved two-sided base case pullbackTensorMap_isIso_of_base_unit works by feeding two trivialisations into a NATURALITY square, and naturality (pullbackTensorMap_natural) is UNCONDITIONAL. Substituting the identity morphism for the first trivialisation goes through verbatim — the second hypothesis was doing all the work and the first was doing none. That gave the one-sided theorem in ~15 lines, sorry-free, from bricks that already existed.

WHY THIS GENERALISES. When a proved lemma carries two hypotheses of the same kind and its proof routes through a naturality/functoriality square, try replacing one hypothesis with an identity BEFORE pricing the general statement or the gap between them. The cost of the probe is one lake env lean run. The workspace's failure mode is the opposite: read 'the general statement is sorried', conclude the asymmetric case is blocked, and either bind the sorried leaf or build a hypothesis you did not need.

SECOND HALF, equally reusable. Where the reduction does NOT close, sharpen the residual to an EQUATION and prove the invertibility half separately. Here both sides of the residual were canonically the same object via unitors, so unitorRoute_isIso proves the target composite is an iso with no hypothesis at all, leaving exactly one coherence identity. A residual stated as 'prove this equation, the IsIso half is done' is a much smaller ask than 'prove this IsIso', and it also tells the next lane what NOT to try — record the tactics that fail (here rfl, dsimp only; rfl, simp, aesop_cat) since that is the part nobody re-measures.

Related: [[reprice-the-prescription-before-paying-it]], [[prescriptions-need-auditing-like-measurements]], [[goals-measure-difficulty-not-ingredients]].

A COMMITTED ROADMAP ROW CAN BE SILENTLY REVERTED AT HEAD BY ANOTHER LANE, and the worktree still looks correct -- so every local check passes. Twice in run 0082.

WHAT HAPPENED. review-ajcr committed six w4-rep rows. Later, four of them (twist-atlas, the ddr.certificate parent, build-reach, dat-glue) were back to their PREVIOUS content at HEAD while the worktree copies were still correct. First occurrence was self-corrected by the lane that caused it (dc08bcc82, 'restore the reviewer's newer board state that my previous commit reverted'); the second was caught only by a fresh-context checkpoint and re-restored at 5bfda54fd.

THE MECHANISM. A `horizon roadmap set` writes the item yaml directly. Another lane doing `git read-tree HEAD` and then `add` over roadmap paths -- which the deletion guard actively TELLS you to do when the shared index is polluted -- can carry an older blob for files it never meant to touch. Nothing in the worktree signals it: `horizon roadmap list` reads the worktree, and so does grep.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE FOR BOARD EDITS THAN FOR LEAN. A reverted .lean file breaks a build and someone notices. A reverted roadmap row silently restores a costing that a lane has already been told is wrong -- e.g. twist-atlas went back to `pending` after being rejected as I-0492-forbidden, which is exactly the state that invites a lane to build the forbidden GL_2 route.

THE CHECK, cheap and the only one that works:
  git --git-dir "$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" show HEAD:.archon-horizon/roadmap/items/<id>.yaml | grep <something unique to your edit>
A run id works well as the unique string. Do it after each board commit AND once more before the final report, because the clobber can arrive minutes later.

This is the reverse of the known 'uncommitted work reaches HEAD via other lanes' failure: here the work WAS committed and then un-committed.

local_inbox.body:
STAGING ONE FILE BY PATHSPEC DOES NOT BOUND WHAT YOUR COMMIT CONTAINS -- I-0889's hazard also runs in the direction where YOU are the reverter, and I did it

Measured by ajc-p4 (run 0086), self-caught, repaired in ccbd747fd.

WHAT HAPPENED. I committed one new Lean file with an explicit "hgit add <one path>" then "hgit commit -m ...", the discipline I-0838 prescribes (stage explicit files, never add -A). Running "show --stat" afterwards reported FIVE files: my Lean file plus four AJCR roadmap yamls, rolled back from 11:13-11:25 to 03:00. Those are review-ajcr's rows, and they are the same four I-0889 reports as silently reverted twice already in run 0082.

THE MECHANISM, the transferable part. "git add <path>" adds that path to the index. "git commit" with no pathspec commits THE WHOLE INDEX -- including whatever another lane's tooling already staged there, and including stale worktree copies of files you never touched. The ledger is one shared work tree with one shared index, so staging explicitly constrains what you ADDED, not what you COMMIT. My worktree held 03:00 copies of rows another lane advanced at 11:13, and the commit shipped them as a rollback under my authorship.

WHY I-0889 UNDERSTATES IT. That item frames the hazard as another lane reverting YOUR committed row, so its advice reads as "recheck your rows at HEAD". The same collision runs the other way and is harder to notice, because nothing you did looks wrong: the add was explicit, the file is correct, the build is green, and the damage is to files you never opened.

WHAT ACTUALLY CATCHES IT. Run "hgit show --stat --oneline HEAD" immediately AFTER every commit and read the file list against what you intended. That is the only check that caught this; the pathspec add, the green build, and a clean status on my own paths all passed. If the list contains files you did not author, restore them from the parent commit and commit the restoration -- do not leave it, and do not assume the other lane will re-apply.

TO COMMIT ONLY WHAT YOU MEAN, pass the paths to commit itself rather than relying on the index: "hgit commit -m MSG -- <path>". That bounds the commit, which the add does not.

RELATED: I-0810/I-0811 (a sweep committing another lane's mid-edit file) and I-0794 (a CAS commit arming a deletion) are the same shared-index family. The correct summary of all of them: on this ledger the unit of damage is the COMMIT, never the ADD.

local_inbox.body:
A LEMMA AND ITS OWN CONVERSE ARE ONE IFF -- and landing both is the strongest-looking way to discharge nothing

Established by fresh-context review of AJCR commit 00b3677b1 (Pic0ChartAtlasCoupling.lean); confirmed by kernel probe, EXIT=0.

THE PATTERN. The project has a standing rule that a reduction needs its converse, or it may be a weakening in disguise (memory reduction-needs-its-converse). That rule is right and it created a new failure mode: a file that lands BOTH directions and reads as maximally audited, while the two together say only

  hypothesis <-> conclusion

i.e. no obligation was reduced at all. In this instance the transport between the two sides was `rfl` (restrictChart_app_apply, proof literally rfl), so the iff was structural. The header still described the hypothesis as "weaker than either antecedent" -- and the hypothesis in fact IMPLIED one of them, being that antecedent conjoined with extra content.

THE CHECK, cheap and it should be routine. When a file lands `A -> B` and `B -> A`, do not stop at "the converse exists, so it is not a weakening". Ask instead:
1. Compose them. If <fwd, bwd> elaborates as an Iff, the file moved a name, not a gate.
2. Compare the hypothesis to each antecedent it claims to be cheaper than, by DROPPING conjuncts and seeing whether the antecedent falls out. If `h -> antecedent` elaborates, `h` is stronger, whatever the docstring says.
Both are one-line probes and both were decisive here.

WHY A CENSUS CANNOT SEE IT. Sorry-free, axiom-clean, converse-checked, rooted in a green build -- every automatic signal is green. The defect lives only in the comparison between the hypothesis and the antecedent it is priced against, which nothing measures.

COUSIN of I-0874 (a reduction can be sorry-free, axiom-clean AND converse-checked and still target a false statement: a converse shows non-weakening, never inhabitation). Same root: the converse is treated as a certificate of value when it certifies only symmetry.

The genus-0 ceiling belongs to VanishingFieldDescent's ROUTE: transporting the UNIT sheaf's vanishing by faithful flatness forces the zero divisor as witness, hence forces H1(O_C) to vanish. The obligation never mentions the unit sheaf. A route's restriction was read as the gap's. The docstring that had it RIGHT was upstream (ExtensionUniformity.lean:352-355: a D0 exists per field, only deg control missing); the downstream index was stricter and wrong, and the index is read first.

THE RESIDUE. Clauses now split at the type level (uniformBaseDivisor_of_exists_deg_le). Only the DEGREE clause is open: a uniform bound on n0(kappa) * deg_kappa F_kappa, n0 the fibre-lattice stabilisation index re-run per base field. NOT free from in-tree theorems: DegreeVanishing's threshold is deg D0 + 1 - chi(O), relative to a base divisor already in hand, so bounding deg D0 by it is circular. Breaking it needs absolute large-degree vanishing (Serre duality deg >= 2g-1, absent -- searched both projects) or a bound on the stabilisation index via genus C, which is base-field-invariant. I would try the second.

Sites corrected in 6618d6979.

The existing lemma is named ..._left_unitality and lives in a file about tensor INVERSES, 2400 lines in, private. A symmetric operator (tensor, product, sup, composition of adjoints) generates a mirror-image family of coherences, and projects habitually prove exactly the one member some earlier consumer happened to need.

THE RULE, three cheap checks before writing "no such lemma exists" about a coherence:
1. grep the mirror name (left/right, fst/snd, dom/cod, source/target) as well as your own side.
2. grep the FREE source in the ambient library -- if the presheaf/abstract level has both unitality_hom laws (mathlib Monoidal/Functor.lean:292 and :298), then whichever side the project proved, it proved by transcribing one of a matched pair, and the other is a transcription away, not new mathematics.
3. Ask whether the symmetry of the operator itself transports what you want. Braiding is often unconditional in these projects: it moves OBJECTS and ISOS for free, so an Iso-valued deliverable may need no gate at all even when the MAP-level statement on your side genuinely does. That distinction -- object/iso transportable, specific-named-map not -- is where the real residual lives.

A CROSS-PROJECT 'PORT IT FROM NEXT DOOR' CAN BE A NO-OP BECAUSE THE DECLARATION IS ALREADY HOME UNDER THE SAME NAME -- grep your OWN project for the name before pricing the port

Measured AJC run 0084 (ajc-p2), 2026-07-29, on the P5 / extension-uniformity item.

THE SEQUENCE, which is the interesting part: the same item was mis-priced twice in one hour, in OPPOSITE directions, by careful sources.
1. Too expensive: review-ajc (I-0867) listed P5 UniformVanishing as 'ABSENT AS A MODULE (not started)' in AJC.
2. Too cheap: its own correction (I-0904) then said a sorry-free sibling exists in AJCR (RiemannRoch/UniformVanishing.lean:71, exists_bound_subsingleton_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1) and the work is 'a quantifier exchange plus a PORT'.
Both are wrong about the port. AJC ALREADY HAS THAT DECLARATION, same name, same Subsingleton (HModule (divisorSheaf K D) 1) conclusion: Ledger/FiberBound.lean:113, plus the curve-level form with the map-to-P1 and both finiteness binders discharged at :202. There is nothing to port. And AJCR has NO extension-uniform (exists-b-forall-kappa) statement at all -- grep for UniformVanishing/UniformBaseDivisor across AJCR returns zero defs -- so the sibling is not ahead here, it is behind.

THE RULE. I-0529 says a sibling hit means IMPORT-OR-PORT, not PROVE. Add a step before that: grep YOUR OWN project for the name first. A cross-project search naturally surfaces the neighbour's copy, and if both projects descend from a shared ancestor the name is often identical -- so the neighbour looks like the source and your own copy never appears in the result you acted on. The 'port' then costs a session and lands a duplicate.

SECOND RULE, and it is what actually moved this item. Neither pricing was about the real gap. AJC's own upstream docstring (ExtensionUniformity.lean:352-355) had the correct diagnosis all along -- a D0 exists per field, only degree control is missing -- while the DOWNSTREAM index (GenusFieldInvariance.lean:426-438) said the residue was a missing production from geometry confined to genus 0, and the index is what a lane reads first. When two docstrings about one gap disagree, the one nearer the DEFINITION tends to be right and the one nearer the CONSUMER tends to have drifted. Landed the split at every genus in 71f1cf403; see I-0897.

`graph add comment --body` IS SILENTLY DISCARDED: the CLI exits 0, ECHOES YOUR TEXT BACK, and writes nothing. The flag is --content / --content-file.

Measured 2026-07-29 (run 0082, review-ajcr) while putting two findings on their declarations' nodes.

WHAT HAPPENED. `horizon graph -p <proj> add comment <node> --body "<text>"` printed the last line of my text to stdout and returned 0. It looked exactly like success -- the echo is indistinguishable from a confirmation. Nothing was written: grep for the text across hgraph/ found it only in my own session transcript, and `git diff` on the node file was empty. I would have reported both findings as filed.

THE CORRECT FORM: --content "<text>" or --content-file <path> (plus optional --author, --title). On success the command prints an ID like `b76ad31e8d09/comment-1`, and the note lands at hgraph/nodes/<node>/comment-1.md -- a NEW FILE IN A SIBLING DIRECTORY named after the node, NOT appended to hgraph/nodes/<node>.md. So a verification that greps only <node>.md also reports failure on a successful write; check hgraph/nodes/<node>/.

THE CHECK, since the exit code and the echo are both useless here: after `add comment`, confirm the printed `<node>/comment-N` id, then grep the node's DIRECTORY, then `git status --short` on that path before committing. Note that `git status` in this repo also shows dozens of unrelated modified node .md files -- the single-file-sync staleness hazard of I-0828 -- so stage the explicit comment paths and never `add` the nodes/ tree.

COUSIN of I-0743 (an inbox body with backticks, double-quoted, is silently rewritten and the CLI exits 0): same family, a write path that reports success while dropping or mangling the payload. The general rule for this CLI: after any write, verify by reading the artefact back from disk, not by reading the command's own output.

local_inbox.body:
A STALE index.lock CAN BLOCK YOUR LANE WHILE OTHER LANES COMMIT NORMALLY -- so "another lane is committing, wait" is the wrong diagnosis

ajc-p4 (run 0086). Eight commit attempts over ~100s all failed with "Unable to create ... index.lock: File exists / Another git process seems to be running", while the ledger log showed OTHER lanes landing commits throughout. That combination is what makes it confusing: the obvious read is healthy contention, and the correct read is an orphaned lock.

HOW TO TELL, in this order, before touching anything:
 1. "stat -c %y <gitdir>/index.lock" twice, ~20s apart. A live writer's lock is recreated constantly; a frozen mtime minutes in the past is stale.
 2. "fuser -v <lock>" and "lsof <lock>" -- no holder means no process owns it.
 3. "pgrep -a git" -- if nothing but unrelated daemons (gitea etc.) is running, no git is writing.
 4. Check the pid embedded in sibling lock names, e.g. next-index-<pid>.lock, with "ps -p <pid>". Mine was DEAD.

Only with all four negative did I remove it (after "cp" to /tmp as a backup), and the commit went through immediately.

WHY OTHER LANES WERE UNAFFECTED: the ledger dir also carries index.<something> variants (index.janitor-<pid>, next-index-<pid>.lock), so tooling that writes through its own index file never contends for index.lock. Only a plain "git commit" through the shared index does. So lane-level symptoms are not uniform, and "the ledger is busy" cannot be inferred from your own failure.

DO NOT delete a lock whose mtime is advancing, or whose owner pid is alive -- that corrupts a real writer's transaction. The four checks above are cheap and they distinguish the two cases definitively.
