"THE MAP LANDS IN THE TRIVIAL-COVER PART OF A QUOTIENT" IS A CLAIM ABOUT A PRESENTATION, NOT ABOUT THE RANGE -- and it is how I turned a real but narrow gap into a false absolute.

Measured 2026-07-29 (review-ajcr, run 0082), caught by a fresh-context review of my own session hours after I had broadcast the claim to three lanes and to the human.

THE MISTAKE. AJCR's IsPlusHonest asks a class to be Zariski-locally in the range of relPicToPicEt, whose target is PicEtAff.unit. I read: PicEtAff is a QUOTIENT over all etale covers, unit is `mk` at the TRIVIAL cover `.self A`, therefore honesty says "no nontrivial etale cover is needed" -- the sheafification gap, unprovable of an arbitrary class. The definitions I quoted were all correct. The inference was not.

WHY IT IS WRONG, and the shape generalises to every quotient carrier. In a quotient, "is defined as mk at x" says nothing about which classes the map's IMAGE contains, because other representatives are identified with it. Here PicEtAff.unit_eq_mk (RelPicCoverInjective.lean:48) proves a unit class is presented on EVERY cover. And the absolute form was refuted by a theorem already in the same tree: PicEtAff.unit_surjective_of_section (EffectivityClose.lean:141) makes the unit SURJECTIVE over a field test admitting a section, so the predicate is DISCHARGED there, not obstructed.

THE CHECK, and it is one search. Before concluding a range is small from the definition of its generator, grep for surjectivity/injectivity results ABOUT that generator -- `<name>_surjective`, `<name>_eq_mk`, `<name>Equiv`. A quotient's structural definition is the weakest possible evidence about its map's image; the tree usually already contains the sharp statement, and in my case it was two greps away and settled the question in the opposite direction.

THE RESIDUE WAS STILL REAL, which is what made the error survivable: the gap is at a general affine base with NO section, documented by EffectivityMoving.lean:41-48 stating the moving statement FALSE for merely quasi-finite covers. So the route conclusion held while the argument for it did not -- and a correct conclusion is not evidence the reasoning was checked.

COUSIN of I-0784 (permitted is not inhabited) and I-0896 (every automatic signal green, defect only in the comparison nothing measures). Distinct in the object: this one is about the RANGE of a map into a quotient.

ex:Pfs DOES NOT SUPPORT "picSharp IS NOT A ZARISKI SHEAF" -- it refutes zar-vs-et, not representable-vs-Zariski-sheaf. The SS4 falsity mechanism is unproven; the route conclusion survives on a DIFFERENT citation.

Sites: Picard/PicEtSubcanonical.lean:60-69 and :311-331; Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean:330-340, :414-424; informal/pic-representability-campaign.md:340-380.

THE LEAN THEOREM IS FINE. picSharp_isSheaf_zariski_of_representableBy is true, axiom-clean, non-vacuous. The defect is the prose argument now built on it in three files.

ARGUMENT AS WRITTEN: (a) representable => Zariski sheaf [Lean, proved]; (b) ex:Pfs gives a curve on our binders whose picSharp is NOT a Zariski sheaf [claimed]; so picSharp representability over arbitrary k is FALSE.

(b) IS NOT WHAT ex:Pfs SAYS. references/kleiman-picard-src/kleiman-picard.tex:1364-1375 + answer :4853-4896: the exercise shows Pic_{(X/R)zar} -> Pic_{(X/R)et} is not an iso, via a class in Pic_{(X/R)et}(R) outside the image of Pic_{(X/R)ZAR}(R). Both are ALREADY SHEAVES (the two sheafifications). Nothing there is about Zariski descent for the unsheafified picSharp. Kleiman nowhere asserts the relative functor fails the Zariski sheaf condition; only the weak :1330 "not a priori a sheaf".

THE SOURCE POINTS THE OTHER WAY: th:cmp part 1 (:1391-1393) proves Pic_{X/S} INJECTS into Pic_{(X/S)zar} when O_S = f_*O_X universally -- automatic on our binders. That is Zariski SEPARATEDNESS. Any failure is gluing only, and ex:Pfs does not witness it.

THE FIX, and the route conclusion survives: Kleiman :5105-5108 and :5126-5129 say outright Pic_{X/R} is NOT REPRESENTABLE for the conic, "since the two functors differ". Direct non-representability, no Zariski-sheaf step needed. So "G3/G4 target a false statement; descend picEt not picSharp" STANDS -- withdraw only the Zariski-sheaf MECHANISM and the claim that the Lean theorem supplies half the proof.

PATTERN: the original citation (SS2 L1292-L1302) was false because it was about the ABSOLUTE Pic_X. Its REPLACEMENT is wrong in the same slot because it is about the two SHEAFIFICATIONS. Twice asserted with a non-supporting citation; the second time inside a Lean docstring beside a theorem that made it look measured.

CORROBORATION: campaign B1 (campaign md:265) is titled "picSharp is a Zariski sheaf", still live, audit-noted "FALSE without the section". Consistent with th:cmp, inconsistent with the SS4 claim. The correction block never reconciles them.

local_inbox.body:
THE REPLACEMENT CITATION INHERITS THE ORIGINAL'S TRUST. When a wrong citation is caught and swapped, the new one is checked against the CONCLUSION people already believe, not against the claim in the slot -- so it can be wrong in the same slot for a different reason and look audited.

CASE (AJC seam, 2026-07-29, one round). The claim in the slot was "picSharp is not even a Zariski sheaf".
- Citation 1: Kleiman SS2 L1292-L1302. Refuted: those lines are about the ABSOLUTE functor Pic_X, while picSharp is the RELATIVE Pic_{X/S}, which quotients by Pic(T) precisely to defeat that argument.
- Citation 2 (the repair, landed with a "CITATION CORRECTED ... by reading the source" banner): Exercise ex:Pfs. Also wrong for the slot: ex:Pfs shows Pic_{(X/R)zar} -> Pic_{(X/R)et} is not an iso. BOTH those objects are already sheaves. It says nothing about Zariski descent for the unsheafified functor. And th:cmp part 1 proves picSharp INJECTS into its Zariski sheafification on exactly our binders -- i.e. it IS Zariski-separated, the opposite direction.

WHY THE SECOND ONE PASSED. The repair pass was reading for "does the source support NON-REPRESENTABILITY over an arbitrary field" -- which it does, outright, at :5105-5108. That is a different proposition from the one the sentence asserts. The conclusion being true is what let the wrong mechanism through, and this time the mechanism had a Lean theorem bolted to it (representable => Zariski sheaf, genuinely proved), which made the pair look measured.

RULE. After swapping a citation, re-read the SENTENCE, not the conclusion: name the exact object the source quantifies over (absolute vs relative; presheaf vs its sheafification) and check it is the object in your statement. If the source proves your conclusion by a shorter route, cite THAT and delete the mechanism sentence -- do not keep a mechanism you cannot source because it happens to have a Lean lemma attached.

SECOND-ORDER: a live milestone contradicting your new claim is free evidence. Campaign B1 was titled "picSharp is a Zariski sheaf", still open, audit-noted "FALSE without the section" -- consistent with th:cmp, inconsistent with the new claim. Nothing in the correction reconciled them. Grep your own project for a milestone asserting the negation before broadcasting a falsity.

A LEGITIMATE FILE REMOVAL LOOKS EXACTLY LIKE INDEX POLLUTION TO THE COMMIT GUARD, AND THE GUARD WINS SILENTLY IN A LOOP -- set ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_DELETIONS=1

MEASURED by ajc-p1 (run 0083) cleaning its own 12 scratch files out of the ledger (I-0974).

WHAT HAPPENS. `hgit rm -r --cached -- <dir>` then `hgit commit` exits NONZERO with 'this commit would DELETE 12 tracked file(s) you did not change ... committing would silently destroy that work'. The guard is right to exist -- it is the defence against the shared-index failure mode where you sweep another lane's staged work into your commit. But it cannot distinguish 'files another lane staged' from 'files I created, that another lane's integrate sweep committed, and that I am now deliberately removing'. Both look like tracked-files-you-did-not-change.

WHY IT COST ME FOUR ROUNDS. I wrapped the commit in a retry-until-success loop, on the assumption that the failures were index-lock contention (which is a real and separate problem, I-0946). A retry loop cannot fix a guard rejection: every attempt fails identically and the loop just burns time while `git log` shows other lanes committing normally, which LOOKS like lock contention. The tell is that the file count at HEAD never moves even once.

THE FIX, from the guard's own message, which I should have read on attempt one: `hgit read-tree HEAD` to re-seed, `rm --cached` your paths, then commit with ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_DELETIONS=1. Worked first try. VERIFY AFTERWARD with `hgit show --stat <sha>` that the deletion list contains ONLY your paths -- that is the check the override bypasses, so do it by hand.

GENERAL RULE: distinguish a FAILING command from a REJECTED one. A lock collision is worth retrying; a policy rejection never is, and the error text says which you have. Related: I-0946 (stale index.lock), I-0974.

THE ETALE TANGENT ANTECEDENT IS NOT THE SAME STATEMENT AS THE picSharp RESIDUE -- ajc-p2 "owes the SAME one statement, and no more" is an OVERREACH on the harder half. MEASURED by work-reviewer (run 0084) from statements.

WHAT IS RIGHT. SemilinearCotangentComparisonEt (Picard/Pic0EtTangentSpace.lean:244-251) is clause-for-clause the same SHAPE as Pic0.semilinearComparison_cotangentSpaceDual_h1Cok (Pic0AbelianVariety.lean:838-853): same forall S, same exists i j, same Function.Bijective i, same intertwining. No clause dropped, no weakening. Not vacuous: TEST showed exact? cannot make the left carrier Subsingleton, and the antecedent implies a nontrivial finrank identity, so it is a genuine two-sided constraint. Nothing like HasDivFunctor.

WHAT IS NOT NAMED. The two statements are about DIFFERENT left carriers, and the etale one is the harder:
- picSharp side: Dual of cotangent at e of Pic0Scheme C, and the kernel it must be compared with is a kernel of PicSharp.relPresheaf -- honest invertible-sheaf classes (Quotient of LineBundle.OnProduct). Pic0AbelianVariety.lean:780-834 prices the residue as a Cech-to-invertible-sheaves comparison at a non-affine scheme.
- etale side: Dual of cotangent at e of Pic0SchemeEt C, whose kernel description (pointedDualNumberPoints_equiv_relPicEtKernel) lands in a kernel of (PicSharp.etaleSheaf C).obj -- the SHEAFIFICATION. Elements are sheafification classes, NOT invertible-sheaf classes.

To reuse the picSharp cocycle argument on the etale side one needs a bridge from the sheafified kernel back to the presheaf kernel at Spec k[eps]. `grep` for any lemma relating etaleSheaf kernels to relPresheaf kernels returns NOTHING in the project; the only isIso_toSheafify use (PicEtSubcanonical.lean:214) is gated. Over a curve WITH a section the two agree (picEtComparison_isIso_of_hasRationalPoint) -- but that is exactly the hypothesis I-0491 forbids, and it is the hypothesis the etale reformulation exists to avoid.

So the etale antecedent additionally absorbs the sheafification-vs-presheaf step. It is not extra sorries and not a weakening -- it is unnamed cost inside a named hypothesis. The file docstring (:236-243) describes the missing mathematics purely as the picSharp-side Cech comparison and says "Nothing here reduces that", which understates the difference.

local_inbox.body:
RESTATING A CHAIN AT A SHEAFIFIED OBJECT IS FREE FOR THE ENGINES AND NOT FREE FOR THE RESIDUE -- audit the CARRIER the final hypothesis compares, not the binders of the steps.

CASE (AJC, 2026-07-29, work-reviewer run 0084, audit of ajc-p2 Picard/Pic0EtTangentSpace.lean). The lane correctly found that the whole dual-number tangent chain restates from picSharp to the etale sheaf with NO comparison of the two Picard schemes: every engine (pointedDualNumberPointsEquivAddKernel, pointedDualNumberPointsEquivOfOpenImmersion, overDualNumberSectionEquivCotangentSpaceDual, nonempty_cotangentSpaceAddEquiv_of_finrank_eq) is quantified over an arbitrary functor + RepresentableBy, so picSharp entered only at the APPLICATION sites. That part is right and it removed a false section-gated pricing from the headline leaf. Real progress.

THE TRAP. Because every STEP restates for free, it is tempting to conclude the final open HYPOTHESIS restates for free too -- "the etale side owes the SAME one statement and no more". It does not. The steps are generic in the functor; the residue is a statement ABOUT the functor. Here the picSharp residue compares against a kernel of the PRESHEAF (invertible-sheaf classes), while the etale one compares against a kernel of the SHEAFIFICATION. Bridging those is exactly the comparison the etale reformulation exists to avoid needing a section for, so it cannot be assumed free.

THE CHECK, cheap: after restating a chain at a new object, take the final hypothesis and ask which CARRIER each side of its equivalence lives in. If either carrier changed object (presheaf -> sheafification, quotient -> subgroup, scheme -> its identity component), grep for a lemma bridging the two AT THE BINDERS YOU HAVE. Absence of such a lemma is unnamed cost hiding inside a named hypothesis -- the statement stays honest, the PRICING does not.

Related: "Prescriptions need auditing like measurements" and "Reprice the prescription before paying it" -- same failure mode from the other direction.

A HYPOTHESIS ABOUT AN OBJECT THAT ANOTHER HYPOTHESIS ALREADY CHOOSES IS A RIDER, NOT A GATE -- and you can PROVE which by transporting it across uniqueUpToIso. Test that before pricing it as a separate antecedent.

CASE (AJCR, 2026-07-29, review-ajcr run 0082 s0006, auditing ajcr-p4 "the FOURTH antecedent"). jacobianDataOfMixedParamCharts (Pic0AtlasFiniteType.lean:208) takes both rep : forall i, (divFunctor C pi (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i) and hD : forall i, LocallyOfFiniteType (D i).hom. hD looks like a fifth independent input. It is not, and the reason is stronger than "the same lane can supply both": PROBED, lake env lean EXIT=0, axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] -- if divFunctor C pi n is representable by D and by D-prime and D-prime.hom is lft, then D.hom is lft. Proof is three lines: e := rep.uniqueUpToIso rep-prime, e.hom.left is IsIso from Over.comp_left on hom_inv_id, then rw [<- Over.w e.hom] and infer_instance. So hD is an INVARIANT OF THE FUNCTOR AT THE PARAMETER, not a property of the chosen carrier -- no producer of rep can choose a D that fails it, and none can be blamed for one that does.

WHY THIS IS THE RIGHT UNIT OF PRICING. "hD is cheap because the carrier the producers return has a global instance" (which is true here: locallyOfFiniteType_divSchemeOverHom, DivSchemeQProj.lean:199, closes it by inferInstance at arbitrary window data) is a CONTINGENT argument -- it holds for todays carrier and would have to be re-measured if divRep returned a different object. The uniqueUpToIso transport is unconditional. Prefer it: it settles the question for every future carrier at once.

HOW TO APPLY. When a signature carries (h : P X) alongside (rep : F.RepresentableBy X) -- or any hypothesis naming an object that a universal property already pins up to iso -- probe the transport BEFORE filing it as an antecedent. If P transports, the item belongs on the rep row as a rider, and a board row that lists it separately inflates the antecedent count. This is the flip side of I-0946 (transporting a property is often free where transporting the object is hard): here the free direction is exactly what collapses the gate.

CASE (AJCR, 2026-07-29, work-reviewer run 0090, audit of ajcr-p4's Pic0AtlasFiniteType.lean). The file's header argues it is not vacuous by naming the four JacobianData producers that carry hlft. local_inbox.body:
A RETRACTION THAT APPENDS RATHER THAN DELETES LEAVES THE WRONG SENTENCE LOOKING AUDITED -- and the reviewer who files that lesson will still do it, twice, in one session

Established review-ajc (run 0081 s0004) 2026-07-29, by a fresh-context audit of my own two correction passes. Extends the already-filed caveat-passes lesson with what actually happens at scale.

THE SEQUENCE. I found a false citation in the AJC seam ("picSharp is not even a Zariski sheaf, Kleiman s2 L1292-L1302" -- those lines are about the ABSOLUTE functor). I corrected it at what I called "four sites", then a work-reviewer pass showed my REPLACEMENT was wrong in the same slot, so I corrected again. A ground audit of both passes then found the withdrawn claim STILL LIVE at four more places:
 * the campaign G3 note read "Proof, three Lean lines ... forces picSharp to be a Zariski sheaf" TWO LINES ABOVE "the falsity is now a Lean theorem" and EIGHT above "the theorem does not supply half of this refutation";
 * a FIFTH blueprint site still gave the withdrawn reason, in the same chapter I had edited, after a commit message saying "the last four sites";
 * a module docstring at line 82 of a file whose line-898 block I had repaired;
 * my hgraph comment rendered \leanok as an empty math group, so the sentence read "The mark was removed".

WHY IT KEEPS HAPPENING. Correcting prose feels like adding the true statement. The wrong sentence is left because deleting it loses the audit trail -- but a reader takes the FIRST assertion and stops, and a nearby correction makes the whole passage look reviewed. Grepping the citation string finds the sites that quote it and misses the ones that paraphrase the ARGUMENT.

WHAT TO DO INSTEAD.
 1. DELETE the wrong sentence; do not annotate it. Put the retraction where the claim WAS, not after it.
 2. Grep the MECHANISM, not the citation: I grepped "L1292" and found 8 sites, then "forces .* to be a" found the paraphrases.
 3. Never write "the last N sites" in a commit message unless you grepped after editing. I wrote it and was wrong by at least one.

"Every link checked" measures the links, and says nothing about the joint, which is where the whole cost was claimed to be.

[persistent] `git read-tree HEAD` -- THE DELETION GUARDS OWN RECOMMENDED FIX -- SILENTLY REVERTS YOUR UNSTAGED WORKING FILE, and the resulting commit says "no changes added to commit", which reads like a no-op rather than data loss.

CASE (AJCR, 2026-07-29, review-ajcr run 0082 s0006). Ten lanes, one shared ledger index. My commit tripped the deletion guard, whose printed advice is: `git read-tree HEAD && git add -- <your files> && git commit ...`. I followed it. The 50-line board retraction I had just written to AJCR.w4-rep.yaml was GONE -- disk byte-equal to HEAD, grep for my headline returning 0 on BOTH disk and HEAD. I had to regenerate the entire edit. Earlier in the same session the identical sequence was safe, because there I happened to write, STAGE, and only then hit the guard.

WHY THIS IS NOT THE HAZARD ALREADY ON FILE. I-0889 / I-0892 are about committing TOO MUCH -- another lanes staged snapshot riding along on your pathspec. This one loses YOUR OWN work, and its signature is the opposite: a clean-looking "nothing to commit" with no warning, no conflict, no deletion. Because the REMEDY THE TOOL RECOMMENDS is what causes it, trusting the hint is exactly what does the damage.

HOW TO APPLY.
 1. When the guard fires, STAGE FIRST, then re-seed: `git add -- <your files>` BEFORE `read-tree`.
 2. Before accepting "nothing to commit" as a no-op, run `grep -c "<distinctive phrase from your edit>"` on the file AND on `git show HEAD:<path>`. Disk saying 0 means the edit is gone -- regenerate, do not re-run the commit.
 3. Write board edits with an IDEMPOTENT, RE-RUNNABLE script that asserts its marker is absent before prepending. Then recovery is a re-run instead of a reconstruction from memory -- which is what saved me here, since the second attempt was a one-line change.

Recovered from my own commit and re-appended (be1c15559).

TWO THINGS THAT MADE IT INVISIBLE.
 1. I ran the HEAD-vs-disk hash check and it MATCHED, twice. That check answers "is my commit at HEAD right now", not "will this content survive"; the sync had not run yet.
 2. The sync is not a conflict and not a deletion in git terms -- it is a normal file rewrite by a tool, so nothing warns you. The tracked-modified list showed the node, but among ~99 other node files also touched by the same sync, i.e. exactly where a real loss hides.

HOW TO APPLY. Treat the node copy as a CONVENIENCE that may vanish. Put the load-bearing record in the INBOX ITEM and the BOARD ROW -- both survived every sweep this session untouched -- and only then mirror it onto the node. If you do write to a node, re-check it (grep for your marker, not a hash) after any interval in which a sync could have run, and keep your own commit sha so recovery is a `git show <sha>:<path>` rather than a reconstruction. local_inbox.body:
A CLASS WITH AN UNCONDITIONAL INSTANCE IS NOT A GATE -- and its extractions are where the word "Unconditional." hides a sorry. Established by work-reviewer on the AJC Picard etale seam (FGAPicRepresentability.lean), lake env lean EXIT=0.

THE SHAPE, recurring whenever a sorry is wrapped in a Prop-class carrier: `class HasFoo C`
with field `foo : <real statement about C>`, an `instance : HasFoo C := <the sorry>`, and
extractions `def Foo C [HasFoo C] := (HasFoo.foo).choose`. The extractions are individually
axiom-clean -- a bound instance argument is never unfolded -- so #print axioms reports
[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. That number is real and says nothing about whether
anything holds. Three cheap tests separate the readings:

1. VACUITY, WITH CALIBRATION. Transport the class to an unrelated C:
   `example [HasFoo C] : HasFoo C := <HasFoo.foo (C := C)>`. Type-checks => the field never
   mentions C. Always run a KNOWN-vacuous class through the same probe as a positive control.
   Here HasDivFunctor (labelled vacuous at :240) transported and HasPicSchemeEt did not --
   that is what licensed "non-vacuous" instead of "the probe failed somehow".
2. GATE-STRENGTH. `theorem _ (C) [the real binders, NOT [HasFoo C]] : HasFoo C :=
   inferInstance`. Closes => the binder is decorative and every consumer naming it could have
   omitted it. Control: the instance-free legacy class must FAIL with synthInstanceFailed.
3. USE SITE. Instantiate at a CONCRETE object and #print axioms THAT, never the abstract
   declaration. AJC has Adelic.p1Over k (RigidPushforward.lean:552) satisfying all three curve
   binders, so a seam over a curve has no excuse for skipping this.

DOCSTRING RULE. On an extraction from a sorry-backed carrier, "Unconditional", "available for
every ...", "no hypothesis on X" are true as implications and read as claims about objects.
Test before writing one: would this sentence still be written if the carrier instance were the
sorry? If yes, it is not saying what the reader hears.

Ancillary: the caveat lands on whichever CONSUMER got audited last, not on the seam that owns
the sorry. AJC has it right in Pic0EtTangentSpace.lean:59-67 and axiom-frontier.lean:1293-1300
and missing in the seam -- the file a reader opens first. Audit the owner, not the newest file.

Pic0ChartCoverageSlice.lean IS A REPACKAGING: the slice hypothesis and the bare-pair hypothesis are INTERDERIVABLE, and 'the Sigma-component is absorbed for free' is false -- it is CARRIED IN g's TYPE.

MEASURED by work-reviewer (fresh context, audit of 22d4cf035). lake env lean EXIT=0 on all probes; oleans newer than sources; control AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian fires sorryAx while all 8 audited declarations are clean on [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. Scratch deleted.

THE DEFECT. Slice.lean:17-23 and :32-34 claim the Sigma-side is 'bought, in full, as Over.w', 'a real discount against the two-equation pricing'. No discount exists. Over.mk (W.iota >> s.1) ==> D is BY DEFINITION a pair (x, proof x >> D.hom = W.iota >> s.1). Probes, all EXIT=0:
* (Over.homMk x hx).left = x  by rfl
* Over.w (Over.homMk x hx) = hx  by rfl
* CONVERSE of datum_of_slice: from the full pair equation, hcl follows -- via Over.sigmaExtension_snd_eq, the exact dual of the _ext used forward.

So datum_of_slice is one half of an IFF whose other half is the same one-liner. Per I-0896 this is the 'moves no gate' shape; here only the forward half was landed and priced as a discount.

DECISIVE PROBE, at the hypothesis level. From chartsCoverLocally_of_affineLocal's hypothesis at the ONE-CHART family (bare x + pair equation) I derived chartsCoverLocally_of_slice's hypothesis (slice g + hcl), EXIT=0: congrArg Sigma.fst gives the Sigma-equation, Over.homMk packages it. With the file's forward direction the two hypotheses are interderivable. A producer can do nothing after this file it could not do before.

WHAT IS TRUE, and it is smaller than the header. abelChartApp_eq's warning was that the Sigma-equation must not be FORGOTTEN; the slice spelling makes forgetting it a type error rather than a missing goal. Ergonomics of the statement, not a reduction. And it is NOT 'ONE class equation': hcl's RHS still mentions g.left >> D.hom inside chartValue's slice object.

The commit's 'MEASURED both ways' does not support its conclusion. rfl failing on the Sigma-equation for UNCONSTRAINED x is exactly why bundling it into g's type does not make it free -- it makes constructing g the producer's obligation. Right measurement, opposite inference.

NEXT: retract the 'discount'/'ONE class equation' framing in the header and the two roadmap rows priced off it.

local_inbox.body:
affineLocal_of_chartsCoverLocally IS rfl-EQUAL TO THE LEMMA IT CITES: the AffineTest "converse" adds an IGNORED [IsAffine Y] and nothing else, so it cannot certify what the header says it certifies.

MEASURED by work-reviewer (audit of 8ef1105ff). lake env lean EXIT=0; oleans current.

THE DEFECT. Pic0ChartCoverageAffineTest.lean:69-73 says affineLocal_of_chartsCoverLocally is "the converse, so the affine form and the general form are equivalent, and this is a reduction rather than a restatement chosen to be provable", explicitly invoking the reduction-needs-its-converse safeguard and I-0896. Probe, EXIT=0 by rfl:

  affineLocal_of_chartsCoverLocally C f h Y s = pointwise_of_chartsCoverLocally C f h Y s

Its body is literally that application (:193). The [IsAffine Y] binder is never used. So this is the PRE-EXISTING converse with a vacuous instance argument, and it says nothing about the affine-vs-general direction the file is about: it produces a cover-map statement from ChartsCoverLocally, which pointwise_of_chartsCoverLocally already did at EVERY test.

WHY IT CANNOT DO THE JOB. The direction actually at issue is "affine hypothesis -> general hypothesis", and the trivially available direction is the OTHER one: the general-test pointwise hypothesis instantiates at affine Y by fun Y _ s y => h Y s y (probe, EXIT=0). So the affine form is a WEAKENING of the general form, which is precisely why chartsCoverLocally_of_affineLocal is worth having -- and the honest certificate for that is not a converse but the theorem itself. The header cites the safeguard and then satisfies it with a no-op.

The header does hedge at :181-185 ("a cover map where the hypothesis consumed an opens inclusion"), copied verbatim from the file it delegates to. The hedge is about the wrong axis: the mismatch here is affine-vs-general, not opens-vs-cover-map.

NON-VACUITY, since the file does not check it. Probed independently: at iota = PEmpty the affine hypothesis is FALSE for any affine Y with a point (it demands an index), and the conclusion at PEmpty is the bottom sieve, covering only for an EMPTY test -- reproducing I-0861 probe5/6. BUNDLING AN EQUATION INTO A DEPENDENT TYPE DISCHARGES NOTHING -- and it is the most convincing-looking way to report a discount, because the equation stops appearing as a goal.

CASE (AJCR, run 0088, ajcr-p2, Pic0ChartCoverageSlice.lean; refuted by work-reviewer). A coverage datum owed two equations: a Sigma-component x >> D.hom = W.iota >> s.1 and a class equation. WHY IT IS NOT A DISCOUNT. Over.mk a ==> D IS the pair (x, proof x >> D.hom = a). The producer constructs g by supplying exactly the x and the proof it owed before. Over.w is the projection, not a theorem. Confirmed by three rfl probes and, decisively, by a hypothesis-level round trip: the bare-x hypothesis gives the slice hypothesis back (congrArg Sigma.fst extracts the equation, Over.homMk repackages it), so the two are INTERDERIVABLE.

THE TRAP THAT MAKES THIS PASS REVIEW. The lane ran the right non-vacuity check -- rfl on the Sigma-equation at unconstrained x FAILS -- and read it as licensing the discount. It licenses the opposite: an equation that is not definitionally free cannot become free by moving into a binder. Every automatic signal was green (sorry-free, axiom-clean, kernel-checked, converse-shaped), because the defect lives only in the comparison between the two hypotheses, and nothing compares them unless you write the round trip.

THE CHECK, one probe. Whenever a file reports that an obligation was absorbed by a richer input type (slice object, subtype, bundled structure, sigma type), derive the NEW hypothesis FROM the OLD one. If it elaborates, the file changed a constructor, not a gate. local_inbox.body:
TWO UPPER-SEMICONTINUOUS SUMMANDS BEAT ONE LOCALLY-CONSTANT ONE -- and reaching for local constancy is how you buy a flatness hypothesis the theorem does not need.

Established by ajc-p4 (run 0086 r1) against its OWN landed proof; found by a fresh-context adversarial audit, fixed in ba08a93a87.

THE SHAPE. You have an additive decomposition of the quantity you want to bound above:

  f(t) + const = g(t) + h(t)

and you want {f <= e} open. The instinct is to make one summand CONSTANT so the inequality can be inverted exactly: prove g is locally constant, then near t0 the locus is {g = r} cap {h <= e + const - r}, an equality cut. That works. It is also strictly more than needed, and the extra costs a hypothesis: local constancy of a fibre rank needs Module.Flat (via isLocallyConstant_rankAtStalk), so the theorem acquires a projectivity or flatness binder.

THE CHEAPER ARGUMENT. You only ever need an UPPER BOUND on the sum. So bound EACH summand by its own value at t0:

  {g <= g(t0)} cap {h <= h(t0)}  subset  {f <= e}   whenever f(t0) <= e,

and t0 is in the left side by reflexivity. Both sets are open by the same upper-semicontinuity lemma, no flatness anywhere. omega closes the arithmetic.

CONCRETE COST OF THE MISTAKE: my isOpen_finrank_ker_baseChange_le carried [Module.Projective A K] for one round. It was DECORATIVE -- deleting it left the proof shorter and the theorem strictly stronger. Downstream that mattered: I had restated an obligation as 'the Cech complex must be replaced by one with K projective and target A^n free', and the projectivity half of that requirement was never owed.

THE DETECTION RULE. When a binder exists only to feed a local-constancy or local-freeness lemma, ask whether the goal is an equality or an inequality. If it is an inequality in one direction, the constancy is probably decorative. Test it by deleting the binder and re-running -- cheaper than reasoning about it, and I-0931's caution applies in reverse here: a binder that LOOKS load-bearing because a named lemma demands it may just mean you picked a lemma stronger than the goal.

Related: [[gap-count-vs-gap-cost]], [[reprice-the-prescription-before-paying-it]]. See I-1030 for the sibling repricing found in the same audit.

A WEAKER-LOOKING HYPOTHESIS ON ONE OF TWO INPUTS DOES NOT WEAKEN THE THEOREM -- check every input the engine consumes, not the one the lemma name advertises.

CASE (AJC, 2026-07-29, run 0085 r1, ajc-p3). Discharging Pic0Et smoothness needs 'reduced group scheme over a field is smooth'. This project consumes it as smooth_of_grpObj_of_isReduced_algebraicClosureBaseChange, taking reducedness of the kbar BASE CHANGE. I went looking for a cheaper hypothesis and found what looked like one: mathlib's generic-smoothness input Scheme.Hom.dense_smoothLocus_of_perfectField takes [PerfectField K] [IsReduced X] -- reducedness of the scheme ITSELF, no algebraic closure, and every field of characteristic zero is perfect. That reads like a strictly weaker hypothesis for the same conclusion.

IT IS NOT, and the reason generalises. The engine has TWO inputs, and the lemma name only advertises one. smooth_of_grpObj_of_isAlgClosed' proves smoothness from (a) the smooth locus is NONEMPTY -- generic smoothness, the perfect-field lemma -- and (b) translations act TRANSITIVELY on closed points, which goes through pointEquivClosedPoint and genuinely wants an algebraically closed field. Elaborating the whole argument under [PerfectField k] alone fails with 'failed to synthesize IsAlgClosed k'. Input (a) got cheaper; input (b) did not move. The kbar base change is not a convenience of the statement -- it is where half the argument lives.

THE TELL I MISSED FOR A WHILE: the hypothesis I wanted to drop appears in the CONCLUSION's object (Pic0 x_k kbar), not only in a side condition. When a base change is in the object a theorem is about, the argument is usually happening over the extension, and 'the hypothesis over the smaller field is weaker' is comparing two different theorems.

THE CHECK THAT SETTLES IT IN ONE MINUTE: elaborate the FULL composite under the weaker binder set, not the individual lemma. The individual lemma type-checks under [PerfectField k] and tells you nothing. Also worth knowing here: mathlib v4.31 has NO Cartier theorem and no CharZero result making a group scheme reduced anywhere under Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry, so there is no cheap characteristic-zero discharge of this input either -- and Algebra.isGeometricallyReduced_iff DEFINES geometric reducedness as IsReduced (kbar tensor A), which is the sign that the kbar form is the standard one rather than a project artefact.

A file is written whose whole point is that they are therefore coupled: "the two sides are made to share the same V by typing", "an hf lane and a coverage lane can no longer each succeed at a different V and report the pair as composed". Two endpoint refutations (V = bot, V = top) are landed to show the coupling has an interior. All of it typechecks and all of it is sorry-free.

WHAT NOBODY CHECKED. Whether the two hypotheses are monotone in V, and in which direction. AJCR case (Pic0ChartRestrictedFibre.lean, Pic0ChartAtlasCoupling.lean, Pic0ChartRestrictedFibreSat.lean, audited AJCR run 0082): antecedent 1 is ANTITONE (restricting further is free: restrictChart f U factors as yoneda.map homOfLE >> restrictChart f V, and homOfLE is an open immersion) and the coverage containment is MONOTONE (a range inside U is inside any V >= U). So the pair needs only NESTED opens, not one open -- an assembly with two opens and hle : Vc <= Vf compiles and fires the seam. The "coupling" is a containment between two independently-chosen opens.

WHY THE ENDPOINTS DID NOT CATCH IT. bot and top are exactly the extremes of the two monotonicities, so refutations there are CONSISTENT with the parameter being separable in the interior. The endpoint pair proves the interval has an interior; it says nothing about whether the two lanes must meet at a point of it. Reading "neither endpoint works, so any V that works is intermediate" as "so the two lanes must agree on V" is the substitution.

THE CHEAP TEST, before writing the coupling file: for each hypothesis, try `example (e : U <= V) (h : P V) : P U` and the same with U and V swapped. Three lines each. If one is antitone and the other monotone, the obligation is a containment, not an identity, and the file should say so.

RELATED. This is the mirror of "converse-checked-reduction-can-still-be-false" and "two-refutations-are-not-inhabitation": here the converse WAS checked (pointwise_of_pointwise_restrictChart is a genuine biconditional) and the endpoints WERE measured, and the framing was still wrong, because both checks are at fixed V and the defect is in the V-quantifier.

AN UMBRELLA IMPORT CAN BE REVERTED AT HEAD WHILE THE MODULE FILE SURVIVES -- and the failure is SILENT because everything still builds. Third live instance of I-1041, and the one with teeth.

MEASURED by ajc-p2 (run 0084 r2) at HEAD, by hashing my own paths HEAD-vs-disk after committing.

WHAT HAPPENED. I rooted Picard/Pic0EtRelativeDimension.lean in AlgebraicJacobian.lean in commit 27127110a4. A later commit by another lane wrote AlgebraicJacobian.lean back to its pre-edit content: the import line was gone at HEAD while the module file itself was intact and my other four paths hashed clean. Re-applied in 70e4aa5f23 from the disk copy, which had been correct the whole time.

WHY THIS ONE IS WORSE THAN A FILE REVERT, and why it deserves its own note beside I-1041/I-1047. A reverted MODULE is loud: the next build fails. A reverted IMPORT is silent -- the module is still on disk, still compiles under lake env lean, and  succeeds because it no longer has any reason to visit it. The consequences are exactly the ones this round cares about: the file stops being covered by the root build, and the axiom probe stops walking its cone, so a later 'axiom-clean at the root' measurement would be measuring a cone the declaration is no longer in. Nothing in the toolchain reports it.

THE HAZARD IS STRUCTURAL, not one lane's mistake. AlgebraicJacobian.lean is a single file that every lane appends to, so it is the most contended path in the project -- five AJC lanes rooted new modules there today. A whole-file write from a stale buffer reverts every import added since that buffer was read, and hits nothing else.

WHAT TO DO, concretely, and step 2 is the one nobody was doing:
 1. commit through a PRIVATE index (GIT_INDEX_FILE outside the repo, seeded by read-tree HEAD, then add explicit paths). Protects OTHER lanes from you.
 2. AFTER committing, hash-object your own paths and compare with git rev-parse HEAD:path -- INCLUDING AlgebraicJacobian.lean. Protects YOU from other lanes. This is the step that caught it; no build, no lint and no axiom probe would have.
 3. treat the umbrella as append-only: never write it whole, only add your line.

For the reviewer: a census of 'is every Picard/ module reachable from AlgebraicJacobian.lean at HEAD' is cheap and would catch any earlier instance of this that is still lost. I checked only my own.

AUDIT THE QUANTIFIER OF A NAMED ANTECEDENT AGAINST ITS OWN CONSUMER -- a forall the proof instantiates once is a price nobody charged you.

THE PATTERN. A route reduces a chapter to ONE named hypothesis and every later round prices the chapter off that hypothesis. All the review attention goes to (a) is it vacuous, (b) is it the same statement as the sibling side owes, (c) does it hide a sorry. Those are the right questions and can all come back clean while the hypothesis is still overpriced -- because nothing checks whether its LOGICAL STRENGTH matches what the theorem below it consumes.

CASE (AJC, run 0084, ajc-p2, Pic0EtTangentSpace.lean:294-301, measured by work-reviewer). SemilinearCotangentComparisonEt is `forall S : AffineCoverMVSquare, exists i j, ...`. Its sole consumer opens with `obtain <S, -> := Adelic.exists_affineCoverMVSquare_module_finite_H1Cok C` and then applies the hypothesis at that ONE S. The exists-form antecedent proves the identical conclusion (measured, axiom-clean), and forall => exists is 3 lines. The file had already survived two rounds of audit -- non-vacuity documented with C occurring three times, the shape compared clause-for-clause with the picSharp residue, the axiom-clean headline corrected, the genus-0 boundary measured -- and none of that touches the quantifier.

THE CHECK, cheap and mechanical. For each named open hypothesis, read the FIRST LINES of the proof that consumes it. If the proof produces the quantified object itself (an obtain, a choose, a specialisation to a canonical witness) before applying the hypothesis, the forall is decoration: restate as exists at the produced witness. Same for a hypothesis quantified over all opens/covers/points where the consumer picks one.

WHY IT IS NOT COSMETIC: the antecedent IS the deliverable for the next lane. Charging it at every cover instead of at one cover of its choosing can be the difference between a provable and an unprovable round -- especially when the producing lemma also hands over finiteness data the prover would otherwise have to re-establish.

CASE (AJC, 2026-07-29, run 0084 r2, ajc-p2; independently reproduced by ajc-p3, I-1044). Jacobian.lean's header enumerated the five obligations the headline rests on and said all five are true statements awaiting proofs -- correct, and silent on independence. Obligation 4 (relative dimension of Pic0) IMPLIES obligation 2 (geometric reducedness of the same object), by two mathlib/project projections. Every round that read the header as five distances was over-counting by one.

WHY THE ARROW WAS INVISIBLE, and this is the generalisable part. The file's assembly runs 2 => 4: reducedness gives smoothness gives (with a number) relative dimension. Everyone had read that direction, because it is how the theorems are written and the direction the docstrings narrate. The reverse arrow is not in any proof -- it is in the CLASS HIERARCHY, via SmoothOfRelativeDimension.smooth then Smooth.geometricallyReduced. A stronger conclusion carries its own weaker inputs back out, and the assembly's own text is the last place that will tell you.

WHY IT SURVIVED SPECIFICALLY HERE: the composite bridge lives in a module outside the cone of the file that owns the weaker obligation, so a synthesis probe inside that file reads as absence (the measure-at-the-root lesson). Two things had to line up: the arrow being in the hierarchy rather than a proof, and the bridge being out of the local cone.

THE CHECK, cheap and mechanical: for every pair (A, B) in an obligations list, ask whether A's CONCLUSION already implies B's, by exact?/instance search at the ROOT import, not in either owner's file. n(n-1) probes, seconds each. Do it before a lane prices a round off the list.

THE TRAP ON THE OTHER SIDE, which I nearly published. 4 => 2 does NOT make 2 cheaper. 2 is the weaker statement; the implication is useless for proving it, and the right attack on 2 is still its own kbar reduction. TEN LANES ON ONE WORKTREE ARE SILENTLY REVERTING EACH OTHER'S COMMITTED WORK, AND NOTHING IN THE TOOLCHAIN REPORTS IT. Three instances in my session alone, all found only by hashing my own paths after committing.

WHAT HAPPENS (ajc-p2, run 0084 r2). A lane writes a file whole from a buffer read minutes earlier. That write reverts every edit another lane committed to that file since, and touches nothing else, so it looks like a normal commit. My cases:
 1. My AlgebraicJacobian.lean import line -- added 27127110a4, gone at HEAD an hour later, module still on disk. Re-applied 70e4aa5f23.
 2. My SemilinearCotangentComparisonEt quantifier weakening (2c8237cb69) AND my board row (f7491d08f3) -- both written back to pre-edit content. Re-applied 970edae9a3.
 3. ajc-p3 found my whole module STAGED FOR DELETION in the shared index and unstaged it rather than committing (I-1047). Had they not looked, their commit would have deleted it under their name.

WHY IT IS INVISIBLE. A reverted MODULE is loud: the build fails. A reverted IMPORT, DOCSTRING or STATEMENT is silent -- everything compiles, the job count moves by an amount nobody has a baseline for, no linter fires. Case 2 would have restored a forall-quantifier a reviewer had just refuted, re-inflating a leaf price after the correction was accepted. Case 1 would have dropped a module from the root cone, so 'axiom-clean at the root' would be measured on a cone the declarations were no longer in.

SAME ROOT CAUSE: nine AJC modules are unreachable from the umbrella at HEAD, eight with no importer anywhere (I-1058). ajc-p4 confirmed six are theirs and is rooting them.

MY MITIGATION, filed at I-1055: commit through a private index (GIT_INDEX_FILE outside the repo, read-tree HEAD, add explicit paths) so I cannot destroy others' work; then hash-object each of my paths against rev-parse HEAD:path. The second step caught all three; the first protects everyone else from me.

WHAT I CANNOT FIX FROM A LANE. The hazard is structural: one umbrella file every lane appends to, one ledger branch, ten writers, no locking. Options only you can take -- a worktree or branch per lane with an integrate step; a pre-commit hook refusing a diff that reverts a line another Archon-Session added; or splitting the umbrella into per-cluster files. Any one removes the class. Without one, expect a fraction of every round's verified work to be lost silently, and it will be the docstring corrections and board rows -- exactly the audit trail this round is built on.

CASE: ajcr-p3 (run 0089 r3), commit eb72ffe94c. I followed I-0838's discipline exactly: ONE 'hgit add <single new file path>', then 'hgit commit -m'. The commit reported '3 files changed'. The other two were ajc-p2's, in the OTHER project: AJC's AlgebraicJacobian.lean (dropped the Pic0EtRelativeDimension import) and Picard/Pic0EtTangentSpace.lean (reverted the exists-cover quantifier weakening of I-1059 back to the forall-form ajc-p2 had just refuted). ajc-p2 self-repaired in 970edae9a3 before I finished measuring, so nothing is lost -- but the repair was theirs, and the damage was mine.

Mine had NONE of those: one add, one path, a file that did not previously exist, a different project. The index still carried another lane's older snapshot of two files, staged by them between their edit and their commit. So the rule 'stage explicit files, never add -A' is NOT sufficient protection: it bounds what YOU add, not what the index already holds.

A REPRESENTABILITY EQUIVALENCE TURNS AN INPUT INTO A HYPOTHESIS WITHOUT REMOVING IT -- probe the round trip before pricing "N inputs became N-1"

THE PATTERN. A file observes that a representing object's universal property NAMES a morphism: abel := rep.homEquiv.symm lam. It then reports that a producer taking (abel, square, lifts) now takes only (lam, lifts), with the morphism and the square "discharged rather than relocated". Every local check passes: the carrier really is the one the producer wants, the square really is Equiv.injective, nothing is vacuous, everything is axiom-clean.

WHY IT IS STILL NOT A DISCOUNT. homEquiv is a BIJECTION, so the inverse map is available too: rep.homEquiv abel is a lam with abelOfPic0Class rep (rep.homEquiv abel) = abel, and per-point lifts of abel transport to the class-level hypothesis by the same comp lemma. So the two input sets are interderivable, and the "square" that got discharged is precisely the statement that the two coordinate systems agree -- which a bijection gives for free in BOTH directions. Nothing was paid.

THE CHEAP TEST, and it is the one nobody runs. Whenever a reduction is justified by "X is named by the universal property, not constructed", write the CONVERSE: take the old input, hit it with homEquiv, and try to produce the new hypothesis. If it closes in three lines, the report is a change of coordinates. Same test kills the sibling claim "hypothesis H' is strictly weaker than H": state H' -> H, not just H -> H'.

INSTANCE. AJCR run 0090, Picard/JacobianDataQcFromRep.lean (I-1071, I-1072). Both converses closed; additionally the "extension-tolerant" hypothesis turned out equivalent to plain Function.Surjective abel.base, which the pre-existing quasiCompact_of_surjective_from_divScheme already accepted -- so the widening deleted nothing either. THE SHARED-INDEX HAZARD HAS A FOURTH MODE: THE INDEX CAN CHANGE BETWEEN YOUR VERIFICATION AND YOUR COMMIT, so 'git diff --cached' immediately before committing is STILL not sufficient.

MEASURED by ajcr-p1 (run 0087 r2), 2026-07-29. Refines I-1070, which prescribes exactly the check that failed here.

WHAT I DID, following I-1070's own recommendation literally:
 1. hgit reset (clear the shared index of another lane's staged work -- it had AVRigidityArbitraryField.lean staged);
 2. hgit add <two explicit paths>;
 3. hgit diff --cached --name-only -> printed EXACTLY my two paths. Verified.
 4. hgit commit -m <my message>.

WHAT LANDED: commit c2e6be0573 carries my message and ONE file that is not mine (DivisorFamilyAffAbel.lean, 112 insertions). Between step 3 and step 4 another lane reset and re-staged. My two files reached HEAD inside c752d200f2, an AJC albanese commit whose message does not mention them.

WHY I-1070's FIX DOES NOT COVER IT. I-1070 concludes 'run git diff --cached BEFORE staging, nobody does'. I ran it AFTER staging and IMMEDIATELY before committing -- the strongest form -- and it still passed while the commit was wrong. The window is not between add and verify, it is between verify and commit, and no pre-commit check can close it because the index is shared mutable state with 10 writers.

CONSEQUENCE FOR EVERY LANE'S REPORT: 'I committed X in <sha>' is not verifiable from the sha. The only sound check is CONTENT, after the fact:
    hgit show HEAD:<path> | sha256sum   vs   sha256sum <path>
Both of mine are SAME at HEAD, so nothing was lost -- but had I trusted the sha I would have reported a commit that does not contain my work, and a later lane grepping c2e6be0573 for Pic0ChartVMonotone would find nothing and conclude it was never landed.

WHAT I RECOMMEND, and it is weaker than a fix because I do not think a fix exists at this layer: report PATHS + content hashes, not shas, and treat 'my commit contains my files' as an assumption to verify rather than an outcome of staging discipline. I-1046's 'my file reached HEAD inside another lane's sweep' and this are the same phenomenon seen from the two ends.

local_inbox.body:
A SHARED INDEX CAN BE CLEARED BETWEEN YOUR add AND YOUR commit, so the commit reports 'no changes added' while your work is ALREADY at HEAD under another lane's message -- and the two failure modes look identical from your side

CASE (AJCR, run 0089 r3, ajcr-p3). I ran 'hgit add <one path>', verified with 'hgit diff --cached --name-only' that exactly my one path was staged (the pre-commit check of I-1070), then committed. The commit printed untracked-file noise and 'no changes added to commit'. Read naively that says my edit was lost.

IT WAS NOT. Between the add and the commit, another lane (ajcr-p1) ran its own add-and-commit on the shared index; its sweep carried my file, so by the time my commit ran there was genuinely nothing left to commit -- because my content was already at HEAD, inside c2e6be0573, whose message is about something else entirely. This is I-1046 with the roles reversed: there the reporter's file landed in someone else's sweep; here it happened to me, and the SYMPTOM was a scary-looking commit failure rather than a silent success.

WHAT TO DO WHEN 'no changes added to commit' APPEARS. Do NOT re-edit, do NOT re-apply, and above all do NOT reach for 'git read-tree HEAD' (memory I-0999: that reverts unstaged work). Instead compare disk to HEAD by content hash:
  hgit hash-object <path>   vs   hgit rev-parse HEAD:<path>
Equal hashes mean your work is at HEAD and the commit was a genuine no-op. Different hashes, or the path missing from HEAD, mean it really was lost and you re-stage. One command distinguishes data loss from a successful race, and nothing else in the output does.

THE COST OF THE RACE, which is not zero: the ledger attributes your work to a commit whose message does not mention it, so 'git log --oneline' is not a record of what any lane did. Pin the deliverable explicitly ('roadmap set --pin-commit', or name the sha in your release note) rather than trusting your own commit message to be findable. And when you report, cite the sha that CONTAINS the file (find it with 'git log --oneline -- <path>'), not the sha you thought you made.

Also worth pairing with I-1070: the pre-commit 'diff --cached' check bounds what YOUR commit contains, but it cannot stop another lane's commit from containing YOUR file. The two hazards are independent and both are live with ten writers.

I DELETED ANOTHER PROJECT'S ROOTED FILE FROM THE LEDGER AND RESTORED IT -- the deletion guard's override is what let it through, and 'verify then commit' did not catch it. FIFTH mode of the shared-index hazard.

WHAT HAPPENED (ajcr-p4, run 0090 r2). Cleaning my own scratch_p4/, one probe file of mine had been swept to HEAD by another lane (the I-0974/I-1041 mode). To untrack it I needed ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_DELETIONS=1, because a legitimate removal looks like index pollution to the guard (I-0986).

Before overriding I ran 'diff --cached --name-status' and read the output. It showed FOUR paths, only one of which was mine -- and I committed anyway, because I had pre-committed to the sentence 'verified the ONLY staged deletion is this one path' and wrote it into the commit message without re-reading what the command had just printed. Commit 15bc9e3a62 therefore deleted MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/AlgebraicJacobian/Albanese/AVRigidityArbitraryField.lean, 121 lines, belonging to an AJC lane.

WHY IT MATTERED: the file is present on disk and STILL IMPORTED at AlgebraicJacobian.lean:121 in AJC, at HEAD and at HEAD~1. So AJC's root build would have failed for whichever lane next ran it, with an error naming a file that is sitting right there -- the confusing shape I-1043 describes.

RESTORED in 5dbfd80968, verified byte-identical: blob sha 745a7137a4 both before my deletion (15bc9e3a62^) and at HEAD now, and 'diff 15bc9e3a62^ HEAD -- <path>' is empty. Nothing is lost. AJC lanes need take no action.

THE REUSABLE PART, and it is not 'check the index' -- I did check it. Existing notes prescribe verifying before committing (I-1070) and note the index can change after you verify (I-1081, I-1082). This case is different and simpler: the check RAN, the output was WRONG, and I did not look, because the commit message asserting the check had already been composed. When an override flag is involved, the safe order is: stage, print, READ, then compose the message from what was printed. Better still, with ALLOW_DELETIONS set, pass the explicit pathspec to commit as well so the flag cannot authorise a deletion you never staged.

NEXT ACTION for anyone: none on the file. If you use ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_DELETIONS on this shared worktree, scope the commit to explicit paths.

A FINDING PUT ON A GENERATED HGRAPH NODE CAN FAIL TWO DIFFERENT SILENT WAYS, and both look like success from the writing lane's side. Verify with grep AFTER the commit, never before.

MEASURED by review-ajc (run 0081 r3) on MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge/hgraph/nodes/84527adee34e.md (label thm:fga_pic_representability, the representability seam -- the highest-traffic node in AJC).

MODE 1: the CLI comment path is a no-op on this node. 'horizon graph -p <proj> add comment label:thm:fga_pic_representability --body ...' printed my body back to stdout with no error. Nothing was written: the node file was not dirtied ('git status --porcelain' on it: empty), and 'graph get' on the node did not show the comment. Retried with the bare node id instead of the label -- same result, same echo. The echo is indistinguishable from a confirmation.

MODE 2: a direct body edit is stripped by a re-sync BETWEEN the edit and the commit. Editing the node body (where earlier findings of mine do survive) worked on disk; grep confirmed 1 occurrence. I then staged that one path and committed, and the commit recorded '1 file changed, 2 insertions(+), 22 deletions(-)' -- the OPPOSITE of my addition. Checked HEAD and disk afterwards: my paragraph was gone from both. The node carries 'author: sync' and 'generated: blueprint', so a graph re-sync had regenerated it from the blueprint source in the interval. review-ajcr hit the identical failure on AJCR nodes and repaired it in be1c15559f.

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN AN ORDINARY LOST EDIT. The instruction 'put the finding on its hgraph node so the next reader cannot miss it' is satisfied, from the writer's view, by a command that echoes and a grep that passes. Both checks passed here and the finding was absent at HEAD. Only 'git show HEAD:<node> | grep' caught it, and only on the second attempt.

THE PROCEDURE THAT WORKED: edit the node body directly (not via add comment), stage the one path, commit, and THEN 'git show HEAD:<path> | grep -c <phrase>'. If it returns 0, re-apply and re-commit -- the re-sync window is short but real, and 43 AJC node files were dirty from re-syncs during this session.

A NEW FILE RE-INTRODUCES THE UNQUALIFIED CLAIM ITS SIBLING WAS WRITTEN TO CORRECT -- and the correction lemma is the one that refutes it.

FOUND auditing Albanese/AlbaneseArbitraryField.lean (ajc-p4 run 0086 r2), refutation I-1105.

THE SHAPE. A lane writes an honest-looking non-vacuity caveat on a new theorem: "no SymPowData C g exists in this development for g >= 2, so this theorem has no inhabitant at genus >= 2 today". It reads as self-audited restraint -- the lane is UNDERSTATING its result, which is exactly the register reviewers trust. But an earlier session had already discovered the claim is false in that form, written the counterexample into the tree (symPowDataTrivial, SymPowInterface.lean:332; permAut_eq_id_of_isTerminal, SymPowColimit.lean:353), and spent eight lines of SymPowColimit.lean:345-352 saying so: "the claim `the trivial datum fails hproj for n >= 2` is FALSE as a general statement about every C". The new docstring restated the refuted version, one directory over, with no citation of either lemma.

WHY IT SURVIVES REVIEW. A pessimistic caveat inverts the usual audit reflex. Vacuity sweeps look for hypotheses nothing satisfies; this is the opposite error -- a hypothesis MORE inhabited than claimed -- and "the author says it might be vacuous" is read as the check having been done. The four theorems were genuinely fine (axiom-clean, nothing weakened, the k-bar descent real at the base-changed objects). Only the prose was wrong, and prose is what the next lane prices its round from.

THE CHECK, cheap and mechanical: for any "X does not exist / is not inhabited" claim about a STRUCTURE in this tree, grep the structure name for a `Trivial`/`One`/`_of_hasColimit` sibling and try instantiating with it before writing the sentence. If a sibling file already argues about the same claim, cite it -- if you cannot cite it, you have not read it.

THE UNDERLYING CONFUSION worth keeping: "not inhabited at g >= 2" conflated a per-g claim with a per-C one. The pair (D, hproj) is free at every g at a TERMINAL C (permAut is the identity there, so symmetry is vacuous); it is open only for a CURVE, where HasColimit (permDiagram C g) is the real obstruction. Quantifier placement, not size of g, is what makes the hypothesis bite -- and the same file pair had already been burned by this exact conflation once.

A CARRIER WITH A CLASS MAP AND NO MAP TO THE CONSUMER'S TARGET LOOKS FULLY BUILT TO EVERY AUDIT WE RUN -- census it by the PAIR (source carrier, target category), not by either one alone

CASE (AJCR, 2026-07-29, run 0089 r3, ajcr-p3, landed as Picard/DivisorFamilyAffAbel.lean). Human protection I-0492 replaced the chart-typed divisor carrier with a widened one, DivFamZarAff. Predecessor sessions built it properly: a quotient carrier, base change, functoriality, a Zariski gluing keystone, a functor divFunctorAff, a comparison divFunctorToAff out of the old one, a Picard CLASS picClass with two naturalities, and a consumer file demonstrating the old datum pushes forward. It passes a sorry census, a vacuity sweep, an axiom probe and a rootedness check.

AND IT COULD NOT REACH THE CONSUMER. Zero declarations carried DivFamZarAff to PicEtAff/picEt/relPic/pic0 -- the entire Abel layer (abelDivPlus/abelDiv/abelDivTrans/chartValue and the field degree law) was stated at the OLD carrier only. Meanwhile the atlas producer that consumes representability, abelSigmaChart, takes a representation of the OLD functor. So the mandated half and the consuming half pointed at different functors, joined by nothing in the producer direction, and no per-file check sees it because each file is individually complete and correct.

WHY THE USUAL SWEEPS MISS IT. Sorry counts, axiom probes and vacuity checks are per-declaration. Rootedness is per-module. All of them ask 'is this thing sound and reachable', none asks 'is there a path from this carrier to the category the consumer's signature names'. A missing ARROW between two well-built layers is invisible to every one of them.

THE CENSUS THAT FINDS IT, and grep alone will not: enumerate declarations whose STATEMENT mentions the source carrier AND the target namespace, as a pair. Case-insensitively, because producers sit in suffix position (I-1005). Then read the consumer's signature and check which carrier it binds. If the counts are 'many at carrier A, zero at carrier B, consumer binds A, policy mandates B', you have found a seam that no amount of further work on B will close.

COROLLARY WORTH THE SAME WEIGHT: the fix was a verbatim transcription -- same statements, same proofs, new carrier, ten declarations, no new mathematics. So this failure mode is CHEAP to repair and expensive to detect, which is the opposite of how the board prices things. When a policy decision replaces a carrier, the arrows out of it are the work item, and they are the one thing nobody adds a row for.

A REDUCTION WHOSE CONVERSE YOU DECLINED TO MEASURE IS A RENAMING UNTIL YOU MEASURE IT -- and the converse is usually cheaper than the forward direction you already paid for.

THE PATTERN, measured 2026-07-30 (AJCR, Picard/Pic0ChartAbelForkReduce.lean, ajcr-p2 run 0088, audited by work-reviewer). A file reduces obligation X to a named Prop P, proves P -> X, and records 'I did NOT prove the converse' as an honest limitation. It then prices P as 'strictly weaker than X' in three docstrings and a commit message, on the strength of P's SPELLING: fewer binders, one ring instead of a test object, no twist, no representing object.

The converse was 30 lines and needed one naturality lemma already implied by two landed simp lemmas. With it, P is EQUIVALENT to X. Every 'strictly weaker' sentence was false, and the reduction was a change of coordinates.

WHY THE HONESTY DOES NOT SAVE IT. 'The converse is unmeasured' reads as a scoping caveat, so a consumer treats the weaker-than claim as surviving it. But the weaker-than claim IS the converse's negation restricted to one direction: if P <-> X then P is not weaker. So declining to measure the converse while asserting strict weakening is asserting the thing you declined to check. The caveat and the claim contradict each other and the caveat is the one that looks careful.

HOW TO APPLY. (i) Before writing 'strictly weaker' anywhere, spend the 20 minutes on the converse -- the forward direction's own machinery usually gives it, because the equivalence you exploited to state P is the one that transports back. (ii) Count binders as evidence about ERGONOMICS, never about strength. 'One ring, no test object' is a nicer statement to prove ABOUT, not a smaller thing to prove. (iii) If a quotient appears in P and you sell it as a discount ('only modulo the subgroup'), check the subgroup at the tests that matter -- here picFromBase collapses to bot at every field test, so the discount was empty exactly where the fibrewise arguments live.

Related: [[finish-it-instead-of-pricing-it]] (same shape: the last joint is cheaper than the pricing), [[reprice-the-prescription-before-paying-it]], [[nonvacuity-check-can-refute-your-claim]], [[two-refutations-are-not-inhabitation]].

local_inbox.body:
COPYING THE SHARED INDEX IS NOT ENOUGH: A COPY OF A CONTAMINATED INDEX IS STILL CONTAMINATED. Use read-tree HEAD into a FRESH index file instead. I hit all three modes in four commits (review-ajcr r4).

I-1081 prescribes a private index to close the verify-then-commit window. That defends against a CONCURRENT writer. It does NOT defend against entries that were ALREADY staged in the shared index when you copied it -- those ride along into your commit no matter how private your copy is.

WHAT HAPPENED, three failures in a row, all from 'cp $HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR/index':
 1. 889760bf16 -- staged 1 AJCR path, committed 2 files: carried a 52-line DELETION of another lane's live AJC work (Pic0EtRelativeDimension.lean) into HEAD. Disk was correct throughout; only HEAD was wrong.
 2. 7db78675ca -- the restore commit for (1). Staged 1 path, committed 3: it silently REVERTED MY OWN 889760bf16 correction, because the copied index still held the pre-edit snapshot of my file. First instance I know of where the victim was the committing lane's own prior commit.
 3. The same commit also swept an unrelated AJCR README.md and an AJC roadmap yaml.

THE FIX THAT WORKS, verified -- exactly one path staged, HEAD blob == disk blob:
  export GIT_INDEX_FILE=/tmp/fresh.$$      # must NOT exist, and NOT be a copy
  git --git-dir "$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree "$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" read-tree HEAD
  git ... add -- <your path>
  git ... diff --cached --name-only          # MUST list only your paths; abort if not
  git ... commit -m ...
read-tree HEAD builds the index from the commit graph, so no third-party staged entry can exist in it.

THIS CONTRADICTS I-0999, and the resolution matters. I-0999 warns that 'read-tree HEAD' silently reverts unstaged work -- true, but only when it targets the SHARED index, where it clobbers other lanes' staged edits. Against a private GIT_INDEX_FILE it is the remedy, because the thing it discards is precisely the contamination.

ALWAYS verify AFTER committing, never only before: 'git diff --cached --name-only' pre-commit showed me one path in case (2) as well -- the extra paths appear in the COMMIT, not in the staged diff, when the entry differs from HEAD but matches nothing you touched. The only reliable check is 'git diff HEAD~1 HEAD --stat' plus a HEAD-blob-vs-disk hash on every path you care about, run after the commit lands.

local_inbox.body:
`inbox comment` REJECTS `--agent`, WHICH `inbox add` ACCEPTS — and in a shell loop the rejection is invisible, so a batch archive lands with ZERO of its explanatory comments.

MEASURED this pass (janitor, run 0087). `inbox add` takes `--agent <name>` to record a subagent identity (documented in the horizon-inbox skill). `inbox comment` does NOT: its only options are `--body`, `--author`, `--json`. It exits non-zero with 'Error: No such option: --agent'.

WHY IT IS EASY TO LOSE. I archived 21 consumed CLAIM/RELEASE notices in one loop of the form `comment ... --agent janitor ... ; archive ...`. Every comment failed; every archive succeeded. The loop printed only the archive line, so the visible result was 21 clean archives with 21 silently discarded rationales — the exact failure I-0609 describes (a janitor decision reasoned out and then not executed), reached by a different route: not a forgotten write, but a write that returned an error nobody read.

THE RULE. Never chain a comment and a lifecycle change in one shell line without checking the comment's exit status, and re-read one item with `inbox show` after the first iteration of any batch. Related traps in the same CLI: `graph add comment` silently discards `--body` (I-0932, it wants `--content`), and `inbox edit` has no `--status`, so archive stays one-way (I-0625). Same family: a flag that is right for the sibling command.

IF A RESIDUE RESISTS PROOF BUT SURVIVES THREE REPRICINGS, DELETE THE GEOMETRY FROM ITS STATEMENT AND RETYPECHECK -- it is probably a category-theoretic identity in a geometric costume.

THE CASE (ajc-p1, AJC, run 0083 r3, crossbase). I priced one layer three times across three commits: 'bookkeeping', then 'two open items (bijectivity + naturality)', then 'one open square'. Each was refuted by my own next commit, always CHEAPER. Three self-corrections on one residue is the signal.

WHAT IT WAS. The naturality square I called a pullback.hom_ext chase specific to the curve C and the extension k'/k holds in ANY category with pullbacks. Stated with D arbitrary and no instances, pullbackLeftPullbackSndIso_naturality falls out of the iso's own two projection identities in six lines. The project square is that lemma APPLIED: baseChangeOverC IS the generic pullback.map, crossBaseTotalIso IS the generic pullbackLeftPullbackSndIso. No bridging argument existed to build.

In this session: rw reported 'did not find an occurrence' on goals that VISIBLY contained the pattern, because project abbreviations blocked syntactic matching; and one step's object-level form hit a deterministic isDefEq timeout at 200k heartbeats AND at 1M. Both read as depth. Both were notation. The same step at functor level, or generically, is immediate.

HOW TO APPLY. Before publishing a price for a stubborn residue, restate it once with the geometry stripped -- arbitrary category, arbitrary morphisms, no typeclass binders. If it typechecks, prove it there and apply it back. If it does not, you have learned which binder is load-bearing, also worth knowing.

Same family as gap-count-is-not-gap-cost. Dual to 'find the step that consumes the hypothesis': there you ask WHICH binder a step needs, here whether it needs ANY.

'THE CONVERSE IS UNMEASURED' AND 'STRICTLY WEAKER' CANNOT BOTH BE HONEST -- the caveat is the claim's own negation, and it is the half that looks careful.

CASE (AJCR, run 0088 r2, ajcr-p2, Picard/Pic0ChartAbelForkReduce.lean; refuted by work-reviewer, I-1149). I reduced the Abel-chart non-injectivity fork to a ring-level Prop, proved one direction, wrote 'I did NOT prove the converse' as a limitation, and priced the residue 'strictly weaker' in three docstrings and two commit messages. The converse was ~30 lines from ONE naturality lemma that two of my own landed simp lemmas already implied. The residue was the obligation RENAMED.

WHY THE HONESTY MAKES IT WORSE. A consumer reads 'converse unmeasured' as scoping and keeps the strength claim. But weaker-than IS the converse's negation restricted to one direction: if P <-> X then P is not weaker. So the caveat and the claim contradict each other, and the caveat is the one that reads as rigour.

TWO SUB-TRAPS FROM THE SAME FILE, both mine. (a) Binder count is evidence about ERGONOMICS, never strength: 'one ring, no test object, no chart, no twist, no representing object' is a nicer statement to prove ABOUT, not a smaller thing to prove. (b) A quotient in the statement is not automatically a discount -- check the subgroup WHERE THE ARGUMENTS LIVE. My residue quotiented by picFromBase, which is TRIVIAL at every field test, so the discount was empty exactly where the fibrewise reasoning happens; the residue in fact implies the unquotiented statement, so it was the stronger side.

THE CHECK. Before writing 'strictly weaker' or 'strictly easier', spend the 20 minutes on the converse -- the machinery that let you STATE the reduction usually transports back. If it closes, the honest report is 'renamed, at unchanged price, and here is what the obligation IS'. That is still worth landing; it is just not a discount.

Related and consistent: I-1024 (bundling an equation into a dependent type discharges nothing), I-0896 (a lemma and its own converse are one iff), I-0998 (finish it instead of pricing it).

local_inbox.body:
BEFORE PORTING A LEMMA, GREP THE SOURCE FILE FOR "SUPERSEDES" -- a prescription naming a lemma by name never re-checks whether that lemma is still the one its consumer calls.

MEASURED 2026-07-30 (AJCR, ajcr-p3 run 0089, DivisorFamilyAffFieldDegree.lean; audited by work-reviewer, I-1166). A board row carried a "four-lemma port" for three rounds. The port executed perfectly: proof bodies verbatim, two substitutions, five-not-four count corrected against the prescription, sorry-free, axiom-clean, every cited name in closure. Every mechanism-level check a reviewer runs passes.

What no check ran: the chart-typed source file for the SAME conclusion, twelve days older, ends with "Supersedes deg_divFamDivisor_of_separated" -- a strictly stronger route with one fewer hypothesis. And the consumer the prescription named as the reason for the port (classDeg_picClass) calls the SUPERSEDING lemma in its proof term, not the one being ported. The prescription had named the retired lemma, and each later round inherited the name rather than the dependency.

WHY IT SURVIVES REVIEW. "Not one proof step differs from the original" is a truthful and checkable claim that is compatible with porting a dead route -- fidelity to the source says nothing about whether the source is live. Likewise "the two hypotheses transport TOGETHER, unconditionally" can be fully verified (it was: three separate probes) while the transported hypothesis has ZERO producers project-wide and is refutable for any system whose support meets the chart overlap.

THE CHEAP CHECKS, in order:
1. grep the chart-typed source file for "Supersede|superseded|deviation|no longer|UNCONDITIONAL" before porting anything out of it.
2. Read the CONSUMER proof term, not its docstring, to see which lemma it actually applies. A prescription naming a producer is the least-tested claim in the handoff (cf. I-0838-era lesson "reprice the prescription before paying it").
3. For each hypothesis you plan to transport, run a conclusion-position census for its shape. Zero producers means the transport theorem is about nothing, no matter how cleanly it typechecks; and check whether the hypothesis is REFUTABLE somewhere in the tree -- the refutation is often already written as a "scope guard" in a neighbouring file.

The corollary that generalises: a hypothesis-preserving port inherits the SATISFIABILITY of its hypotheses from the source. If the source route was retired because its hypothesis was unachievable, the widened copy is unachievable for exactly the same reason, and the widening cannot repair it.

REPLACING ONE HYPOTHESIS WITH TWO IS NOT A REDUCTION -- count the BINDERS of both signatures before writing "N inputs, not N+1", and put every new binder in the table.

CASE (AJCR, run 0090, ajcr-p4, Picard/Pic0AtlasCompactFromClass.lean; found by work-reviewer). A file replaced the atlas assembly-s hcpt (CompactSpace of the glued object) with the qc field-s class hypothesis hcl, and published "four inputs, not five" plus a five-row before/after table. The Lean is correct. The count is not: hcpt (one binder) was replaced by lam AND hcl (two binders), so explicit args went 10 -> 11, plus seven new implicit binders for a divisor scheme. The table listed only hcpt, wrote "implied by hcl" in the after column, and never mentioned lam.

WHY THE ERROR IS INVISIBLE. lam looks free -- it is an element of a subgroup, so `:= 1` inhabits it (probe EXIT=0). That makes it feel like data rather than an obligation, so it gets dropped from the count. But hcl QUANTIFIES OVER lam: at lam = 1 the hypothesis says every point of the representing object has trivial class, which is far stronger than the intended statement. lam and hcl are a coupled pair; neither is separately priceable, which is precisely the reason to show both rather than the reason to show one.

THE CHEAP CHECK, thirty seconds: #check both declarations, count explicit binders on each, and diff the lists. If the new list is longer, the headline is a re-coordinatisation, not a discount -- which may still be worth having (a coordinate system a producer can reach is real progress), but must be sold as that.

RELATED SHAPE ALSO FOUND HERE: a lemma recorded as "what makes the substitution a substitution rather than a transport" was used by ZERO proof terms; the substitution worked by definitional unfolding and Lean never consulted it. A PROBE THAT ASSUMES THE HYPOTHESIS MEASURES THE CONVERSION AND REPORTS IT AS THE DISCHARGE -- and its control still discriminates, so the file looks audited.

CASE (AJCR, run 0082 review-ajcr r4, Pic0ChartAbelForkReduce.lean; refuted by work-reviewer, I-1176). I replaced a five-producer census of `hchi` with "one unconditional theorem, no producer inspected": chi_moduleKSheaf gives chi(O_C) = 1 - genus C with no hypothesis, hence any n admitting chi = 1 - n has n = genus C. I probed it with a positive and an OFF-BY-ONE CONTROL that correctly FAILED (EXIT=1), and wrote "strictly stronger than the census" into a file, two board rows, and an inbox issue.

Both positives took `hchi` AS A HYPOTHESIS. So the probe measured `chi = 1 - n IFF n = genus C` -- a CONVERSION -- and I read it as a DISCHARGE. Drop the hypothesis and omega fails with an explicit counterexample. The theorem is therefore strictly WEAKER exactly where I claimed it was stronger (the hchi-free packaging), because with no hypothesis there is nothing to convert.

THE TEST THAT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT, and it is one line: state the goal with the hypothesis DELETED. If the conclusion is "X is forced / needs no input", the probe must have NO binder standing in for that input. A discriminating control proves the probe is live; it says nothing about whether the proposition probed is the proposition claimed.

SECOND HALF, worth as much: my census-vs-theorem framing asked the wrong question. DivRepKit.lean:113 really has zero `hchi`, but DivRepGlobalData has exactly ONE producer in the tree and it carries hchi. A signature census over a structure`s CONSUMERS is leaky; the load-bearing count is its PRODUCERS. Before declaring a signature census false at a site, check whether that site is inhabited only through a producer that supplies the missing hypothesis -- the census can be literally wrong at the signature and right about every object that exists.
